sentences.zh: 韓文，字貫道，洪洞人，宋宰相琦後也。

translations.literal: Han Wen, style name Guandao, was a native of Hongdong and a descendant of the Song chief minister Han Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wen, whose style was Guandao, came from Hongdong and was descended from the Song chief minister Han Qi.

sentences.zh: 生時，父夢紫衣人抱送文彥博至其家，故名之曰文。

translations.literal: At his birth his father dreamed that a man in purple robes carried Wen Yanbo to his house, and so named him Wen.
translations.idiomatic: When he was born, his father dreamed that a man in purple robes brought Wen Yanbo to the house, and for that reason named him Wen.

sentences.zh: 成化二年舉進士，除工科給事中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chenghua he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chenghua and was appointed a supervising secretary in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 核韋州軍功，劾寧晉伯劉聚，都御史王越、馬文升等濫殺妄報。

translations.literal: When he audited military merit at Weizhou, he impeached the Marquis of Ningjin, Liu Ju, and the censors-in-chief Wang Yue and Ma Wensheng and others for indiscriminate killing and false reports.
translations.idiomatic: While auditing military merit at Weizhou, he impeached the Marquis of Ningjin Liu Ju and the censors-in-chief Wang Yue and Ma Wensheng, among others, for indiscriminate killing and false reporting of victories.

sentences.zh: 尋劾越薦李秉、王竑。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he impeached Yue for recommending Li Bing and Wang Hong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Wang Yue as well for recommending Li Bing and Wang Hong.

sentences.zh: 語頗涉兩宮，帝怒，撻之文華殿庭。

translations.literal: His words touched on both palaces, the emperor was angry, and he was flogged in the courtyard of the Hall of Literary Glory.
translations.idiomatic: His language touched on matters involving both palaces; the emperor was furious and had him flogged in the courtyard of the Hall of Literary Glory.

sentences.zh: 已，進右給事中，出為湖廣右參議。

translations.literal: Thereafter he was promoted to right supervising secretary and sent out as right assistant administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was promoted to right supervising secretary and appointed right assistant administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 中貴督太和山，乾沒公費。

translations.literal: A favored eunuch supervised Mount Taihe and embezzled public funds.
translations.idiomatic: A favored eunuch was supervising Mount Taihe and embezzling public funds.

sentences.zh: 文力遏之，以其羨易粟萬石，備振貸。

translations.literal: Wen forcefully checked him, exchanged the surplus for ten thousand piculs of grain, and set it aside for famine relief loans.
translations.idiomatic: Wen firmly restrained him, converted the surplus funds into ten thousand piculs of grain, and stored it for famine relief and lending.

sentences.zh: 九溪土酋與鄰境爭地相攻，文往諭，皆服。

translations.literal: The native chieftains of Jiuxi fought with neighboring districts over land; Wen went to instruct them, and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Native chieftains of Jiuxi were fighting neighboring districts over land; Wen went to admonish them, and all submitted.

sentences.zh: 閱七年，轉左。

translations.literal: After seven years he was transferred to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years later he was transferred to the left post.

sentences.zh: 弘治改元，王恕以文久淹，用為山東左參政。

translations.literal: When Hongzhi changed the reign title, Wang Shu, because Wen had long been held back, employed him as left administration commissioner of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Hongzhi reign, Wang Shu, seeing that Wen had long been kept in subordinate posts, appointed him left administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 居二年，用倪嶽薦，擢雲南左布政使。

translations.literal: After two years, on Ni Yue's recommendation, he was promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later, on Ni Yue's recommendation, he was promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫湖廣，移撫河南，召為戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: As right vice censor-in-chief he pacified Huguang, was transferred to pacify Henan, and was summoned as right vice minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: As right vice censor-in-chief he served as grand coordinator of Huguang, then was transferred to Henan and summoned to be right vice minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 母喪除，起改吏部，進左。

translations.literal: When mourning for his mother ended, he was recalled, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and advanced to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period for his mother, he was recalled, transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and promoted to the left post.

sentences.zh: 十六年拜南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was appointed minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 歲侵，米價翔踴。

translations.literal: The year suffered crop failure, and rice prices soared.
translations.idiomatic: That year crops failed and rice prices soared.

sentences.zh: 文請預發軍餉三月，戶部難之。

translations.literal: Wen requested advance payment of three months' military stipends; the Ministry of Revenue found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Wen asked to issue three months of military pay in advance, but the Ministry of Revenue resisted.

sentences.zh: 文曰：「救荒如救焚，有罪，吾自當之。」

translations.literal: Wen said, "Relieving famine is like putting out a fire; if there is guilt, I myself will bear it."
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "Famine relief is like fighting a fire—if anyone is to be blamed, let it be me."

sentences.zh: 乃發廩十六萬石，米價為平。

translations.literal: Thereupon he released one hundred sixty thousand piculs from the granaries, and rice prices stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: He then released one hundred sixty thousand piculs from the granaries, and rice prices stabilized.

sentences.zh: 明年召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned and appointed minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 文凝厚雍粹，居常抑抑。

translations.literal: Wen was grave, generous, and pure; in daily life he was restrained and deferential.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was grave, generous, and upright; in ordinary life he was modest and unassuming.

sentences.zh: 至臨大事，剛斷無所撓。

translations.literal: When facing great affairs, he was firm and decisive and yielded to nothing.
translations.idiomatic: But when great affairs were at stake, he was resolute and unyielding.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，賞賚及山陵、大婚諸費，需銀百八十萬兩有奇，部帑不給。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, rewards and the expenses of the imperial tomb and grand wedding required more than 1.8 million taels of silver, and the ministry treasury could not supply them.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong came to the throne, rewards and the costs of the imperial tomb and grand wedding required more than 1.8 million taels of silver, and the ministry treasury could not cover it.

sentences.zh: 文請先發承運庫，詔不許。

translations.literal: Wen requested first drawing on the transport treasury; an edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wen asked to draw first on the transport treasury, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 文言：「帑藏虛，賞賚自京邊軍士外，請分別給銀鈔，稍益以內庫及內府錢，並暫借勛戚賜莊田稅，而敕承運庫內官核所積金銀，著之籍。

translations.literal: Wen said, "The treasury is empty. Apart from soldiers in the capital and on the frontier, please give rewards separately in silver notes, supplement somewhat with funds from the inner treasury and inner palace, and temporarily borrow the tax on estates granted to meritorious kin; also order the eunuchs of the transport treasury to verify accumulated gold and silver and record it in the registers.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The treasury is empty. Apart from soldiers in the capital and on the frontiers, let rewards be paid partly in paper money, supplemented somewhat from the inner treasury and inner palace funds, with a temporary loan from taxes on estates granted to meritorious kin; and order the eunuchs of the transport treasury to audit the gold and silver on hand and enter it in the registers.

sentences.zh: 且盡罷諸不急費。」

translations.literal: Moreover, abolish entirely all non-urgent expenditures."
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, abolish all nonessential expenditures."

sentences.zh: 帝不欲發內帑，命文以漸經畫。

translations.literal: The emperor did not wish to open the inner treasury and ordered Wen to plan the matter gradually.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not wish to open the inner treasury and told Wen to work out the finances step by step.

sentences.zh: 文持大體，務為國惜財。

translations.literal: Wen upheld the larger principles and strove to save state wealth for the country.
translations.idiomatic: Wen held to the larger interest and strove to conserve the state's wealth.

sentences.zh: 真人陳應衤盾、大國師那卜堅參等落職，文請沒其資實國帑。

translations.literal: The True Man Chen Yingxiang, the Great State Preceptor Napo Jianzan, and others were dismissed from office; Wen requested that their assets be confiscated for the state treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When the Daoist adept Chen Yingxiang, the Great State Preceptor Napo Jianzan, and others were dismissed, Wen asked that their property be seized for the state treasury.

sentences.zh: 舊制，監局、倉庫內官不過二三人，後漸添註，或一倉十余人，上林苑、林衡署至三十二人，文力請裁汰。

translations.literal: By old regulation, inner eunuchs at supervisory bureaus and storehouses were no more than two or three; later posts were gradually added, until one storehouse might have more than ten men and the Imperial Park and Forestry Office as many as thirty-two; Wen strongly requested reductions.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old rules, inner eunuchs at supervisory bureaus and storehouses numbered no more than two or three; later appointments multiplied until a single storehouse might have more than ten and the Imperial Park and Forestry Office as many as thirty-two. Wen pressed hard for cutbacks.

sentences.zh: 淳安公主賜田三百頃，復欲奪任丘民業，文力爭乃止。

translations.literal: Princess Chun'an was granted three hundred qing of fields and again wished to seize the livelihoods of the people of Renqiu; Wen struggled hard against it and only then was it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Chun'an had been granted three hundred qing of land and then sought to seize the holdings of commoners in Renqiu; Wen fought the proposal fiercely until it was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時，外戚慶雲、壽寧侯家人及商人譚景清等奏請買補殘鹽至百八十萬引。

translations.literal: In Xiaozong's time, the families of the maternal relatives, the Marquises of Qingyun and Shouning, and the merchant Tan Jingqing and others memorialized to purchase supplemental remnant salt up to 1.8 million yin.
translations.idiomatic: Under Xiaozong, the households of the maternal relatives—the Marquises of Qingyun and Shouning—and the merchant Tan Jingqing and others petitioned to buy supplemental remnant salt licenses totaling 1.8 million yin.

sentences.zh: 文條鹽政夙弊七事，論殘鹽尤切。

translations.literal: Wen listed seven long-standing abuses of the salt administration, speaking especially sharply on remnant salt.
translations.idiomatic: Wen listed seven longstanding abuses in the salt administration, arguing most forcefully against remnant salt.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘉納，未及行而崩，即入武宗登極詔中，罷之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong approved and accepted it, but before it could be carried out he died; it entered Wuzong's accession edict and was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong approved the proposal, but before it could be implemented he died; the measure was then included in Wuzong's accession edict and abolished.

sentences.zh: 侯家復奏乞，下部更議，文等再三執奏，弗從，竟如侯請。

translations.literal: The marquis's household memorialized again to beg it; the ministry was ordered to reconsider; Wen and others repeatedly submitted firm memorials and were not followed; in the end it was as the marquis requested.
translations.idiomatic: The marquis's family petitioned again; the ministry was ordered to reconsider; Wen and others submitted repeated firm memorials in vain, and in the end the court granted the marquis's request.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，內閣及言官復論之，詔下廷議。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, the Grand Secretariat and remonstrance officials debated it again, and an edict ordered court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde the Grand Secretariat and censorial officials debated the matter again, and the emperor ordered a court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 文言：「鹽法之設，專以備邊。

translations.literal: Wen said, "The salt laws were established solely to supply the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Wen said, "The salt monopoly was established solely to fund the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今山、陜饑，寇方大入，度支匱絀，飛挽甚難。

translations.literal: Now Shanxi and Shaanxi suffer famine, bandits are making major incursions, revenue is exhausted, and rapid transport is very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Shanxi and Shaanxi are in famine, raiders are pouring in, revenue is exhausted, and rapid transport of supplies is extremely difficult.

sentences.zh: 奈何壞祖宗法，忽邊防之重。」

translations.literal: How can we destroy the laws of the ancestors and neglect the weight of frontier defense?"
translations.idiomatic: How can we overturn the laws of our ancestors and neglect frontier defense?"

sentences.zh: 景清復陳乞如故。

translations.literal: Jingqing again submitted the old petition.
translations.idiomatic: Jingqing submitted the same petition again.

sentences.zh: 文等劾其桀悍，請執付法官。

translations.literal: Wen and others impeached him for arrogance and violence and requested that he be arrested and handed to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and others impeached him for defiance and asked that he be arrested and handed over to the judiciary.

sentences.zh: 帝不得已，始寢前令。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice and only then set aside the earlier order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having no alternative, finally set aside the earlier order.

sentences.zh: 榮王乞霸州莊田，崇王請自征莊田租，勿令有司與，文皆持卻之。

translations.literal: Prince Rong begged for estate fields in Bazhou; Prince Chong asked to levy estate rents himself and not let the regular officials participate; Wen in each case held firm and refused.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong petitioned for estate land in Bazhou; Prince Chong asked to collect estate rents himself without local officials taking part—Wen blocked each request.

sentences.zh: 保定巡撫王璟請革皇莊，廷議從之，帝命再議。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, grand coordinator of Baoding, requested abolishing imperial estates; court deliberation agreed; the emperor ordered further discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing, grand coordinator of Baoding, asked to abolish imperial estates; the court agreed, but the emperor ordered the matter reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 文請命巡撫官召民佃，畝征銀三分輸內庫，而盡撤中官管莊者，大學士劉健等亦力言內臣管莊擾民。

translations.literal: Wen requested that grand coordinators summon commoners to tenant the land, levy three fen of silver per mu for the inner treasury, and entirely withdraw the inner eunuchs who managed the estates; Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others also strongly said that inner officials managing estates disturbed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Wen proposed that grand coordinators lease the land to commoners, collect three fen of silver per mu for the inner treasury, and remove all inner eunuchs who managed the estates; Grand Secretaries Liu Jian and others also argued forcefully that eunuch estate managers harassed the people.

sentences.zh: 乃命留中官各一人、校尉十人，余如文議。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was ordered to retain one inner eunuch each and ten guardsmen, with the rest as Wen proposed.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered that one inner eunuch and ten guardsmen remain at each estate, with the rest of Wen's plan adopted.

sentences.zh: 中旨索寶石、西珠，文請屏絕珍奇，以養儉德。

translations.literal: By secret edict gems and Western pearls were demanded; Wen requested shutting out curiosities to cultivate frugal virtue.
translations.idiomatic: By secret edict the court demanded gems and Western pearls; Wen asked that such luxuries be refused so as to cultivate frugality.

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: The reply was approval.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 帝將大婚，取戶部銀四十萬兩，文連疏請，得免四之一。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to marry; four hundred thousand taels of silver were taken from the Ministry of Revenue; Wen submitted repeated memorials and secured exemption of one quarter.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was about to marry, four hundred thousand taels were taken from the Ministry of Revenue; Wen submitted repeated memorials and secured a reduction of one quarter.

sentences.zh: 文司國計二年，力遏權幸，權幸深疾之。

translations.literal: Wen directed state finances for two years, forcefully curbing the powerful and favored, who deeply hated him.
translations.idiomatic: For two years Wen directed state finances, firmly checking the powerful and favored, who came to hate him deeply.

sentences.zh: 而是時青宮舊奄劉瑾等八人號「八虎」，日導帝狗馬、鷹兔、歌舞、角觝，不親萬幾。

translations.literal: But at this time the eight former Eastern Palace eunuchs Liu Jin and others were called the Eight Tigers; day by day they led the emperor to dogs and horses, hawks and hares, song and dance, and wrestling, and he did not attend to the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the eight former Eastern Palace eunuchs led by Liu Jin were known as the "Eight Tigers"; day after day they led the emperor to hunting, hawking, music, dance, and wrestling matches, and he neglected the affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 文每退朝，對僚屬語及，輒泣下。

translations.literal: Whenever Wen left court and spoke of it to his colleagues, he would weep.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Wen left court and spoke of this with his colleagues, he wept.

sentences.zh: 郎中李夢陽進曰：「公大臣，義共國休戚，徒泣何為。

translations.literal: Bureau director Li Mengyang advanced and said, "You are a great minister; in duty you share the state's weal and woe—what use is weeping alone?
translations.idiomatic: Bureau director Li Mengyang stepped forward and said, "You are a chief minister and share the state's fortune—what good is weeping alone?

sentences.zh: 諫官疏劾諸奄，執政持甚力。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials have memorialized in impeachment of the eunuchs, and the chief ministers hold very firm.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials have already memorialized against the eunuchs, and the chief ministers are standing firm.

sentences.zh: 公誠及此時率大臣固爭，去『八虎』易易耳。」

translations.literal: If you truly at this time lead the great ministers in firm contention, removing the Eight Tigers would be very easy."
translations.idiomatic: If you would now lead the chief ministers in a united stand, removing the Eight Tigers would be easy."

sentences.zh: 文捋須昂肩，毅然改容曰：「善。

translations.literal: Wen stroked his beard, raised his shoulders, changed his expression resolutely, and said, "Good.
translations.idiomatic: Wen stroked his beard, straightened his shoulders, and said resolutely, "Well said.

sentences.zh: 縱事勿濟，吾年足死矣，不死不足報國。」

translations.literal: Even if the affair does not succeed, my years are enough to die; not to die would be insufficient to repay the state."
translations.idiomatic: Even if we fail, I am old enough to die; if I do not die, I cannot repay the state."

sentences.zh: 即偕諸大臣伏闕上疏，略曰：「人主辨奸為明，人臣犯顏為忠。

translations.literal: Thereupon, together with the great ministers, he prostrated himself before the palace gate and submitted a memorial, in summary saying, "For a ruler to distinguish treachery is wisdom; for a minister to offend the countenance is loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the chief ministers in kneeling before the palace gate to submit a memorial that began, "For a ruler to discern treachery is wisdom; for a minister to speak against the throne is loyalty.

sentences.zh: 況群小作朋，逼近君側，安危治亂胥此焉關。

translations.literal: Moreover, when petty men form factions and draw near the ruler's side, security and danger, order and chaos all hinge on this.
translations.idiomatic: When petty men form factions at the ruler's side, the security of the realm and the fate of good government all hang on this.

sentences.zh: 臣等伏睹近歲朝政日非，號令失當。

translations.literal: Your ministers have bowed and observed that in recent years court governance grows daily worse and orders are ill-timed.
translations.idiomatic: We have observed that in recent years governance has grown daily worse and imperial orders have gone awry.

sentences.zh: 自入秋來，視朝漸晚。

translations.literal: Since autumn began, audiences have grown gradually later.
translations.idiomatic: Since autumn, the emperor has been holding court later and later.

sentences.zh: 仰窺聖容，日漸清削。

translations.literal: Looking up to glimpse the sacred countenance, it grows daily more thin.
translations.idiomatic: When we glimpse your countenance, we see that you grow thinner day by day.

sentences.zh: 皆言太監馬永成、谷大用、張永、羅祥、魏彬、丘聚、劉瑾、高鳳等造作巧偽，淫蕩上心。

translations.literal: All say that the eunuchs Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Zhang Yong, Luo Xiang, Wei Bin, Qiu Ju, Liu Jin, Gao Feng, and others contrive artifice and falsehood and debauch the imperial mind.
translations.idiomatic: All agree that the eunuchs Ma Yongcheng, Gu Dayong, Zhang Yong, Luo Xiang, Wei Bin, Qiu Ju, Liu Jin, Gao Feng, and others contrive deceptions and corrupt your mind with dissipation.

sentences.zh: 擊球走馬，放鷹逐犬，俳優雜劇，錯陳於前。

translations.literal: They strike balls and race horses, fly hawks and chase dogs, actors and mixed plays are set out in confusion before him.
translations.idiomatic: They set before you ball games and horse racing, hawking and hound coursing, actors and variety plays in endless profusion.

sentences.zh: 至導萬乘與外人交易，狎昵媟褻，無復禮體。

translations.literal: They even lead the imperial carriage to trade with outsiders, intimate and lewd without remaining ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: They even lead you to trade with outsiders in familiar and indecent ways, with no regard for ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 日遊不足，夜以繼之，勞耗精神，虧損誌德。

translations.literal: Daytime amusements are not enough; night continues them, exhausting the spirit and impairing resolve and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Daytime diversions are not enough—they continue into the night, wearing down your spirit and harming your virtue.

sentences.zh: 遂使天道失序，地氣靡寧。

translations.literal: Thus the way of Heaven loses order and the qi of earth knows no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's order has been disturbed and the earth is unsettled.

sentences.zh: 雷異星變，桃李秋華。

translations.literal: Thunder is abnormal, stars change, peach and plum blossom in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder has been abnormal, stars have shifted, and peach and plum trees have blossomed in autumn.

sentences.zh: 考厥占候，鹹非吉征。

translations.literal: Examining these prognostications, all are inauspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: By every omen, none of these are auspicious signs.

sentences.zh: 此輩細人，惟知蠱惑君上以便己私，而不思赫赫天命。

translations.literal: These petty men know only to bewitch and delude the ruler for their private advantage and do not think of the august mandate of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: These petty men know only how to beguile you for their private gain and give no thought to Heaven's august mandate.

sentences.zh: 皇皇帝業，在陛下一身。

translations.literal: The august imperial enterprise rests on Your Majesty's person alone.
translations.idiomatic: The august imperial enterprise rests on Your Majesty alone.

sentences.zh: 今大婚雖畢，儲嗣未建。

translations.literal: Now though the grand wedding is finished, the heir is not yet established.
translations.idiomatic: Though the grand wedding is over, no heir has yet been appointed.

sentences.zh: 萬一遊宴損神，起居失節，雖齏粉若輩，何補於事。

translations.literal: If by chance feasting and roaming harm the spirit and daily conduct loses measure, though these men be ground to powder, what good would it do?
translations.idiomatic: If dissipation should harm your health or irregular habits should take hold, grinding these men to dust would avail nothing.

sentences.zh: 高皇帝艱難百戰，取有四海。

translations.literal: The August Emperor fought through a hundred hardships in battle and took possession of all within the four seas.
translations.idiomatic: The August Emperor fought through countless hardships and won the realm.

sentences.zh: 列聖繼承，以至陛下。

translations.literal: The successive sage emperors inherited in turn down to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The sage emperors succeeded one another down to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 先帝臨崩顧命之語，陛下所聞也。

translations.literal: The former emperor's words of testament on his deathbed—Your Majesty heard them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty heard the former emperor's deathbed charge.

sentences.zh: 奈何姑息群小，置之左右，以累聖德？

translations.literal: How can you indulge petty men and place them at your side, thereby burdening sagely virtue?
translations.idiomatic: How can you indulge petty men and keep them at your side, thereby tarnishing your sacred virtue?

sentences.zh: 竊觀前古奄宦誤國，為禍尤烈，漢十常侍、唐甘露之變，其明驗也。

translations.literal: We privately observe that in former ages eunuchs and palace attendants misled states and wrought especially fierce harm—the Han Ten Regular Attendants and the Tang Sweet Dew incident are clear proofs.
translations.idiomatic: History shows that eunuchs have misled states to especially terrible ends—the Ten Regular Attendants of Han and the Sweet Dew incident of Tang are clear proof.

sentences.zh: 今永成等罪惡既著，若縱不治，將來益無忌憚，必患在社稷。

translations.literal: Now Yongcheng and the others' crimes are already manifest; if they are indulged and not punished, hereafter they will be increasingly without fear and disaster is certain for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Yongcheng and the others have already shown their crimes; if they are indulged, they will grow ever bolder and the altars of state will be in peril.

sentences.zh: 伏望陛下奮乾剛，割私愛，上告兩宮，下諭百僚，明正典刑，以回天地之變，泄神人之憤，潛削禍亂之階，永保靈長之業。」

translations.literal: We bow and hope Your Majesty will rouse the firmness of Qian, cut off private affection, report above to both palaces, instruct below the hundred officials, clearly apply the canonical punishments, thereby turn back the changes of Heaven and earth, release the anger of spirits and men, secretly cut away the steps to calamity and rebellion, and forever preserve the enduring enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: We beg Your Majesty to rouse your firm resolve, set aside private affection, inform both palaces, instruct all officials, and apply the proper punishments—thereby turning back Heaven's warnings, appeasing the anger of gods and men, removing the seeds of rebellion, and securing the dynasty for ages to come."

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝驚泣不食。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was startled, wept, and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was received, the emperor was shaken, wept, and refused to eat.

sentences.zh: 瑾等大懼。

translations.literal: Jin and the others were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and the others were terrified.

sentences.zh: 時內閣劉健、謝遷等方持言官章不肯下，文疏復入。

translations.literal: At this time Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and others of the Grand Secretariat were holding the censorial memorials and refusing to release them; Wen's memorial again entered.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Jian, Xie Qian, and others in the Grand Secretariat were holding the censors' memorials and refusing to transmit them; Wen's memorial arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 帝遣司禮太監李榮、王嶽等詣閣議。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the Directorate of Ceremonial eunuchs Li Rong, Wang Yue, and others to the Grand Secretariat to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuchs Li Rong and Wang Yue of the Directorate of Ceremonial to the Grand Secretariat for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 一日三至，健等持益堅。

translations.literal: Three times in one day they came; Jian and the others held firmer still.
translations.idiomatic: They came three times in a single day, but Jian and the others held firmer than ever.

sentences.zh: 嶽素剛直，獨曰：「閣議是。」

translations.literal: Yue was by nature upright and alone said, "The Grand Secretariat's deliberation is correct."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yue, who was upright by nature, alone said, "The Grand Secretariat is right."

sentences.zh: 是夜，八人者環泣帝前。

translations.literal: That night, the eight men surrounded [him] and wept before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: That night, the eight eunuchs gathered around the emperor and wept before him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，立收嶽下詔獄，而外廷固未之知也。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and immediately had Yue taken down and imprisoned in the imperial prison; the outer court, however, did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had Wang Yue seized and thrown into the imperial prison at once, though the outer court knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 明日，文倡九卿科道再詣闕固爭。

translations.literal: The next day, Wen led the Nine Ministers and the censorate and remonstrators to go again to the palace gate and argue firmly.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Han Wen rallied the Nine Ministers and the censorate officials to march on the palace once more and press their demands.

sentences.zh: 俄有旨，宥八人不問。

translations.literal: Soon there was an edict pardoning the eight men and not pursuing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: An edict soon came, pardoning the eight eunuchs and taking no further action.

sentences.zh: 健、遷倉皇致仕去。

translations.literal: Jian and Qian hastily took retirement and left.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jian and Xie Qian hurriedly retired from office and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 八人各分據要地，瑾掌司禮，時事遂大變。

translations.literal: The eight men each seized important posts; Jin controlled the Directorate of Ceremonial, and affairs of the age then changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: The eight eunuchs each took control of key posts; Liu Jin held the Directorate of Ceremonial, and state affairs were transformed overnight.

sentences.zh: 瑾恨文甚，日令人伺文過。

translations.literal: Jin hated Wen deeply and daily had people watch for Wen's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin hated Han Wen bitterly and daily sent men to watch for his missteps.

sentences.zh: 逾月，有以偽銀輸內庫者，遂以為文罪。

translations.literal: After more than a month, someone delivered counterfeit silver to the inner treasury; this was then made Wen's crime.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later, when someone delivered counterfeit silver to the inner treasury, it was made Han Wen's crime.

sentences.zh: 詔降一級致仕，郎中陳仁謫鈞州同知。

translations.literal: An edict demoted [him] one rank to retirement; Bureau Director Chen Ren was banished to be Assistant Prefect of Junzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted Han Wen one rank and forced his retirement; Bureau Director Chen Ren was relegated to Assistant Prefect of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 給事中徐昂乞留文原官。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Xu Ang petitioned to retain Wen in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Xu Ang petitioned that Han Wen be kept in his original post.

sentences.zh: 中旨謂顯有囑托，落文職，以顧佐代，並除昂名。

translations.literal: A secret edict said there was clearly favoritism, removed Wen from office, replaced him with Gu Zuo, and also struck Ang's name [from the rolls].
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict declared that favoritism was plainly involved, stripped Han Wen of office and replaced him with Gu Zuo, and also struck Xu Ang from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 二年三月榜奸黨姓名，自劉健、謝遷外，尚書則文為首，余若張敷華、楊守隨、林瀚等凡五十三人，列於朝堂。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year [of Zhengde], the names of the faction of wicked men were posted; apart from Liu Jian and Xie Qian, among Ministers of the Ministries Wen was listed first, and besides him such men as Zhang Fuhua, Yang Shousui, and Lin Han—in all fifty-three men—were listed in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year, the names of the 'Wicked Faction' were posted: apart from Liu Jian and Xie Qian, Han Wen headed the list of ministers, and fifty-three men in all—including Zhang Fuhua, Yang Shousui, and Lin Han—were displayed in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 文子高唐知州士聰，刑部主事士奇，皆削籍。

translations.literal: Wen's sons—the Gaotang Prefect Shicong and the Ministry of Justice Director Shiji—were both struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Han Wen's sons—the Gaotang prefect Han Shicong and Ministry of Justice Director Han Shiji—were both struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 文出都門，乘一藍輿，行李一車而已。

translations.literal: Wen left the capital gate, riding in a single blue sedan chair, with only one cart of luggage.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Wen left the capital, he rode in a single blue sedan chair and took only one cart of belongings.

sentences.zh: 瑾恨未已，坐以遺失部籍，逮文及侍郎張縉下詔獄。

translations.literal: Jin's hatred was not yet ended; on the charge of losing ministry registers, he had Wen and Vice Minister Zhang Jin taken down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin's grudge was still not satisfied; on a charge of losing ministry registers, he had Han Wen and Vice Minister Zhang Jin thrown into the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 數月始釋，罰米千石輸大同。

translations.literal: Only after several months were they released; [Wen] was fined a thousand piculs of grain to be delivered to Datong.
translations.idiomatic: They were held for several months before release; Han Wen was fined a thousand piculs of grain, payable to Datong.

sentences.zh: 尋復罰米者再，家業蕩然。

translations.literal: Soon there were two more fines of grain; the family property was utterly depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was fined grain twice more, and the family's fortune was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, [Wen] was restored to office and retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, Han Wen was restored to rank and retired.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，遣行人賫璽書存問，賚羊酒。

translations.literal: When Shizong acceded to the throne, he sent a courier bearing an imperial sealed letter to inquire after him and bestowed mutton and wine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, he sent a courier with an imperial letter of inquiry and rewarded him with mutton and wine.

sentences.zh: 令有司月給廩四石，歲給役夫六人終其身。

translations.literal: He ordered the local authorities to supply four piculs of grain monthly and six corvée laborers yearly for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the local authorities to grant him four piculs of grain each month and six corvée laborers each year for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 復加太子太保，蔭一孫光祿寺署丞。

translations.literal: He was again given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and one grandson was granted the post of Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments through yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and one grandson received the post of Acting Director at the Court of Imperial Entertainments by hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年卒，年八十有六。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he died, aged eighty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Jiajing, at the age of eighty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈太傅，謚忠定。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Tutor and given the posthumous name Zhongding.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously ennobled as Grand Tutor with the posthumous name Zhongding, 'Loyal and Steadfast.'

sentences.zh: 士聰，舉人。

translations.literal: Shicong was a provincial graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Shicong was a provincial graduate.

sentences.zh: 罷官後，不復仕。

translations.literal: After being dismissed from office, he did not serve again.
translations.idiomatic: After his dismissal he never held office again.

sentences.zh: 士奇進士，終湖廣參政。

translations.literal: Shiji was a metropolitan graduate and ended as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was a metropolitan graduate and ended his career as Administrative Commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 少子士賢，亦由舉人為開封同知。

translations.literal: The youngest son Shixian likewise, through the provincial graduate route, became Assistant Prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son Shixian likewise rose from provincial graduate to Assistant Prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 孫廷瑋，進士，行太僕卿。

translations.literal: Sun Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as Acting Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tingwei was a metropolitan graduate and served as acting minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 顧佐，字良弼，臨淮人。

translations.literal: Gu Zuo, styled Liangbi, was a man of Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zuo, styled Liangbi, was from Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate of the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授刑部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed Director in the Ministry of Justice; served through Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Ministry of Justice director and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 按錦衣指揮牛循，中官顧雄、鐘欽罪，無所撓。

translations.literal: Investigating the crimes of Brocade Guard Commander Niu Xun and the eunuchs Gu Xiong and Zhong Qin, he was undeterred in any way.
translations.idiomatic: When investigating Brocade Guard Commander Niu Xun and the eunuchs Gu Xiong and Zhong Qin, he yielded to no pressure.

sentences.zh: 出為河間知府。

translations.literal: He went out to serve as Prefect of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted out as Prefect of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，再遷大理少卿，擢右僉都御史巡撫山西。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, twice promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to serve as Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he was twice promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review, then elevated to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 宗室第宅，官為繕，費不貲，佐請悉令自營治。

translations.literal: Princely estates—the officials repaired them, costs beyond reckoning; Zuo requested that all be made to build and maintain them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen's estates were repaired at government expense at staggering cost; Gu Zuo petitioned that the clansmen be required to build and maintain them themselves.

sentences.zh: 正統末，權發太原、平陽民戍邊，後久不代，佐奏令更代。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengtong, Taiyuan and Pingyang commoners were conscripted on an emergency basis for frontier garrison duty; later they were long unreplaced; Zuo memorialized that replacements be ordered.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengtong, civilians from Taiyuan and Pingyang had been conscripted for emergency frontier service and were long overdue for relief; Gu Zuo memorialized that rotations be enforced.

sentences.zh: 入為左副都御史，勘罷遼東總兵官李杲、太監任良、巡撫張玉，歷戶部左、右侍郎，出理陜西軍食。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, investigated and removed Liaodong Regional Commander Li Gao, the eunuch Ren Liang, and Grand Coordinator Zhang Yu; served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue; went out to administer military provisions in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, he investigated and dismissed Liaodong Regional Commander Li Gao, the eunuch Ren Liang, and Grand Coordinator Zhang Yu; he served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Revenue and was then sent to manage military provisions in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 善區畫，儲蓄余三年。

translations.literal: Skilled at planning, he stored provisions in surplus for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at logistics, he built up stores sufficient for three years.

sentences.zh: 正德改元。

translations.literal: The reign title was changed to Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengde reign began.

sentences.zh: 代韓文為尚書。

translations.literal: He replaced Han Wen as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced Han Wen as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾憾文，捃摭萬端。

translations.literal: Liu Jin resented Wen and gathered evidence on a myriad of counts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin nursed a grudge against Han Wen and scraped together charges on every possible pretext.

sentences.zh: 部有故冊逸，欲以為文罪，逼佐上其事。

translations.literal: The ministry had lost an old register; they wished to make this Wen's crime and pressed Zuo to memorialize the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When an old ministry register went missing, they tried to pin the loss on Han Wen and pressured Gu Zuo to memorialize it.

sentences.zh: 佐不可，坐事奪俸三月。

translations.literal: Zuo refused; on account of the affair his salary was withheld for three months.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zuo refused, and for this he was penalized with three months' salary withheld.

sentences.zh: 佐乃再疏乞歸，從之。

translations.literal: Zuo then memorialized again requesting retirement; [the request] was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zuo memorialized again asking to retire, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 瑾憾不置，三罰米輸塞上，至千余石。

translations.literal: Jin's resentment did not cease; three times he fined grain to be delivered to the frontier, reaching more than a thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin's grudge did not end; he three times imposed fines of grain payable to the frontier, totaling more than a thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 家貧，稱貸以償。

translations.literal: The family was poor and borrowed on credit to pay.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and had to borrow money to pay.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: When he died, he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously ennobled as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 陳仁，字子居，莆田人。

translations.literal: Chen Ren, styled Ziju, was a man of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ren, styled Ziju, was from Putian.

sentences.zh: 成化末進士。

translations.literal: Metropolitan graduate at the end of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination near the end of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，官戶部郎中。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign, he served as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he served as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 闕里先聖廟災，疏請修省。

translations.literal: When the Temple of the Sage at Qufu burned, he memorialized requesting self-examination and reform.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Temple of the Sage at Qufu, he memorialized calling on the court to examine itself and reform.

sentences.zh: 陜西進古璽，仁抗疏斥其偽。

translations.literal: Shaanxi presented an ancient seal; Ren submitted a bold memorial denouncing it as a forgery.
translations.idiomatic: When Shaanxi presented an ancient imperial seal, Chen Ren submitted a forceful memorial denouncing it as a forgery.

sentences.zh: 詔召番僧領占竹於四川，仁疏諫。

translations.literal: An edict summoned a Tibetan monk named Ling Zhanzhu to Sichuan; Ren memorialized in remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict summoned the Tibetan monk Ling Zhanzhu to Sichuan, Chen Ren memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 又請復建文忠臣方孝孺等官。

translations.literal: He also requested restoration of the offices of Jianwen loyalists such as Fang Xiaoru.
translations.idiomatic: He also petitioned to restore the official titles of Jianwen loyalists such as Fang Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 多格不行。

translations.literal: Most were rejected and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his proposals were rejected and went unimplemented.

sentences.zh: 正德初，瑾以贗銀事坐尚書文罪，仁並謫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde, Jin on the counterfeit-silver affair made Minister Wen guilty; Ren was banished along with him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhengde, Liu Jin used the counterfeit silver affair to convict Minister Han Wen, and Chen Ren was demoted along with him.

sentences.zh: 後瑾誅，累擢至浙江右布政使。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, through successive promotions he rose to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin was executed, he was promoted step by step to Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 張敷華，字公實，安福人。

translations.literal: Zhang Fuhua, styled Gongshi, was a man of Anfu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuhua, styled Gongshi, was from Anfu.

sentences.zh: 父洪，御史，死土木難。

translations.literal: His father Hong was a censor and died in the Tumu Crisis.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Hong was a censor who died in the Tumu Crisis.

sentences.zh: 敷華少負氣節。

translations.literal: Fuhua from youth possessed force of character and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth Zhang Fuhua showed moral backbone.

sentences.zh: 年七歲，裏社樹為祟，麾群兒盡伐之。

translations.literal: At age seven, when the village shrine tree was said to be haunted, he led the children to cut it all down.
translations.idiomatic: At seven, when the village shrine tree was said to be haunted, he roused the other children and had them chop it down.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，錄死事後，入國學。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingtai, as a descendant of one who died in service, he entered the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jingtai, as the son of a martyr, he entered the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 舉天順八年進士，選庶吉士。

translations.literal: Passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun; was selected as a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Tianshun and was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 成化元年，與劉大夏願就部曹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chenghua, he and Liu Daxia requested to take posts in the ministries.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chenghua he and Liu Daxia both asked to leave the Hanlin Academy for substantive posts in the ministries.

sentences.zh: 除兵部主事，歷郎中。

translations.literal: Appointed Director in the Ministry of War; served through Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a Ministry of War director and rose to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 廉重不撓，名等於大夏。

translations.literal: Upright, stern, and unyielding, his fame equaled that of Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast in integrity and yielding to no pressure, his reputation matched that of Liu Daxia.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出為浙江參議。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he went out to serve as Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was posted as Administration Vice Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 景寧礦盜起，至數千人。

translations.literal: Mining bandits rose in Jingning, reaching several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Mining bandits rose up in Jingning, numbering several thousand.

sentences.zh: 敷華諭散之，執其魁十二人。

translations.literal: Fuhua admonished them and dispersed them, seizing twelve ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuhua talked them into dispersing and arrested twelve ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 居浙十餘年，歷布政使。

translations.literal: He resided in Zhejiang more than ten years, serving through Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than a decade in Zhejiang, eventually rising to provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，遷湖廣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi, he was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，令府縣大修學宮，以傭直資餓者。

translations.literal: In a year of famine, he ordered prefectures and counties to undertake major repairs of school halls, using labor wages to support the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: During a famine year he ordered prefectures and counties to undertake major repairs of school halls, using the labor wages to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 擢右副都御史，巡撫山西。

translations.literal: Elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 中道奔喪，服闋還故官。

translations.literal: Midway he rushed home on bereavement leave; when mourning ended he returned to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He left mid-term to mourn a parent and returned to his former post when the mourning period ended.

sentences.zh: 部內賦輸大同，困於折價。

translations.literal: Tax grain delivery within his jurisdiction to Datong was troubled by conversion to monetary payment.
translations.idiomatic: Tax deliveries from his jurisdiction to Datong were crippled by the policy of commutation to silver.

sentences.zh: 敷華請太原以北可通車者仍輸米，民便之。

translations.literal: Fuhua requested that north of Taiyuan, wherever carts could pass, grain be delivered as before; the people found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuhua petitioned that for routes north of Taiyuan where carts could travel, grain deliveries should continue in kind—a relief to the people.

sentences.zh: 改撫陜西，制婚娶、喪葬之式，納民於禮。

translations.literal: Transferred to Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi, he prescribed forms for marriage and funeral rites, bringing the people within ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Reassigned to Shaanxi, he regulated the forms of marriage and funeral rites, bringing popular customs back into the bounds of ritual.

sentences.zh: 妖僧據終南山為逆，廷議用兵，尚書馬文升曰：「張都御史能辦此。」

translations.literal: A sorcerer-monk seized Zhongnan Mountain in rebellion; the court deliberated on using troops; Minister Ma Wensheng said, "Censor-in-Chief Zhang can handle this."
translations.idiomatic: When a rebel sorcerer-monk seized Mount Zhongnan, the court debated sending troops; Minister Ma Wensheng said, "Censor-in-Chief Zhang can handle this."

sentences.zh: 敷華果以計縛僧歸。

translations.literal: Fuhua indeed by stratagem bound the monk and brought him back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuhua did in fact capture the monk by stratagem and brought him back.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Transferred to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十二年改右都御史，總督漕運兼巡撫淮、揚諸府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, changed to Right Censor-in-Chief, Grand Coordinator of grain transport and concurrently Grand Coordinator of the Huai and Yang prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Right Censor-in-Chief, directing grain transport and concurrently serving as Grand Coordinator of the Huai and Yang prefectures.

sentences.zh: 高郵湖堤圮，浚深溝以殺水勢。

translations.literal: The Gaoyou Lake dyke collapsed; he dredged deep channels to reduce the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: When the Gaoyou Lake dyke collapsed, he dug deep channels to dissipate the floodwaters.

sentences.zh: 又築寶應堤。

translations.literal: He also built the Baoying dyke.
translations.idiomatic: He also built the Baoying dyke.

sentences.zh: 民利賴焉。

translations.literal: The people relied on these benefits.
translations.idiomatic: The people benefited greatly from his work.

sentences.zh: 改掌南京都察院。

translations.literal: Transferred to head the Nanjing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to head the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 與吏部尚書林瀚、僉都御史林俊、祭酒章懋，稱「南都四君子」，就遷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Together with Minister of Personnel Lin Han, Assistant Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun, and Confucian Director Zhang Mao, he was called the 'Four Gentlemen of the Southern Capital'; he was then promoted to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Minister of Personnel Lin Han, Assistant Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun, and Confucian Director Zhang Mao, he was known as the 'Four Worthies of the Southern Capital'; he was soon promoted to Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 正德元年召為左都御史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, summoned to be Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was recalled as Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 其冬，大臣與言官請去劉瑾等，內閣力主之。

translations.literal: That winter, great ministers and remonstrating officials requested removal of Liu Jin and the others; the Grand Secretariat strongly supported this.
translations.idiomatic: That winter ministers and censorial officials petitioned for the removal of Liu Jin and his allies, and the Grand Secretariat strongly backed them.

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫，敷華乃上言：「陛下宴樂逸遊，日狎憸壬，政令與詔旨相背，行事與成憲交乖，致天變上幹，人心下拂。

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated; Fuhua then submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty feasts and amuses himself in dissolute roaming, daily consorting with crafty sycophants; government orders contradict edicts, and conduct clashes with established statutes, causing celestial anomalies to reach upward and popular sentiment to turn downward.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated, and Zhang Fuhua submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty indulges in feasting and idle roaming, keeping daily company with crafty sycophants; government orders contradict your edicts, and your conduct violates established law—drawing celestial warnings from above and alienating the hearts of the people below.

sentences.zh: 今給事中劉蒨，御史朱廷聲、徐鈺等連章論列，但付所司。

translations.literal: Now Supervising Secretary Liu Qian and Censors Zhu Tingsheng and Xu Yu and others have submitted successive memorials discussing and listing [charges], yet they are merely referred to the responsible offices.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Liu Qian and Censors Zhu Tingsheng and Xu Yu have submitted memorial after memorial laying out the abuses, yet Your Majesty merely refers them to the usual offices.

sentences.zh: 英國公懋與臣等列名上請，但雲『朕自處置」。

translations.literal: The Duke of Ying, Mao, and your servants and others submitted a joint petition listing names, yet [Your Majesty] only said, 'I shall handle it myself.'
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Ying Zhang Mao and we your ministers submitted a joint petition, yet Your Majesty replied only, 'I shall handle it myself.'"

sentences.zh: 臣竊嘆惑，請略言時政之弊。

translations.literal: Your servant privately sighs in perplexity and requests to speak briefly of the abuses of current government.
translations.idiomatic: I must sigh in perplexity and beg leave to speak briefly of the ills of current governance.

sentences.zh: 如四十萬庫藏已竭，而取用不已。

translations.literal: For example, the treasury's four hundred thousand [taels] are already exhausted, yet withdrawals do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The four hundred thousand taels in the treasury are already spent, yet spending continues unabated.

sentences.zh: 六七歲童子何知，而招為勇士。

translations.literal: What do boys of six or seven know, yet they are recruited as bold warriors?
translations.idiomatic: What do six- or seven-year-old boys know of war, yet they are recruited as 'bold warriors'?

sentences.zh: 織造已停，傳奉已革，尋復如故。

translations.literal: Weaving works had been halted, palace appointments had been abolished—soon they were restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: Weaving commissions had been halted and palace appointments abolished—only to be restored as before within days.

sentences.zh: 鹽法、莊田方遣官清核，而奏乞之疏隨聞。

translations.literal: Salt regulations and estate lands had just had officials dispatched to audit and verify them, yet petitions requesting favors follow one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Officials had only just been dispatched to audit the salt monopoly and imperial estates, yet petitions begging for exemptions arrive one after another.

sentences.zh: 中官監督京營、鎮守四方者，一時屢有更易。

translations.literal: Eunuchs supervising the capital garrisons and holding garrison commands across the realm—within a short time there were repeated changes.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs supervising the capital garrisons and holding regional commands were replaced again and again in rapid succession.

sentences.zh: 政令紛，弊端滋蔓。

translations.literal: Government orders are confused; abuses proliferate and spread.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts contradict one another, and abuses spread unchecked.

sentences.zh: 夫國家大事，百人爭之不足，數人壞之有余。

translations.literal: As for great affairs of state—a hundred men striving are not enough; a few men can ruin them with room to spare.
translations.idiomatic: In great affairs of state, a hundred men working together may not suffice—but a handful can ruin everything.

sentences.zh: 願陛下審察。」

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to examine and consider carefully.」
translations.idiomatic: I ask Your Majesty to weigh these matters carefully.

sentences.zh: 疏入，不報。

translations.literal: The memorial entered [court]; there was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was received at court, but no answer was issued.

sentences.zh: 既而朝事大變，宦官勢益張。

translations.literal: Before long court affairs changed greatly, and eunuch power increasingly expanded.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward court politics turned sharply, and the eunuchs' influence grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 至除夕朝罷，忽傳旨與楊守隨俱致仕。

translations.literal: Upon reaching New Year's Eve when court adjourned, suddenly an edict was transmitted that he and Yang Shousui should both retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Eve, after the last court session, an edict suddenly came down ordering him and Yang Shousui to retire together.

sentences.zh: 敷華即日就道。

translations.literal: Fuhua that same day set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhua left the capital that very day.

sentences.zh: 至徐州洪，坐小艇，觸石幾溺死。

translations.literal: Arriving at Xuzhou Hong, riding a small boat, he struck a rock and nearly drowned to death.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hong lock near Xuzhou, his small boat hit a rock and he nearly drowned.

sentences.zh: 瑾恨未已，欲借湖廣倉儲浥爛，坐以贓罪。

translations.literal: Jin's hatred was not yet exhausted; he wished to seize upon Huguang granary stores being damp-rotten and convict [Fuhua] on a charge of embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's spite was still not satisfied. He planned to exploit spoiled grain in the Huguang storehouses and use it to charge Fuhua with embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 修撰康海過瑾曰：「吾秦人愛張公如父母，公忍相薄耶？」

translations.literal: Compiler Kang Hai, calling on Jin, said: 'We men of Qin love Lord Zhang as [we love our] parents—can you bear to treat him harshly?」
translations.idiomatic: The compiler Kang Hai called on Jin and said, "We men of Qin love Master Zhang as we love our own parents. How can you bear to treat him so cruelly?"

sentences.zh: 瑾意稍解，猶坐敷華奸黨，與守隨等榜名朝堂。

translations.literal: Jin's intentions slightly eased, yet [Fuhua] was still convicted as a member of Fuhua's villainous faction, and with Shousui and others their names were posted in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: Jin relented somewhat, but Fuhua was still condemned as a factional criminal, and their names—his, Shousui's, and others'—were posted before the court.

sentences.zh: 明年六月病且革，衣冠揖家廟，就榻而卒。

translations.literal: The next year in the sixth month, his illness being near death, in cap and robe he bowed at the family temple, then upon his couch died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year, as his illness turned critical, he dressed in formal cap and robes, bowed before the family shrine, returned to his bed, and died.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅後二年，贈太子少保，謚簡肅。

translations.literal: Two years after Jin was executed, [he was] posthumously granted Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Jiansu.
translations.idiomatic: Two years after Jin's fall and execution, the court posthumously made him Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and gave him the posthumous name Jiansu, 'Simple and Reverent.'

sentences.zh: 敷華性剛介。

translations.literal: Fuhua's nature was stern and uncompromising.
translations.idiomatic: Fuhua was by nature rigid and upright, unwilling to bend.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，劉大夏常薦之，帝曰：「敷華誠佳，但為人太峻耳。」

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Liu Daxia often recommended him. The Emperor said: 'Fuhua is indeed excellent, but as a man he is too stern.」
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, Liu Daxia frequently recommended him. The emperor replied, "Fuhua is certainly a fine man—but he is too unyielding in character."

sentences.zh: 為部郎奉使，盜探其囊，得七金而已。

translations.literal: Serving as a department secretary on an official mission, a thief searched his purse and found only seven [taels of] gold—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as a department secretary on an assignment abroad, a thief rifled his purse and found only seven taels of silver—nothing more.

sentences.zh: 孫鰲山，官御史。

translations.literal: Sun Aoshan—[his] office: censor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Aoshan became a censor.

sentences.zh: 楊守隨，字維貞，鄞人，侍郎守陳從弟也。

translations.literal: Yang Shousui, courtesy name Weizhen, a man of Yin—Vice Minister Shouchen's younger paternal cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shousui, styled Weizhen, was a native of Yin and a younger cousin of the vice minister Yang Shouchen.

sentences.zh: 舉成化二年進士，授御史。

translations.literal: In Chenghua year 2 he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Chenghua and was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 巡視漕運，核大同軍餉，巡按江西，所至以風采見憚。

translations.literal: He inspected grain transport, audited Datong military provisions, and toured and inspected Jiangxi; wherever he went people feared his imposing presence.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the grain-transport system, audited military pay at Datong, and served as touring censor in Jiangxi—wherever he went, men trembled at his stern authority.

sentences.zh: 六年，疏陳六事，言：「郕王受命艱危時，削平禍亂，功甚大。

translations.literal: In year six he submitted a memorial setting forth six matters, saying: 'The Prince of Cheng received the mandate in a perilous time, quelled turmoil, and his merit was very great.
translations.idiomatic: In his sixth year in office he submitted a memorial on six matters, arguing: 'The Prince of Cheng took up the throne in a time of crisis, put down rebellion, and rendered great service to the realm.

sentences.zh: 歿乃謚以『戾』，公論不平。

translations.literal: After his death he was given the posthumous name 'Li,' and public opinion was not fair.
translations.idiomatic: Yet after his death he was given the posthumous name Li—'Unfilial'—and public opinion has never accepted it as just.

sentences.zh: 此非先帝意，權奸逞私憾者為之也。

translations.literal: This was not the late emperor's intent; a powerful villain indulging private resentment did it.
translations.idiomatic: That was not the late emperor's wish—it was done by a powerful minister venting a private grudge.

sentences.zh: 亟宜改易，彰陛下親親之仁。

translations.literal: It should urgently be changed to display Your Majesty's virtue of cherishing kin.
translations.idiomatic: It should be corrected at once, so that Your Majesty may show the world your devotion to your own flesh and blood.

sentences.zh: 尚書李秉效忠守法，一時良臣，為蕭彥莊誣劾致仕，乞即召還。

translations.literal: Minister Li Bing was loyal and law-abiding, a fine minister of the time; he was slanderously impeached by Xiao Yanzhuang and forced to retire—I beg that he be immediately recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Li Bing served with loyalty and upheld the law; he was one of the finest officials of his day. Xiao Yanzhuang falsely impeached him and drove him from office. I ask that he be recalled at once.

sentences.zh: 律令犯公罪者不罷，近御史朱賢、婁芳等並除名，乞復其官，且戒所司毋法外加罪，一以律令從事。

translations.literal: By statute and ordinance, those who commit public crimes are not dismissed; recently Censors Zhu Xian, Lou Fang, and others were all stripped of their names—I beg that their offices be restored, and that officials be warned not to add crimes beyond the law, handling all matters strictly according to statute.
translations.idiomatic: The law does not require dismissal for public offenses, yet Censors Zhu Xian, Lou Fang, and others were recently expelled from office. I ask that they be reinstated, and that all departments be warned against inventing charges beyond what the law provides.

sentences.zh: 西征之役，以數萬甲兵討出沒不常之寇，千里轉輸，曠日持久。

translations.literal: The western campaign uses tens of thousands of armored troops to suppress raiders who appear and vanish without pattern; supplies are transported a thousand li, and the days drag on without end.
translations.idiomatic: The western campaign sends tens of thousands of soldiers after raiders who strike and vanish at will. Supply lines stretch a thousand li, and the war drags on without resolution.

sentences.zh: 恐外患未平，內地先敝。

translations.literal: I fear that before external trouble is settled, the interior will first be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: I fear the frontier may never be pacified while the heartland is worn down first.

sentences.zh: 乞速班師，戒邊臣慎封守。

translations.literal: I beg that the army be swiftly withdrawn and border officials warned to guard the frontier carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the troops be recalled promptly and that frontier commanders be charged to hold the borders with care.

sentences.zh: 近例，軍官犯罪未結正者，遇赦即原，致此曹遷延，以希幸免。

translations.literal: By recent precedent, military officers whose crimes are not yet finally adjudicated are pardoned when an amnesty occurs, causing these men to delay proceedings in hope of escaping punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under recent practice, military officers whose cases remain open are pardoned whenever an amnesty is declared, so offenders stall proceedings hoping to slip free.

sentences.zh: 自今眾證明白者，即據律定案，毋使逃罪。

translations.literal: From now on, where collective evidence is clear, let the case be decided immediately according to law, and do not let guilt escape.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when the evidence is conclusive, cases should be decided at once under the law, with no opportunity to evade punishment.

sentences.zh: 雖遇赦免，亦不得管軍。

translations.literal: Even if they encounter amnesty and are spared, they still may not command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Even when pardoned, they should never again be allowed to command troops.

sentences.zh: 在外官俸、兵餉，有逾年不給者，由郡縣蓄積少也。

translations.literal: Official salaries and military pay in the provinces sometimes go unpaid for more than a year, because prefectures and counties accumulate too little.
translations.idiomatic: Salaries and military pay in the provinces sometimes go unpaid for more than a year because local governments hold too little in reserve.

sentences.zh: 請於起運外，量加存留，以濟乏匱。」

translations.literal: I request that beyond the amount dispatched for transport, a measured portion be retained locally to relieve shortage and destitution.」
translations.idiomatic: I ask that a portion of grain be retained locally, beyond what is shipped out, to meet urgent shortfalls.'

sentences.zh: 疏奏，時不能從。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; at the time [the court] could not comply.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the court would not act on it.

sentences.zh: 太常少卿孫廣安母喪起復，守隨與給事中李和等連章論之，乃令守制。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Sun Guo'an was recalled from mourning for his mother; Shousui together with Supervising Secretary Li He and others submitted successive memorials arguing against it, and [Sun] was then ordered to observe mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When Vice Director Sun Guo'an was recalled to office while still in mourning for his mother, Shousui joined Supervising Secretary Li He and others in a series of memorials protesting the appointment, and Sun was finally ordered to resume mourning.

sentences.zh: 八年冬以災異陳時政九事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, winter, on account of disasters and portents he set forth nine matters of current policy.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of his eighth year he submitted nine policy recommendations in response to natural disasters and ominous signs.

sentences.zh: 廷議四方災傷，停遣刷卷御史。

translations.literal: The court discussed disasters and damage in all directions and halted the dispatch of document-reviewing censors.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated famine and disaster across the realm, it agreed to suspend sending out censors to review local records.

sentences.zh: 會昌侯孫繼宗請並停在京者，守隨言：「繼宗等任情作奸，恐罪及，假此祈免。」

translations.literal: Marquis of Huichang Sun Jizong requested that those in the capital also be halted. Shousui said: 'Jizong and others act wilfully and commit wrongdoing; fearing guilt will reach them, they use this to seek exemption.」
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Sun Jizong asked that the censors stationed in the capital be suspended as well. Shousui objected: "Men like Jizong have long abused their power. Fearing prosecution, they are using this proposal to escape scrutiny."

sentences.zh: 帝置繼宗不問，而刷卷如故。

translations.literal: The Emperor set Jizong aside without inquiry, and document review continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ignored Jizong's request, and the document reviews continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 山東饑，廷議吏納銀免考，授冠帶。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered famine; the court discussed officials paying silver to be exempted from examination and granted ceremonial cap and sash.
translations.idiomatic: During famine in Shandong, the court debated letting officials buy their way out of performance review with silver in exchange for honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 守隨極言不可，帝即罷之。

translations.literal: Shousui spoke with utmost force that it could not be done; the Emperor immediately abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: Shousui argued vehemently against the plan, and the emperor dropped it at once.

sentences.zh: 擢應天府丞，未上，母憂歸。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Assistant Prefect of Yingtian; before taking office, his mother died and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to assistant prefect of Yingtian, but before he could take up the post his mother died and he went home to mourn.

sentences.zh: 服除無缺，添註視事。

translations.literal: When mourning ended there was no vacancy; he was added as supernumerary to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended no regular post was open, so he was assigned supernumerary duties.

sentences.zh: 初，李孜省授太常寺丞，因守隨言改上林監副，憾之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zisheng was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; because of Shousui's words [the appointment] was changed to Assistant Supervisor of the Upper Forest Park, and [Li] resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Zisheng had been appointed vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but after Shousui objected the appointment was changed to assistant supervisor of the imperial park—a demotion Li never forgave.

sentences.zh: 至是譖於帝，中旨責守隨不當添註，調南寧知府。

translations.literal: At this time he slandered [Shousui] to the Emperor; a secret edict blamed Shousui for improper supernumerary assignment and transferred him to Prefect of Nanning.
translations.idiomatic: Now Li denounced him to the emperor. By secret edict Shousui was rebuked for accepting a supernumerary post and transferred to prefect of Nanning.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，召為應天府尹，勘南京守備中官蔣琮罪。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was recalled as Prefect of Yingtian and investigated the crimes of the Nanjing garrison eunuch Jiang Cong.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he was recalled to serve as prefect of Yingtian and was charged with investigating the eunuch Jiang Cong, military superintendent at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 琮嗾其黨郭鏞劾守隨按給事方向獄不公，謫廣西右參政。

translations.literal: Cong instigated his follower Guo Yong to impeach Shousui for unfair handling of Supervising Secretary Xiang Fang's case, and [Shousui] was demoted to Right Vice Commissioner in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Cong then had his ally Guo Yong impeach Shousui for mishandling the case of Supervising Secretary Xiang Fang, and Shousui was demoted to vice commissioner in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 久之，進按察使。

translations.literal: After a long time he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Years later he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八年召為南京右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: In year eight he was summoned as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing, supervising patrol of the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled to Nanjing as right vice censor-in-chief with command over Yangtze River defenses.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京大理卿。

translations.literal: He served successively as Chief Judge of the Great Court of Appeals in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as chief judge of the Great Court of Appeals in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 九載滿，進工部尚書，仍掌大理寺。

translations.literal: When nine years were complete he was promoted to Minister of Works, still holding charge of the Great Court of Appeals.
translations.idiomatic: After nine years in office he was promoted to minister of works while continuing to head the Great Court of Appeals.

sentences.zh: 刑部獄送寺覆讞者多加刑，主事朱瑽論其非。

translations.literal: Prisoners sent from the Ministry of Punishments to the Court for review of sentences often received heavier punishment; Chief Clerk Zhu Zheng argued that this was wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners sent from the Ministry of Punishments for sentence review at the Court often received harsher penalties; Chief Clerk Zhu Zheng protested that this was improper.

sentences.zh: 守隨言：「自永樂間，寺已設刑具。

translations.literal: Shousui said: 'Since the Yongle period, the Court has already had punishment implements.
translations.idiomatic: Shousui replied, 'The Court has maintained instruments of punishment since the Yongle reign.

sentences.zh: 部囚多未得實，安得不更訊。」

translations.literal: Prisoners from the Ministry mostly have not yet obtained the truth—how can they not be re-interrogated?」
translations.idiomatic: Most cases arriving from the Ministry are still unproved—how can we fail to examine them again?'

sentences.zh: 帝乃瑽寢奏。

translations.literal: The Emperor then shelved Zhu Zheng's memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then set Zhu's memorial aside.

sentences.zh: 孝宗崩，中官張瑜等以誤用禦藥下獄，守隨會訊杖之。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong died, eunuchs Zhang Yu and others were imprisoned for wrongly using imperial medicine; Shousui joined in the interrogation and had them beaten.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozong's death, the eunuchs Zhang Yu and others were imprisoned for administering the wrong medicine to the emperor. Shousui took part in their interrogation and ordered them flogged.

sentences.zh: 正德元年四月，守隨奏：「每歲熱審，行於京師而不行於南京，五歲一審錄，詳於在京而略於在外，皆非是。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, fourth month, Shousui submitted: 'Each year's hot-weather review is conducted in the capital but not in Nanjing; the review every five years is detailed for those in the capital but cursory for those outside—all of this is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhengde, Shousui memorialized: 'The annual summer review of prisoners is held in Beijing but not in Nanjing, and the quinquennial review is thorough for the capital but perfunctory for the provinces—both practices are wrong.

sentences.zh: 請更定其制。」

translations.literal: I request that the system be revised and fixed.」
translations.idiomatic: I ask that these procedures be reformed.'

sentences.zh: 報可。

translations.literal: [The memorial] was reported and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 中官李興擅伐陵木論死，令家人以銀四十萬兩求變其獄。

translations.literal: Eunuch Li Xing, for illegally felling tomb timber, was sentenced to death; he had his family members offer four hundred thousand taels of silver to seek alteration of his case.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Li Xing was sentenced to death for illegally cutting timber from the imperial tombs. His family offered four hundred thousand taels of silver to have the verdict overturned.

sentences.zh: 守隨持之堅，獄不得解。

translations.literal: Shousui held firm, and the case could not be resolved [in Li's favor].
translations.idiomatic: Shousui stood firm, and the case could not be overturned.

sentences.zh: 廷臣之爭余鹽也，中旨詰「是何大事？」

translations.literal: When court ministers disputed surplus salt, a secret edict questioned: 'What great matter is this?」
translations.idiomatic: When court officials protested the surplus-salt monopoly, a secret edict demanded: "What is so important about this?"

sentences.zh: 守隨語韓文曰：「事誠有大於是者。」

translations.literal: Shousui told Han Wen: 'The matter truly has greater [issues] than this.'」
translations.idiomatic: Shousui told Han Wen, 'There are matters far graver than this.'

sentences.zh: 文遂偕九卿伏闕論「八黨」。

translations.literal: Wen then together with the Nine Ministers knelt at the palace gate to discuss the 'Eight Faction.'
translations.idiomatic: Han Wen then joined the Nine Ministers in kneeling before the palace gate to denounce the 'Eight Tigers.'

sentences.zh: 文等既逐，守隨憤，獨上章極論之曰：

translations.literal: After Wen and the others were expelled, Shousui in anger alone submitted a memorial vehemently arguing, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After Han Wen and the others were driven from office, Shousui, furious, submitted a lone memorial of his own, arguing with full force:

sentences.zh: 陛下嗣位以來，左右迫臣，不能只承德意，盡取先朝良法而更張之，盡誣先朝碩輔而刬汰之。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty succeeded to the throne, those at your side have compelled ministers; [Your Majesty] cannot simply inherit the late emperor's intent—[you] take all the good laws of the prior dynasty and overturn them, and slander all the great aides of the prior dynasty and purge them.
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty took the throne, those around you have pressed your ministers so hard that you can no longer carry forward the late emperor's wise policies. Good institutions of the previous reign have been overturned wholesale, and eminent ministers of that era have been slandered and driven out.

sentences.zh: 天下嗷嗷，莫措手足，致古今罕見之災，交集數月以內。

translations.literal: Under Heaven there is clamor; nowhere can hands and feet be placed; causing disasters rare in ancient and modern times to converge within a few months.
translations.idiomatic: The realm groans in distress and men scarcely know what to do. Disasters seldom seen in any age have struck one after another within the space of a few months.

sentences.zh: 陛下獨不思其故乎？

translations.literal: Does Your Majesty alone not think of the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Does Your Majesty never ask why this is so?

sentences.zh: 內臣劉瑾等八人，奸險佞巧，誣罔恣肆，人目為「八虎」，而瑾尤甚，日以荒縱導陛下。

translations.literal: The eight inner ministers Liu Jin and others are treacherous, dangerous, sycophantic, and cunning; they deceive, obstruct, and act wilfully—people call them the 'Eight Tigers,' and Jin is worst of all, daily guiding Your Majesty with dissipation and indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: The eight inner ministers led by Liu Jin are treacherous, deceitful, and utterly unrestrained. Men call them the 'Eight Tigers,' and Jin is the worst of them—day after day he leads Your Majesty deeper into dissipation.

sentences.zh: 或在西海擎鷹搏兔，或於南城躡峻登高，禁內鼓鉦震於遠邇，宮中火炮聲徹晝夜。
