translations.literal: Sometimes in the Western Sea [they] hold hawks and hunt rabbits; sometimes in the southern city [they] climb steep heights; within the forbidden precinct drums and gongs shake far and near, and in the palace cannon fire sounds through day and night.
translations.idiomatic: One day they hawk and hunt rabbits in the Western Sea; the next they climb steep heights in the southern quarter of the city. Drums and gongs thunder through the palace precincts, and cannon fire echoes day and night.

sentences.zh: 淆雜尊卑，陵夷貴賤。

translations.literal: They mix and confuse honorable and base; they erode and degrade noble and low.
translations.idiomatic: They blur the line between high and low and trample the order of rank.

sentences.zh: 引車騎而供執鞭之役，列市肆而親商賈之為。

translations.literal: They lead chariots and horsemen yet perform the service of holding the whip; they line up market stalls yet personally do the deeds of merchants.
translations.idiomatic: They command carriages and cavalry yet take the whip in hand themselves; they set up market stalls and haggle like common traders.

sentences.zh: 致陛下日高未朝，漏盡不寢。

translations.literal: They cause Your Majesty, when the sun is high, not yet to hold court; when the water clock is empty, not yet to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: They have brought Your Majesty to the point where the sun stands high before you hold court, and the night is far spent before you retire.

sentences.zh: 此數人者，方且竊攬威權，詐傳詔旨。

translations.literal: These few men are just now secretly grasping awesome power and falsely transmitting imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: These men have already seized power for themselves and circulate forged edicts in Your Majesty's name.

sentences.zh: 放逐大臣，刑誅臺諫。

translations.literal: They exile great ministers and punish and execute censorate remonstrators.
translations.idiomatic: They banish senior ministers and punish or execute the censors who speak out.

sentences.zh: 邀阻封章，廣納貨賂。

translations.literal: They intercept and block sealed memorials and widely accept goods and bribes.
translations.idiomatic: They intercept memorials bound for the throne and take bribes on a vast scale.

sentences.zh: 傳奉冗員，多至千百。

translations.literal: Supernumerary posts by transmitted appointment reach as many as hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: They have created hundreds and even thousands of superfluous appointments by personal edict.

sentences.zh: 招募武勇，收及孩童。

translations.literal: They recruit martial braves, gathering even children.
translations.idiomatic: They recruit fighting men—and even enlist boys.

sentences.zh: 紫綬金貂盡予爪牙之士，蟒衣玉帶濫授心腹之人。

translations.literal: Purple sashes and golden rank badges are all given to claw-and-tooth men; python robes and jade belts are lavishly granted to trusted followers.
translations.idiomatic: They bestow purple sashes and golden badges on their henchmen, and hand out python robes and jade belts to their inner circle without restraint.

sentences.zh: 附己者進官，忤意者褫職。

translations.literal: Those who attach to them receive promotion; those who disobey their intent are stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Those who align with them are promoted; those who cross them are dismissed.

sentences.zh: 內外臣僚。

translations.literal: Inner and outer officials and aides.
translations.idiomatic: Officials throughout the government—

sentences.zh: 但知畏瑾，不知畏陛下。

translations.literal: Only know fear of Jin, and do not know fear of Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: —now fear Jin alone and no longer fear Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 向也二三大臣受遺夾輔，今則有潛交默附、漏泄事機者矣。

translations.literal: Formerly two or three great ministers received the testament and assisted from both sides; now there are those who secretly associate, silently attach, and leak affairs and secrets.
translations.idiomatic: Once, two or three senior ministers stood by the late emperor's deathbed to guide the new reign. Now there are men who secretly court the eunuchs and leak state secrets.

sentences.zh: 向也南北群僚，矢心痛疾，今則有畫策主文，依附時勢者矣。

translations.literal: Formerly north and south officials in groups, arrow-like in heart and pained in sickness; now there are those who draft strategies and compose essays, attaching to the current power.
translations.idiomatic: Once, officials north and south grieved for the realm as if pierced to the heart. Now there are men who draft policy and write memorials to curry favor with the prevailing power.

sentences.zh: 而且數易邊境將帥之臣，大更四方鎮守之職，誌欲何為？

translations.literal: Moreover they frequently change border generals and commanders, and greatly alter garrison posts in all directions—what intent do they harbor?
translations.idiomatic: They constantly replace frontier commanders and shuffle regional garrison appointments—what do they intend?

sentences.zh: 夫太阿之柄不可授人。

translations.literal: The handle of supreme authority must not be entrusted to others.
translations.idiomatic: The sword of supreme power must never be placed in another's hands.

sentences.zh: 今陛下於兵刑財賦之區，機務根本之地，悉以委之。

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty in the zones of military affairs, punishment, finance, and taxation—in places fundamental to state business—entrusts all to them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty has entrusted them with every domain that matters—war, justice, revenue, and the machinery of government itself.

sentences.zh: 或掌團營，或主兩廠，或典司禮，或督倉場，大權在手，彼復何憚？

translations.literal: Some manage training camps, some head the two bureaus, some preside over ritual affairs, some supervise granary depots—with great power in hand, what would they fear?
translations.idiomatic: Some command the training camps, some head the secret police bureaus, some oversee court ritual, some control the granaries—with such power in their grasp, what would they not dare?

sentences.zh: 於是大行殺戮，廣肆誅求。

translations.literal: Thereupon they greatly carry out slaughter and widely practice extortion and pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: They have unleashed a reign of bloodshed and extortion across the land.

sentences.zh: 府藏竭於上，財力匱於下，武勇疲於邊。

translations.literal: Treasury stores are exhausted above, financial strength is depleted below, and martial courage is worn out at the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial treasury is empty, the provinces are drained, and the frontier armies are exhausted.

sentences.zh: 上下胥讒，神人共憤。

translations.literal: Above and below all slander; gods and men jointly rage.
translations.idiomatic: Recrimination fills every level of government, and both heaven and earth cry out in anger.

sentences.zh: 陛下猶不覺悟，方且謂委任得人，何其舛也！

translations.literal: Your Majesty still does not awaken to this, yet just now says that entrusting [power] has obtained the right men—how wrong!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty remains unaware of all this and even declares that you have chosen the right men—how grievously mistaken!

sentences.zh: 伏望大奮乾綱，立置此曹重典，遠鑒延熹之失，毋使臣蹈蕃、武已覆之轍。

translations.literal: I humbly hope Your Majesty will greatly rouse the imperial authority, immediately impose heavy punishment on this lot, take distant mirror from the error of Yanshi, and do not let your minister tread the already overturned track of Fan and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to seize hold of imperial authority, punish these men without delay, heed the lesson of the Yanshi reign, and do not let your servant follow in the doomed footsteps of the eunuchs Fan and Wu.

sentences.zh: 疏入，帝不省。

translations.literal: The memorial entered; the Emperor did not examine it.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the emperor paid it no heed.

sentences.zh: 瑾輩深銜之，傳旨致仕。

translations.literal: Jin's clique deeply harbored resentment toward him and transmitted an edict [ordering him] to retire from office.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and his followers deeply resented him and issued an edict forcing him to retire.

sentences.zh: 守隨去，李興遂以中旨免死矣。

translations.literal: Shousui departed; Li Xing then by secret edict was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shousui was gone, Li Xing was spared execution by secret edict.

sentences.zh: 瑾憾未釋。

translations.literal: Jin's resentment was not yet released.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's grudge was still not satisfied.

sentences.zh: 三年四月坐覆讞失出，逮赴京系獄，罰米千石輸塞上。

translations.literal: In year three, fourth month, convicted for review of sentence with erroneous release, he was arrested, sent to the capital, imprisoned, and fined one thousand shi of grain to be delivered to frontier fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he was convicted of releasing a prisoner improperly during sentence review, arrested and sent to the capital, imprisoned, and fined one thousand shi of grain for the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復坐庇鄉人重獄，除名，追毀誥命，再罰米二百石。

translations.literal: After more than a year, again convicted for shielding a fellow townsman's serious case, his name was removed, his patent of honor was pursued and destroyed, and he was again fined two hundred shi of grain.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later he was convicted again for shielding a townsman in a capital case. He was expelled from office, his patents of honor were revoked, and he was fined another two hundred shi of grain.

sentences.zh: 守隨家立破。

translations.literal: Shousui's household immediately was ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Shousui's family was ruined overnight.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, [his] office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's execution he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 又十年卒，年八十五。

translations.literal: After another ten years he died, age eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Ten years later he died, at the age of eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚康簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously awarded Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous name Kangjian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous name Kangjian (Simple and Upright).

sentences.zh: 從弟守隅，由進士歷官江西參政，有政績。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Shouyu, through jinshi appointment, successively held office as Jiangxi Provincial Administrator, with administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: His younger cousin Shouyu, a jinshi graduate, rose through the ranks to serve as Jiangxi Provincial Administrator and won a record of solid governance.

sentences.zh: 寧府祿米，石征銀一兩，後漸增十之五。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning's stipend grain was levied at one tael of silver per shi; later it was gradually increased by five-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning's stipend grain had been assessed at one tael of silver per shi, but the levy was later raised by half.

sentences.zh: 守隅入請於王，裁減如舊。

translations.literal: Shouyu entered and petitioned the prince, who cut [the levy] back as before.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyu went in person to petition the prince, who reduced the levy to its former rate.

sentences.zh: 瑾惡守隨，並罷守隅官。

translations.literal: Jin hated Shousui and also dismissed Shouyu from office.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jin hated Shousui, he also stripped Shouyu of his post.

sentences.zh: 瑾死後，起官四川，終廣西布政使。

translations.literal: After Jin died, [Shouyu] was reappointed in Sichuan and ultimately served as Guangxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's death he was recalled to serve in Sichuan and eventually ended his career as Guangxi Provincial Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 許進，字季升，靈寶人。

translations.literal: Xu Jin, style name Jisheng, was a native of Lingbao.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jin, styled Jisheng, was a native of Lingbao.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the second year of the Chenghua reign.

sentences.zh: 除御史。

translations.literal: Appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a censor.

sentences.zh: 歷按甘肅、山東，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He successively toured and inspected Gansu and Shandong, both with reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He successively conducted inspections in Gansu and Shandong, earning a strong reputation in both provinces.

sentences.zh: 陳鉞激變遼東，為御史強珍所劾，進亦率同官論之。

translations.literal: Chen Yue provoked rebellion in Liaodong and was impeached by Censor Qiang Zhen; Jin also led fellow censors in denouncing him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Yue stirred up unrest in Liaodong, Censor Qiang Zhen impeached him, and Jin led his fellow censors in joining the denunciation.

sentences.zh: 汪直怒，構珍下獄，摘進他疏偽字，廷杖之幾殆。

translations.literal: Wang Zhi was enraged, framed Zhen and imprisoned him, picked out forged characters in Jin's other memorials, and had him beaten in court almost to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhi was furious. He framed Zhen and had him thrown into prison, then seized on spurious characters in Jin's other memorials and had Jin beaten in the outer court, nearly killing him.

sentences.zh: 滿三考，遷山東副使。

translations.literal: After completing three terms of evaluation, he was transferred to Shandong Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After three rounds of performance review he was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 辨疑獄，人稱神明。

translations.literal: He settled doubtful criminal cases; people called him divinely perceptive.
translations.idiomatic: He resolved baffling criminal cases, and people hailed him as uncannily perceptive.

sentences.zh: 分巡遼東，坐累，征下詔獄。

translations.literal: While divisional intendant of Liaodong, he was implicated and summoned to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as divisional intendant of Liaodong he was caught up in a case, summoned to the capital, and imprisoned in the imperial jail.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嗣位，釋還。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong succeeded, [he] was released and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong came to the throne, he was released and allowed to return home.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年擢右僉都御史，巡撫大同。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Datong.

sentences.zh: 小王子久不通貢，遣使千五百余人款關，進以便宜納之。

translations.literal: The Little Prince had long ceased tribute; he sent more than 1,500 emissaries to present themselves at the pass, and Jin at his discretion admitted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Little Prince had long stopped sending tribute. He dispatched more than fifteen hundred emissaries to present themselves at the border pass, and Jin, exercising his discretionary authority, admitted them.

sentences.zh: 請於朝，詔許五百人至京師。

translations.literal: He petitioned the court; an edict permitted five hundred persons to come to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He reported the matter to court, and an edict allowed five hundred of them to proceed to the capital.

sentences.zh: 已而屢盜邊，進被劾，不問。

translations.literal: Before long [they] repeatedly raided the border; Jin was impeached but not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they raided the frontier again and again. Jin was impeached, but no action was taken against him.

sentences.zh: 三年復窺邊，進等整軍待之。

translations.literal: In the third year [they] again spied on the border; Jin and others marshaled the army to await them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they again probed the frontier. Jin and his officers mustered their forces and stood ready.

sentences.zh: 新寧伯譚祐以京軍援，乃遁去。

translations.literal: The Earl of Xining Tan You came with capital troops as reinforcements, and [they] then fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Earl of Xining, Tan You, arrived with capital reinforcements, the raiders fled.

sentences.zh: 又乞通貢，進再為請，帝許之。

translations.literal: They again sought to resume tribute; Jin once more pleaded on their behalf, and the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: They again petitioned to reopen tribute relations. Jin interceded for them a second time, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 當是時，大同士馬盛強，邊防修整。

translations.literal: At that time Datong's troops and horses were numerous and strong, and border defenses were well maintained.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Datong's forces were at full strength and the frontier defenses were in excellent order.

sentences.zh: 貢使每至關，率下馬脫弓矢入館，俯首聽命，無敢嘩者。

translations.literal: Whenever tribute emissaries reached the pass, they invariably dismounted, laid aside bow and arrows, entered the guesthouse, bowed their heads and obeyed orders, and none dared make a commotion.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tribute envoys reached the pass, they invariably dismounted, laid down their bows and arrows, entered the guesthouse, bowed their heads, and obeyed orders without a murmur of defiance.

sentences.zh: 會進與分守中官石巖相訐，巖征還，進亦謫兗州知府。

translations.literal: When Jin quarreled with the eunuch defender Shi Yan, Yan was recalled and Jin was also demoted to prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then clashed with the eunuch defender Shi Yan. Yan was recalled to the capital, and Jin was demoted to prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年遷陜西按察使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was transferred to Shaanxi Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to the post of Shaanxi Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 土魯番阿黑麻攻陷哈密，執忠順王陜巴去，使其將牙蘭守之。

translations.literal: Turpan's Aq Aqma attacked and captured Hami, seized the loyal and submissive king Shaban and carried him away, and set his general Yalian to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Aq Aqma of Turpan stormed and seized Hami, took the loyal and submissive king Shaban captive, and left his general Yalian to hold the city.

sentences.zh: 尚書馬文升謂復哈密非進不可，乃薦為右僉都御史，巡撫甘肅。

translations.literal: Minister Ma Wensheng said recovering Hami could not be achieved without Jin, and so recommended him as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ma Wensheng declared that Hami could not be recovered without Xu Jin and recommended him for appointment as Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 明年蒞鎮，告諸將曰：「小醜陸梁，謂我不敢深入耳。

translations.literal: The next year he arrived to take command and told the generals: "These petty villains run riot, thinking we dare not push deep.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took up his command and told his generals, "These petty raiders strut about because they think we dare not strike deep into their territory.

sentences.zh: 堂堂天朝不能發一鏃塞外，何以慰遠人。」

translations.literal: How can the august Celestial dynasty not let fly a single arrow beyond the frontier — how are we to reassure distant peoples?
translations.idiomatic: Can the great Celestial dynasty not send a single arrow beyond the frontier? How else are we to reassure the peoples on our borders?"

sentences.zh: 諸將難之。

translations.literal: The generals objected.
translations.idiomatic: The generals balked at the plan.

sentences.zh: 乃獨與總兵官劉寧謀，厚結小列禿，使以四千騎往，殺數百人，小列禿中流矢卒。

translations.literal: He then alone consulted with Commander-in-chief Liu Ning, lavishly won over Xiaolietu, and had him go with four thousand horsemen; several hundred were killed, and Xiaolietu was struck by a flying arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then conferred privately with Commander-in-chief Liu Ning, lavishly secured the alliance of Xiaolietu, and sent him forward with four thousand horsemen. Several hundred enemies were killed, but Xiaolietu was hit by a stray arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 小列禿故與土魯番世相仇，及死，其子卜六阿歹益憤。

translations.literal: Xiaolietu had long been hereditary enemies with Turpan; after his death, his son Buluo'adai grew all the more enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaolietu had been hereditary enemies of Turpan for generations. After his death his son Buluo'adai was all the more inflamed with hatred.

sentences.zh: 進復厚結之，使斷賊道，無令東援牙蘭，而重犒赤斤、罕東及哈密遺種之居苦峪者，令出兵助討。

translations.literal: Jin again lavishly won him over and had him cut the enemy's route so that no eastern reinforcements could reach Yalian; he also generously rewarded Chijin, Handong, and Hami remnant tribes dwelling at Kuyu, ordering them to send troops to assist the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Jin again won Buluo'adai over with rich gifts and had him block the enemy's supply lines so that no reinforcements could reach Yalian from the east. He also handsomely rewarded the Chijin and Handong tribes and the Hami remnant peoples living at Kuyu, ordering them to join the expedition.

sentences.zh: 十一月，副將彭清以精騎千五百出嘉峪關前行，寧與中官陸訚統二千五百騎繼之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Vice Commander Peng Qing led fifteen hundred elite cavalry out through Jiayu Pass first; Ning and the eunuch Lu Yan commanded twenty-five hundred cavalry in follow-up.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Vice Commander Peng Qing led fifteen hundred elite cavalry out through Jiayu Pass as the vanguard, while Ning and the eunuch Lu Yan followed with twenty-five hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 越八日，諸軍俱會，羽集乜川。

translations.literal: After eight days all armies assembled, gathering swiftly at Michuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eight days later the armies converged, gathering in force at Michuan.

sentences.zh: 薄暮大風揚沙，軍士寒栗僵臥。

translations.literal: At dusk a great wind blew up sand; the soldiers shivered with cold and lay stiff.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk a fierce wind whipped up the sand. The soldiers shivered with cold and lay stiff on the ground.

sentences.zh: 進出帳外勞軍，有異烏悲鳴，將士多雨泣。

translations.literal: Jin came out of his tent to encourage the troops; a strange bird wailed mournfully, and many officers and men wept in the rain.
translations.idiomatic: Jin came out of his tent to rally the men. A strange bird cried mournfully overhead, and many officers and soldiers wept in the driving rain.

sentences.zh: 進慷慨曰：「男兒報國，死沙場幸耳，何泣為！」

translations.literal: Jin spoke ardently: "For a man to serve the state, dying on the battlefield is fortune itself — why weep!
translations.idiomatic: Jin spoke with fierce conviction: "A man serves his country — to die on the battlefield is good fortune. Why weep?"

sentences.zh: 將士皆感奮。

translations.literal: The officers and men were all stirred and roused.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men alike were moved and rallied to the cause.

sentences.zh: 夜半風止，大雨雪。

translations.literal: At midnight the wind stopped; heavy snow and rain fell.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the wind died away and a heavy snowstorm set in.

sentences.zh: 時番兵俱集，惟罕東兵未至，眾欲待之。

translations.literal: At the time all the frontier troops had gathered, but Handong's forces had not arrived; the multitude wished to wait.
translations.idiomatic: By then the frontier allies had all assembled, but the Handong contingent had not yet arrived, and many wanted to wait for them.

sentences.zh: 進曰：「潛師遠襲，利在捷速，兵已足用，不須待也。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "A secret force raiding from afar profits from speed; the troops we have are sufficient — there is no need to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "A secret force striking from afar depends on speed. We already have enough men — there is no need to wait."

sentences.zh: 及明，冒雪倍道進。

translations.literal: At daybreak they pushed forward through the snow by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they pressed forward through the snow at double speed.

sentences.zh: 又六日奄至哈密城下。

translations.literal: Six days later they suddenly arrived beneath Hami's walls.
translations.idiomatic: Six days later they suddenly appeared beneath the walls of Hami.

sentences.zh: 牙蘭已先遁去，余賊拒守。

translations.literal: Yalian had already fled ahead of time; the remaining bandits held out in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yalian had already fled, and the remaining defenders held the city.

sentences.zh: 官軍四面並進，拔其城，獲陜巴妻女。

translations.literal: Government troops advanced on all four sides, stormed the city, and captured Shaban's wife and daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Government forces attacked from all four sides, took the city, and captured Shaban's wife and daughter.

sentences.zh: 賊退保土剌。

translations.literal: The bandits retreated to hold Tula.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy withdrew to make a stand at Tula.

sentences.zh: 土剌，華言大臺也。

translations.literal: Tula — in Chinese speech, "Great Terrace."
translations.idiomatic: Tula — in Chinese, the "Great Terrace."

sentences.zh: 守者八百人，諸軍再戰不下。

translations.literal: Eight hundred defenders; the armies fought again but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Eight hundred men held the position, and even after renewed fighting the armies could not break through.

sentences.zh: 問其俘，則皆哈密人為牙蘭所劫者，進乃令勿攻。

translations.literal: Questioning their captives, [they found] they were all Hami people whom Yalian had seized by force; Jin then ordered that there be no attack.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogating prisoners, they learned that the defenders were all Hami people whom Yalian had forced into service. Jin then ordered the attack halted.

sentences.zh: 或欲盡殲之，進不可，遣使撫諭即下。

translations.literal: Some wanted to annihilate them entirely; Jin would not allow it and sent messengers to soothe and instruct them, whereupon they surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged that they be wiped out entirely, but Jin refused. He sent envoys to reassure them, and they surrendered at once.

sentences.zh: 於是探牙蘭所向，分守要害。

translations.literal: Thereupon they traced Yalian's whereabouts and posted men to guard key points.
translations.idiomatic: They then tracked Yalian's movements and posted troops at the strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 而疏請懷輯罕東諸衛為援，散土魯番黨與孤其勢，遂班師。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to win over and gather the Handong garrisons as support, scatter Turpan's confederates and isolate their strength, and then withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized asking that the Handong garrisons be rallied as allies, that Turpan's confederates be dispersed to isolate their power, and then withdrew the army.

sentences.zh: 錄功，加右副都御史。

translations.literal: Recording merit, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When merits were recorded he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 明年移撫陜西，歷戶部右侍郎，進左。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to grand coordinator of Shaanxi, served as Right Vice Minister of Revenue, then promoted to Left.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Shaanxi, then served as Right Vice Minister of Revenue before being promoted to Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 十三年，火篩大舉犯大同，邊將屢敗。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Huoshai launched a major invasion of Datong; border generals were repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Huoshai launched a major invasion of Datong, and the frontier generals suffered defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 敕進與太監金輔、平江伯陳銳率京軍禦之，無功。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin together with eunuch Jin Fu and the Earl of Pingjiang Chen Rui to lead capital troops against him, without success.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Jin, together with the eunuch Jin Fu and the Earl of Pingjiang Chen Rui, to lead capital troops against the invaders, but they achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 言官劾輔等玩寇，並論進，致仕去。

translations.literal: Censorial officials impeached Fu and others for treating the bandits lightly and also blamed Jin; he resigned and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials impeached Fu and his colleagues for negligence toward the enemy and also held Jin accountable. He resigned and left office.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，乃起為兵部左侍郎，提督團營。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended, [Jin] was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War and placed in charge of the Tuan camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong came to the throne, Jin was recalled as Left Vice Minister of War and put in charge of the Tuan camp.

sentences.zh: 正德元年代劉大夏為尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he replaced Liu Daxia as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he succeeded Liu Daxia as Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 七月應詔陳時政八事，極言內監役京軍，守皇城內侍橫索月錢諸弊，多格不行。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, responding to an imperial edict, he set forth eight points on current governance, speaking at length of abuses such as eunuchs employing capital troops and inner-palace attendants extorting monthly pay while guarding the Forbidden City; most were blocked and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, in response to an imperial edict, he submitted eight proposals on current affairs. He spoke at length against abuses such as eunuchs conscripting capital troops and inner-palace attendants extorting monthly pay while guarding the Forbidden City. Most of his recommendations were blocked and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 又以帝狎比群小，請崇聖學，以古荒淫主為戒，不納。

translations.literal: He also [said] the emperor consorted closely with petty companions, and pleaded to exalt the sage's learning and take ancient dissolute rulers as a warning — not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that because the emperor kept company with low companions, the court should exalt the sage's learning and take ancient dissolute rulers as a warning. The advice was rejected.

sentences.zh: 中官王嶽奏官校王縉等緝事捕盜功，各進一秩。

translations.literal: Eunuch Wang Yue memorialized that official runners Wang Jin and others had merit in investigating and catching bandits; each was promoted one rank.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Yue memorialized that the official runners Wang Jin and others deserved credit for investigating cases and catching bandits, and requested that each be promoted one rank.

sentences.zh: 進言：「邊將出萬死馘一賊，始獲晉級。

translations.literal: Jin said: "Border generals risk death ten thousand times to cut off one bandit's head before they gain promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Jin objected: "A border general must risk death again and again to cut down a single bandit before he earns promotion.

sentences.zh: 此輩乃冒濫得之，孰不解體？」

translations.literal: These men obtained it through shameless abuse — who would not be disheartened to the core?
translations.idiomatic: Yet these men receive it through shameless favoritism. Who would not be utterly disheartened?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「團營軍非為營造設，宜悉令歸伍。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Tuan camp soldiers were not established for construction work; they should all be sent back to their units."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "The Tuan camp was not created for construction work. Its soldiers should all be sent back to their regular units."

sentences.zh: 居兵部半歲，改吏部，明年加太子少保。

translations.literal: After half a year in the Ministry of War he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel; the next year he was appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year in the Ministry of War he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, and the following year was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 進以才見用，能任人，性通敏。

translations.literal: Jin was employed for his talent, able to employ men, and naturally quick and astute.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was valued for his ability, knew how to use men well, and was by nature quick and perceptive.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾弄權，亦多委蛇徇其意，而瑾終不悅。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin manipulated power, [Jin] also often went along and indulged his wishes, but Jin was never pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin seized power, Xu Jin often went along and indulged his wishes, yet Liu Jin was never satisfied with him.

sentences.zh: 方進督團營時，與瑾同事。

translations.literal: When Jin was supervising the Tuan camp, he served alongside Jin.
translations.idiomatic: While Jin was supervising the Tuan camp, he worked alongside Liu Jin.

sentences.zh: 每閱操，談笑指揮，意度閑雅，瑾及諸將鹹服。

translations.literal: Whenever he reviewed drills he commanded with easy talk and laughter, bearing refined and at ease; Liu Jin and all the generals were uniformly impressed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he inspected drills he commanded with easy talk and laughter, his manner calm and polished. Liu Jin and all the generals were deeply impressed.

sentences.zh: 一日操畢，忽呼三校前，各杖數十。

translations.literal: One day when drill ended, he suddenly summoned three sergeants forward and had each beaten several dozen strokes.
translations.idiomatic: One day after drill ended he suddenly summoned three sergeants forward and had each of them beaten several dozen strokes.

sentences.zh: 瑾請其故，進出權貴請托書示之。

translations.literal: Liu Jin asked the reason; Jin produced letters of request from powerful nobles and showed them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin asked why. Jin produced letters from powerful nobles soliciting favors and showed them to him.

sentences.zh: 瑾陽稱善，心不喜。

translations.literal: Liu Jin outwardly praised it but inwardly was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin praised the action to his face but inwardly resented it.

sentences.zh: 至是，欲去進用劉宇代。

translations.literal: At this point he wished to remove Jin and use Liu Yu in his place.
translations.idiomatic: By then he wanted to remove Xu Jin and replace him with Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 焦芳以幹請不得，亦因擠進。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang, because his solicitations were not granted, also therefore pushed Jin out.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang, whose own solicitations had gone unheeded, also joined in driving Jin out.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，南京刑部郎中闕，適無實授員外郎，進循故事以署事主事二人上。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, a vacancy opened for Lang in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments; as there happened to be no directly appointed outer-court secretary, Jin followed precedent and submitted two acting chief clerks to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year a vacancy opened in the Nanjing Ministry of Punishments for a department director. As there happened to be no secretary with a regular appointment available, Jin followed precedent and submitted two acting chief clerks for the post.

sentences.zh: 瑾以為非制，令對狀。

translations.literal: Liu Jin deemed this irregular and ordered them to confront the throne for examination.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin declared the appointment irregular and ordered the men brought before the throne for examination.

sentences.zh: 進不引咎，三降嚴旨譙責。

translations.literal: Jin did not accept blame; three times stern edicts descended rebuking him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin refused to accept blame, and three stern edicts descended rebuking him.

sentences.zh: 不得已請罪，乃令致仕。

translations.literal: Having no choice he pleaded guilt, and was then ordered to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Left with no alternative, he pleaded guilty and was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 未幾，坐用雍泰削其籍。

translations.literal: Before long, for employing Yong Tai, his name was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was struck from the rolls for having employed Yong Tai.

sentences.zh: 二子誥、贊在翰林，俱輸贖調外任。

translations.literal: His two sons Gao and Zan were in the Hanlin Academy; both paid fines and were transferred to outer postings.
translations.idiomatic: His two sons Gao and Zan, both in the Hanlin Academy, paid fines and were transferred to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 尋與劉健等六百七十五人，並追奪誥命。

translations.literal: Soon, together with Liu Jian and six hundred seventy-five others, their patents of honor were all pursued and revoked.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was grouped with Liu Jian and six hundred seventy-five others, and all their patents of honor were revoked.

sentences.zh: 瑾又摘進在大同時籍軍出雇役錢，失勾校，欲籍其家。

translations.literal: Liu Jin again picked out that when Jin was at Datong he requisitioned soldiers' hired-labor money and failed to reconcile accounts, intending to confiscate his household.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin also seized on the fact that while Jin was at Datong he had requisitioned soldiers' hired-labor funds and failed to reconcile the accounts, and sought to confiscate his property.

sentences.zh: 會瑾誅得解，復官致仕。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin was executed he obtained release, was restored to office, and retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin was executed he was cleared, restored to office, and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 未聞命卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: Before the order [of restoration] arrived he died, age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: Before word of his restoration reached him he died, at the age of seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年謚襄毅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jiajing he was given posthumous name Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Jiajing he was given the posthumous name Xiangyi (Assisting and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子誥、贊、詩、詞、論。

translations.literal: Sons: Gao, Zan, Shi, Ci, Lun.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Gao, Zan, Shi, Ci, and Lun.

sentences.zh: 詩，工部郎中。

translations.literal: Shi [served as] Lang in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Shi served as a department director in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 詞，知府。

translations.literal: Ci [served as] prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Ci served as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 誥，字廷綸，進次子也。

translations.literal: Gao, style name Tinglun, was Jin's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Gao, styled Tinglun, was Xu Jin's second son.

sentences.zh: 弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twelfth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Appointed supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a supervising secretary in the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 出視延綏軍儲，論丁糧、丁草之害，帝褒納之。

translations.literal: Sent out to inspect Yan-sui military stores, he discoursed on the harm of ding-grain and ding-forage levies; the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect military stores in Yan-sui, he submitted a memorial on the abuses of the ding-grain and ding-forage levies. The emperor praised his report and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 尋劾監督中官苗逵貪肆罪，進刑科右給事中。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached the supervising eunuch Miao Kui for greed and license; he was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary in the Punishments Section.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he impeached the supervising eunuch Miao Kui for greed and misconduct and was promoted to Right Supervising Secretary in the Punishments Section.

sentences.zh: 正德元年，父進為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde, his father Jin became Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde his father Xu Jin became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 故事，大臣子不得居言職，遂改翰林檢討。

translations.literal: By precedent, sons of grand ministers could not hold remonstrance posts, so he was changed to Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: By established rule, the sons of senior ministers could not hold remonstrance posts, so he was transferred to the post of Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 及進忤劉瑾削籍，並謫誥全州判官。

translations.literal: When Jin offended Liu Jin and was struck from the rolls, Gao was also demoted to magistrate of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jin ran afoul of Liu Jin and was struck from the rolls, Gao was also demoted to magistrate of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父喪歸。

translations.literal: On his father's death, he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 久之，薦起尚寶丞。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was recommended and recalled as Director of Ceremonials in the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was recommended and recalled to serve as Director of Ceremonials in the Directorate of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 復引疾歸，家居授徒講學。

translations.literal: Again citing illness, he returned home and, living in retirement, taught pupils and lectured on learning.
translations.idiomatic: He again pleaded illness and retired, remaining at home to teach students and lecture on the classics.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，起南京通政參議，改侍講學士，直經筵，遷太常卿掌國子監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiajing, he was recalled as Assistant Director of the Office of Transmission at Nanjing, changed to Reader-in-Waiting, attended the Lectures on the Classics, and was transferred to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while directing the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jiajing reign he was recalled as Assistant Director of the Office of Transmission at Nanjing, then made Reader-in-Waiting and assigned to the Lectures on the Classics. He was later promoted to Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and appointed to direct the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 請於太學中建敬一亭，勒禦制《敬一箴註》、程子《四箴》、範浚《心箴》於石。

translations.literal: He requested that a Jingyi Pavilion be built in the Imperial Academy and that the imperially composed Annotated Jingyi Admonition, Cheng Zi's Four Admonitions, and Fan Jun's Heart Admonition be carved in stone.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to build a Jingyi Pavilion in the Imperial Academy and to have carved in stone the imperial Annotated Jingyi Admonition, Cheng Zi's Four Admonitions, and Fan Jun's Heart Admonition.

sentences.zh: 帝悅從之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and approved the request.

sentences.zh: 帝將正文廟祀典，誥請用木主。

translations.literal: When the emperor was about to revise the Confucian temple sacrificial regulations, Gao requested the use of wooden spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor planned to revise the Confucian temple sacrificial rites, Gao petitioned that wooden spirit tablets be used.

sentences.zh: 文華殿東室舊有釋像，帝命撤去。

translations.literal: The east chamber of Wenhua Hall had formerly held a Buddhist image; the emperor ordered it removed.
translations.idiomatic: A Buddhist image had long stood in the east chamber of Wenhua Hall, and the emperor ordered it removed.

sentences.zh: 誥所撰《道統書》言宜崇祀五帝、三王，以周公、孔子配。

translations.literal: In his Treatise on the Transmission of the Way, Gao argued that the Five Emperors and Three Sage Kings should be honored in sacrifice, with the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as associates.
translations.idiomatic: In his Treatise on the Transmission of the Way, Gao argued that the Five Emperors and Three Sage Kings should be honored in sacrifice, with the Duke of Zhou and Confucius as their associates.

sentences.zh: 帝即采用其言。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately adopted his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 十一年擢吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 其冬，拜南京戶部尚書，弟贊亦長戶部。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, while his younger brother Zan also headed the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed Minister of Revenue at Nanjing, while his younger brother Zan headed the Ministry of Revenue in the capital.

sentences.zh: 兄弟並司兩京邦計，縉紳以為榮。

translations.literal: The brothers together managed the finances of the two capitals, and officials regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: With the brothers together overseeing the finances of the two capitals, officials regarded it as a signal honor.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈太子太保，謚莊敏。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously granted the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, with the posthumous name Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 誥官祭酒時，諸生旅櫬不能歸者三十余，皆為葬之，衣食不繼者並周恤。

translations.literal: When Gao served as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, more than thirty students whose coffins could not be returned home were all given burial by him, and those whose food and clothing were insufficient were likewise relieved.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, Gao buried more than thirty students whose families could not afford to transport their coffins home, and he also provided for those who lacked food and clothing.

sentences.zh: 然頗善傅會。

translations.literal: Yet he was rather adept at forced interpretation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was rather given to forced interpretations that flattered the throne.

sentences.zh: 時有白鵲之瑞，誥獻論，司業陳寰獻頌，並宣付史館。

translations.literal: At the time there was an auspicious white magpie; Gao submitted a discourse and Vice-Chancellor Chen Huan submitted a eulogy, both ordered transmitted to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: When an auspicious white magpie appeared, Gao submitted a discourse and Vice-Chancellor Chen Huan submitted a eulogy; both were ordered transmitted to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 給事中張裕、謝存儒，御史馮恩皆劾誥，裕至比之祝欽明。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yu and Xie Cunru and Censor Feng En all impeached Gao; Zhang Yu even compared him to Zhu Qinming.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Zhang Yu and Xie Cunru and Censor Feng En all impeached Gao, and Zhang Yu even compared him to the notorious flatterer Zhu Qinming.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下裕獄，謫福建布政司照磨，存儒亦調邊方。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, imprisoned Zhang Yu, and demoted him to proofreader in the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission; Cunru was also transferred to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged, had Zhang Yu imprisoned, and demoted him to proofreader in the Fujian Provincial Administration Commission; Cunru was also transferred to a frontier post.

sentences.zh: 恩詆誥學術迂邪，誥求罷。

translations.literal: Feng En denounced Gao's learning as pedantic and perverse, and Gao requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Feng En denounced Gao's scholarship as pedantic and perverse, and Gao asked to be dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「恩所詆乃指前日去土偶用木主事也。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What En denounces refers to the earlier matter of removing clay figures and using wooden spirit tablets.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "What Feng denounces refers to the earlier matter of replacing clay figures with wooden spirit tablets.

sentences.zh: 爾以是介意邪？」

translations.literal: Do you take offense at that?
translations.idiomatic: Are you taking offense at that?"

sentences.zh: 其為帝眷寵如此。

translations.literal: Such was the imperial favor he enjoyed.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the favor he enjoyed at court.

sentences.zh: 讃，字廷美，進第三子也。

translations.literal: Zan, style name Tingmei, was Jin's third son.
translations.idiomatic: Zan, styled Tingmei, was Xu Jin's third son.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the ninth year of Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 授大名推官。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating censor of Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Daming.

sentences.zh: 亦以辨疑獄知名，召拜御史。

translations.literal: He also became known for resolving doubtful cases and was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: He also became known for resolving doubtful legal cases and was summoned to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 正德元年改編修。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was changed to Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was transferred to the post of Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾逐進，讃亦出為臨淄知縣。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin drove out Xu Jin, Zan was also sent out as magistrate of Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin drove Xu Jin from office, Zan was also sent out to serve as magistrate of Linzi.

sentences.zh: 累遷浙江左布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Left Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年入為光祿卿，歷刑部左、右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing he entered the capital as Minister of Imperial Entertainments and served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing he entered the capital as Minister of Imperial Entertainments and later served as Left and Right Vice Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 知州金輅謫戍，賂武定侯郭勛。

translations.literal: Prefect Jin Luo, banished to military service, bribed the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Jin Luo, banished to frontier military service, bribed the Marquis of Wuding, Guo Xun.

sentences.zh: 勛遣人篡取之，指揮王臣不與。

translations.literal: Xun sent men to seize it by force; Commander Wang Chen would not yield it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun sent men to seize the bribe by force, but Commander Wang Chen refused to hand it over.

sentences.zh: 縛臣以歸，掠取其賄。

translations.literal: They bound Chen and took him away, plundering the bribe.
translations.idiomatic: They bound Wang Chen and took him away, seizing the bribe in the process.

sentences.zh: 事覺，讃等請論如律。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Zan and others requested judgment according to law.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair came to light, Zan and the others requested that the case be judged according to law.

sentences.zh: 帝憐勛，諭法司毋刑輅等，輅等遂不承。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied Xun and instructed the judicial offices not to torture Jin Luo and the others, whereupon they refused to confess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on Guo Xun and instructed the judicial offices not to apply torture to Jin Luo and the others, whereupon they refused to confess.

sentences.zh: 尚書高友璣在告，坐畏縮，被劾去。

translations.literal: Minister Gao Youji was on leave and, charged with timidity, was impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Gao Youji was on leave at the time and, charged with timidity in the case, was impeached and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 讃請如常訊，具得勛納賄狀，乃再奪其祿。

translations.literal: Zan requested routine interrogation, fully established Xun's receipt of the bribe, and only then was his stipend again confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Zan requested routine interrogation, fully established Guo Xun's acceptance of the bribe, and only then was his stipend confiscated again.

sentences.zh: 八年，進尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to minister.

sentences.zh: 詔許六部歷事監生發廷臣奸弊。

translations.literal: An edict permitted students serving rotations in the Six Ministries to expose the misconduct of court officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict permitted students serving rotations in the Six Ministries to expose the misconduct of court officials.

sentences.zh: 有詹摐者，訐吏部侍郎徐縉，下都御史汪鋐訊。

translations.literal: There was one Zhan Cong, who denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jin; the case was sent down to Censor-in-Chief Wang Yao for investigation.
translations.idiomatic: One Zhan Cong denounced Vice Minister of Personnel Xu Jin, and the case was referred to Censor-in-Chief Wang Yao for investigation.

sentences.zh: 摐語塞，已論罪，摐復訐縉及通政陳經等。

translations.literal: Cong was speechless; he had already been judged guilty, yet Cong again denounced Xu Jin and Assistant Director of Transmission Chen Jing and others.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan Cong was left speechless under questioning and had already been found guilty, yet he again denounced Xu Jin, Assistant Director of Transmission Chen Jing, and others.

sentences.zh: 再下鋐訊，鋐力斥其妄。

translations.literal: The case was again sent down to Wang Yao for investigation, and Yao forcefully rejected his charges as false.
translations.idiomatic: The case was again referred to Wang Yao for investigation, and Wang forcefully rejected the charges as false.

sentences.zh: 會太常卿彭澤欲傾縉代之，偽為縉書抵張孚敬求解，復惎孚敬劾縉賄己。

translations.literal: Meanwhile Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Peng Ze wished to overthrow Xu Jin and replace him; he forged a letter in Xu's name to Zhang Fuxing seeking exoneration, then incited Fuxing to impeach Xu for bribing him.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Peng Ze wished to bring down Xu Jin and take his place. He forged a letter in Xu's name to Zhang Fuxing seeking exoneration, then incited Fuxing to impeach Xu for having bribed him.

sentences.zh: 縉疏辨，詔法司會錦衣衛訊。

translations.literal: Xu Jin submitted a memorial in his defense; an edict ordered the judicial offices jointly with the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jin submitted a memorial in his own defense, and an edict ordered the judicial offices to investigate jointly with the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 讃等卒論摐誣罔，而縉行賄事莫能白，坐除名。

translations.literal: Zan and the others finally judged Cong guilty of false accusation, but Xu's bribery could not be cleared, and he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Zan and the others finally found Zhan Cong guilty of false accusation, but Xu Jin's alleged bribery could not be cleared, and he was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 帝方嘉摐能奉詔言事，竟宥摐罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was then praising Cong for obeying the edict and speaking out, and in the end pardoned Cong's offense.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then praising Zhan Cong for obeying the edict and speaking out, and in the end pardoned his offense.

sentences.zh: 於是無賴子率持朝士陰事，索資財，妄構事端入奏，諸司為惕息。

translations.literal: Thereupon riffraff generally seized on officials' private affairs, demanded money, and recklessly fabricated cases for memorials; the various offices trembled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon riffraff of every sort seized on officials' private affairs, demanded money, and recklessly fabricated charges for memorials to the throne, and the various offices trembled in fear.

sentences.zh: 軍人童源訐中官張永造塋，犯天壽山龍脈，復嗾永弟容仆王謙等發容違法事。

translations.literal: The soldier Tong Yuan denounced the eunuch Zhang Yong for building a tomb that violated the geomantic line of Tianshou Mountain, and further incited Yong's younger brother Rong's servant Wang Qian and others to expose Rong's illegal acts.
translations.idiomatic: The soldier Tong Yuan denounced the eunuch Zhang Yong for building a tomb that violated the geomantic line of Tianshou Mountain, and further incited Yong's younger brother Rong's servant Wang Qian and others to expose Rong's illegal conduct.

sentences.zh: 奸人張雄又為謙草奏，詆讃與兄誥及汪鋐、廖道南、史道，內臣黃錦輩數十人受容重賂，源亦上疏助之。

translations.literal: The scoundrel Zhang Xiong also drafted a memorial for Qian, denouncing Zan, his elder brother Gao, Wang Yao, Liao Daonan, Shi Dao, and dozens of inner-court officials such as Huang Jin for receiving heavy bribes from Rong; Tong Yuan also submitted a memorial in support.
translations.idiomatic: The scoundrel Zhang Xiong also drafted a memorial for Wang Qian, denouncing Zan, his elder brother Gao, Wang Yao, Liao Daonan, Shi Dao, and dozens of inner-court officials including Huang Jin for receiving heavy bribes from Rong; Tong Yuan also submitted a supporting memorial.

sentences.zh: 鞫得實，源等並戍極邊，告訐始少衰。

translations.literal: On investigation the facts were established; Tong Yuan and the others were all banished to the farthest frontier, and malicious denunciations only then began to decline.
translations.idiomatic: On investigation the false charges were exposed; Tong Yuan and the others were all banished to the farthest frontier, and malicious denunciations only then began to subside.

sentences.zh: 十年，改讃戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Zan was changed to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Zan was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 馳驛歸省母。

translations.literal: He traveled by courier relay to return and visit his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He traveled by courier relay to return home and visit his mother.

sentences.zh: 母先卒。

translations.literal: His mother had already died.
translations.idiomatic: His mother had already died.

sentences.zh: 服未闋，詔以為吏部尚書，服除始入朝。

translations.literal: Before mourning was complete, an edict appointed him Minister of Personnel; he entered court only after mourning ended.
translations.idiomatic: Before his mourning period was complete, an edict appointed him Minister of Personnel; he entered court only after mourning ended.

sentences.zh: 帝以讃醇謹，虛位待。

translations.literal: The emperor, considering Zan upright and careful, kept the post vacant awaiting him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, considering Zan upright and careful, kept the post vacant awaiting his arrival.

sentences.zh: 及至，論列不當意。

translations.literal: When he arrived, his recommendations did not please the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When he finally arrived, his recommendations did not please the emperor.

sentences.zh: 詔選宮僚，閣臣多引私黨，言官劾罷十余人，帝以屬吏部。

translations.literal: An edict called for selection of palace staff; grand secretaries mostly recommended their private factions, and remonstrance officials impeached and removed more than ten; the emperor entrusted the matter to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called for the selection of palace staff. The grand secretaries mostly recommended their private factions, and remonstrance officials impeached and removed more than ten of them; the emperor entrusted the matter to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 讃乃舉霍韜、毛伯溫、顧璘、呂柟、鄒守益、徐階、任瀚、薛蕙、周鈇、趙時春等，詔璘、柟、蕙仍故官，余俱用之。

translations.literal: Zan then recommended Huo Tao, Mao Bowen, Gu Lin, Lü Shan, Zou Shouyi, Xu Jie, Ren Han, Xue Hui, Zhou Fu, Zhao Shichun, and others; an edict ordered Lin, Shan, and Hui to remain in their former posts, and the rest were all appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Zan then recommended Huo Tao, Mao Bowen, Gu Lin, Lü Shan, Zou Shouyi, Xu Jie, Ren Han, Xue Hui, Zhou Fu, Zhao Shichun, and others. An edict ordered Gu Lin, Lü Shan, and Xue Hui to remain in their former posts, and the rest were all appointed.

sentences.zh: 屢加少保兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly given the additional titles of Junior Guardian and Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九廟災，自陳免。

translations.literal: When the Nine Temples burned, he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When fire destroyed the Nine Temples, he submitted a memorial requesting dismissal from office.

sentences.zh: 居半歲，帝難其代，復起讃任之。

translations.literal: After half a year the emperor found no suitable replacement and recalled Zan to the post.
translations.idiomatic: After half a year the emperor found no suitable replacement and recalled Zan to the post.

sentences.zh: 請發內帑，借百官俸，括富民財，開鬻爵之令，以濟邊需。

translations.literal: He requested disbursement from the inner treasury, borrowing officials' salaries, seizing the wealth of rich households, and opening an order for the sale of ranks to meet frontier needs.
translations.idiomatic: He requested disbursement from the inner treasury, borrowing officials' salaries, seizing the wealth of rich households, and opening an order for the sale of ranks to meet frontier needs.

sentences.zh: 時議內地築墩堡，讃謂非計。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of building blockhouses in the interior; Zan said it was not a good plan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was discussion of building blockhouses in the interior, and Zan argued that it was not a sound plan.

sentences.zh: 帝以借俸、括財非盛世事，已之。

translations.literal: The emperor held that borrowing salaries and seizing wealth were not measures for an age of prosperity, and dropped them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that borrowing salaries and seizing private wealth were not measures fit for an age of prosperity, and dropped them.

sentences.zh: 墩堡議亦寢。

translations.literal: The blockhouse proposal also lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The blockhouse proposal also lapsed.

sentences.zh: 翟鑾、嚴嵩柄政，多所請托。

translations.literal: Zhai Luan and Yan Song held power and made many requests and recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Luan and Yan Song held power and made many requests and recommendations on others' behalf.

sentences.zh: 郎中王與齡勸讃發之。

translations.literal: Director Wang Yuling urged Zan to expose them.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Yuling urged Zan to expose them.

sentences.zh: 嵩辨之強，帝眷嵩，反切責讃，除與齡籍。

translations.literal: Song defended himself forcefully; the emperor favored Song and instead sharply rebuked Zan, striking Yuling from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song defended himself forcefully. The emperor favored Song and instead sharply rebuked Zan, striking Wang Yuling from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 讃自是懾嵩不敢抗，亦頗以賄聞矣。

translations.literal: From then on Zan feared Song and did not dare resist; he also became rather known for bribery.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Zan feared Yan Song and did not dare resist him, and he also became rather known for accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 鑾罷，帝謀代者。

translations.literal: When Luan was dismissed, the emperor planned for a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhai Luan was dismissed, the emperor planned for a replacement.

sentences.zh: 嵩以讃柔和易制，引之。

translations.literal: Song, considering Zan mild and easy to control, recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song, considering Zan mild and easy to control, recommended him.

sentences.zh: 詔以本官兼文淵閣大學士參預機務。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him in his existing post concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion to participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him in his existing post concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion to participate in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 政事一決於嵩，讃無所可否。

translations.literal: All government affairs were decided by Song alone; Zan neither approved nor disapproved.
translations.idiomatic: All government affairs were decided by Yan Song alone; Zan neither approved nor disapproved.

sentences.zh: 久之加少傅。

translations.literal: After a long while he was given the additional title of Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was given the additional title of Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 以年逾七十，數乞休。

translations.literal: As he passed seventy, he repeatedly requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: As he passed seventy, he repeatedly requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 帝責其忘君愛身，落職閑住。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked him for forgetting his lord and cherishing his person, stripped him of office, and allowed him to live in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked him for forgetting his sovereign and cherishing his own safety, stripped him of office, and allowed him to live in retirement.

sentences.zh: 歸三年卒。

translations.literal: After three years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after returning home he died.

sentences.zh: 後復官，贈少師，謚文簡。

translations.literal: Later his office was restored; he was posthumously granted Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Later his office was restored posthumously; he was granted the title Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous name Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 論，字廷議，進少子也。

translations.literal: Lun, style name Tingyi, was Jin's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Lun, styled Tingyi, was Xu Jin's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the fifth year of Jiajing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 授順德推官，入為兵部主事，改禮部。

translations.literal: Appointed investigating censor of Shunde, he entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War and was changed to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor of Shunde, then entered the capital as a secretary in the Ministry of War before being transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 好談兵，幼從父歷邊境，盡知厄塞險易，因著《九邊圖論》上之。

translations.literal: He loved to discuss military affairs; from youth he had followed his father along the borders and knew thoroughly the strategic passes and their difficulties and advantages, and therefore composed and submitted his Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to discuss military affairs. From youth he had followed his father along the borders and knew thoroughly the strategic passes and their difficulties and advantages, and therefore composed and submitted his Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，頒邊臣議行，自是以知兵聞。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased, ordered it distributed to frontier officials for discussion and implementation, and from then on he became known for military knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased, ordered it distributed to frontier officials for discussion and implementation, and from then on Lun became known for his military expertise.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京大理寺丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Vice Director of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 會廷推順天巡撫，論名列第二。

translations.literal: When the court recommended candidates for Censor-in-Chief of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.
translations.idiomatic: When the court recommended candidates for Censor-in-Chief of Shuntian, Lun's name ranked second.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「是上《九邊圖論》者」，即拜右僉都御史，任之。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "That is the one who submitted the Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated," and immediately appointed him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and assigned him the post.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "That is the one who submitted the Treatise on the Nine Border Regions Illustrated," and immediately appointed him Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and assigned him the post.

sentences.zh: 白通事以千余騎犯黃崖口，論督將士敗之。

translations.literal: Bai Tongshi invaded Huangyakou with more than a thousand horsemen; Lun directed the officers and soldiers and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Tongshi invaded Huangyakou Pass with more than a thousand horsemen; Lun directed the officers and soldiers and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 再犯大木谷，復為官軍所卻。

translations.literal: He invaded again at Damugu Valley and was again repulsed by government troops.
translations.idiomatic: He invaded again at Damugu Valley and was again repulsed by government troops.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進右副都御史。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以病免。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was dismissed on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 俺答薄都城，起故官撫山西。

translations.literal: When Altan pressed close to the capital, he was recalled to his former post to govern Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When Altan Khan pressed close to the capital, Lun was recalled to his former post to serve as governor of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 錄防秋功，進兵部右侍郎，召理京營戎政。

translations.literal: His merit in autumn defense was recorded; he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and summoned to administer the military affairs of the capital garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in the autumn defense was recorded; he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of War and summoned to administer the military affairs of the capital garrisons.

sentences.zh: 以築京師外城轉左。

translations.literal: For building the outer wall of the capital he was transferred to the left post.
translations.idiomatic: For supervising construction of the outer wall of the capital he was transferred to Left Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 三十三年出督宣、大、山西軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he went out to supervise military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year he went out to supervise military affairs in Xuanfu, Datong, and Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 奸人呂鶴初與邱富以左道惑眾。

translations.literal: The scoundrels Lu He and Qiu Fu at first deluded the people with heterodox doctrines.
translations.idiomatic: The scoundrels Lu He and Qiu Fu at first deluded the people with heterodox doctrines.

sentences.zh: 富叛降俺答，為之謀主。

translations.literal: Fu defected and surrendered to Altan, becoming his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu defected and surrendered to Altan Khan, becoming his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 鶴遣其黨闌出塞外，引寇入犯，為偵卒所獲。

translations.literal: He sent his followers to slip out beyond the frontier and lead raiders in invasion; they were captured by scouts.
translations.idiomatic: Lu He sent his followers to slip out beyond the frontier and lead raiders in an invasion, but they were captured by scouts.

sentences.zh: 論遣兵捕鶴，並誅其黨。

translations.literal: Lun sent troops to capture He and executed his followers as well.
translations.idiomatic: Lun sent troops to capture Lu He and executed his followers as well.

sentences.zh: 以功進右都御史，再以功進兵部尚書，蔭子錦衣世千戶。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, and again for merit to Minister of War; his son was granted hereditary battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, and again for merit to Minister of War; his son was granted hereditary battalion commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 翁萬達為總督，築大同邊墻六百里，裏建一墩臺於墻內。

translations.literal: Weng Wanda served as governor-general; he built six hundred li of Datong border wall, building one beacon tower every li inside the wall.
translations.idiomatic: When Weng Wanda was governor-general, he built six hundred li of border wall at Datong, placing a beacon tower every li on the inside of the wall.

sentences.zh: 後以兵少墻不能守，盡撤而守臺。

translations.literal: Later because troops were few the wall could not be guarded; they withdrew completely and guarded the towers.
translations.idiomatic: Later, with too few troops to hold the wall, they abandoned it entirely and manned only the towers.

sentences.zh: 論言：「兵既守臺，則寇攻墻不得用其力。

translations.literal: Lun said: "Since the troops already guard the towers, when bandits attack the wall they cannot use their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Lun argued: "With the troops holding the towers, raiders assaulting the wall cannot bring their full strength to bear.

sentences.zh: 及寇入墻，率震駭逃散。

translations.literal: And when bandits enter the wall, they are mostly shocked and terrified and flee scattering.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when raiders breach the wall, the garrison panics and scatters.

sentences.zh: 請改築於墻外，每三百步建一臺，俾矢石相及。

translations.literal: I request rebuilding outside the wall, every three hundred paces building one tower, so that arrows and stones can reach each other.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that towers be built outside the wall, one every three hundred paces, so their arrow and stone shot could cover one another.

sentences.zh: 去墻不得越三十步，高廣方四丈五尺，其顛損三之一，上置女墻、營舍，守以壯士十人。

translations.literal: Distance from the wall must not exceed thirty paces; height and breadth each four zhang five chi; the top reduced by one-third; on top place battlements and barracks, guarded by ten stalwart men.
translations.idiomatic: They were to stand no more than thirty paces from the wall, measure four zhang five chi square in height and breadth, with the top third cut down; battlements and barracks were to be set on top, each defended by ten picked soldiers.

sentences.zh: 下築月城，穴門通出入。

translations.literal: Below build a crescent moon fort, with a tunnel gate for passage in and out.
translations.idiomatic: Below each was to be a semicircular outwork with a tunnel gate for access.

sentences.zh: 度工費不過九萬金，數月而足。」

translations.literal: Estimated labor costs would not exceed ninety thousand in gold; sufficient in several months."
translations.idiomatic: The project was estimated at no more than ninety thousand taels and could be finished in a few months."

sentences.zh: 詔立從之。

translations.literal: An edict immediately ordered compliance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved the proposal at once.

sentences.zh: 寇萬騎犯山西，論督軍遮破之朔州川。

translations.literal: Bandits ten thousand horsemen invaded Shanxi; Lun supervised the army, intercepted and defeated them at Shuozhou River.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders ten thousand strong invaded Shanxi; Lun commanded the army and routed them at the Shuozhou River.

sentences.zh: 其犯宣府、龍門者，亦為將士所敗，先後俘斬五百三十有奇。

translations.literal: Those who invaded Xuanfu and Longmen were also defeated by officers and soldiers; in succession captives killed five hundred thirty odd.
translations.idiomatic: Those who raided Xuanfu and Longmen were likewise beaten by his troops; in all, more than five hundred thirty were captured or slain.

sentences.zh: 加太子太保，蔭子如初。

translations.literal: Added Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; ennobled his son as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and his son received the same hereditary privilege as before.

sentences.zh: 三十五年，兵部尚書楊博以父喪去，召論代之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year Minister of War Yang Bo left on father's mourning; Lun was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fifth year Yang Bo, Minister of War, left office to observe mourning for his father, and Lun was summoned to replace him.

sentences.zh: 當是時，嚴嵩父子用事，將帥率以賄進。

translations.literal: At that time Yan Song father and son wielded power; commanders-in-chief generally advanced through bribery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan Song and his son were in power, and frontier generals generally bought their promotions with bribes.

sentences.zh: 南北用兵，帝責中樞甚急。

translations.literal: North and south used troops; the emperor blamed the central command urgently.
translations.idiomatic: With war on both northern and southern fronts, the emperor pressed the central military command relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 丁汝夔、王邦瑞、趙錦、聶豹，鹹不得善去。

translations.literal: Ding Ruai, Wang Bangrui, Zhao Jin, and Nie Bao—all did not leave their posts well.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Ruai, Wang Bangrui, Zhao Jin, and Nie Bao all left their posts in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 論時已老，重自顧念。

translations.literal: Lun was already old and reflected heavily on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lun was by then old and deeply uneasy in the post.

sentences.zh: 一切將帥黜陟，兵機進止，悉聽世蕃指揮，望由此損。

translations.literal: All appointment and dismissal of generals, military plans advance and halt, entirely listened to Shifan's direction; his standing thereby was damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Every promotion or dismissal of generals and every military move had to follow Shifan's orders, and Lun's standing suffered accordingly.

sentences.zh: 俺答子辛愛憤總督楊順納其逃妾，擁眾圍大同右衛城數重，城中析屋而爨。

translations.literal: Altan's son Xin'ai, angry that Governor Yang Shun took in his escaped concubine, led masses to surround Datong Right Guard city in many layers; in the city they split houses to cook.
translations.idiomatic: Altan's son Xin'ai, furious that Governor Yang Shun had accepted his runaway concubine, led a large force to besiege Datong Right Guard in successive rings; inside the city people tore down houses for fuel.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，深以為憂，密問嵩。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and was deeply worried; he secretly asked Song.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he was deeply alarmed and secretly consulted Yan Song.

sentences.zh: 嵩意欲棄之而難於發言，則請降諭問本兵。

translations.literal: Song wished to abandon it but found it hard to speak; then he requested an edict lowering the question to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Song wanted to abandon the city but could not bring himself to say so; instead he asked that an edict be issued directing the question to the Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 論請復右衛軍馬，歲辦五十萬金，故為難詞，冀以動帝。

translations.literal: Lun requested restoring Right Guard military horses and yearly providing five hundred thousand in gold, deliberately using difficult words, hoping to move the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Lun asked that the Right Guard's war-horses be restored and that five hundred thousand taels be allocated annually—deliberately making the demand sound harsh in hopes of stirring the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝顧亟措餉發兵，易置文武將吏，右衛圍亦尋解。

translations.literal: The emperor instead hurried to raise funds and send troops, replaced civil and military officers; the Right Guard siege also soon was relieved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instead rushed to raise supplies and dispatch troops, replaced the civil and military commanders, and the siege of the Right Guard was soon lifted.

sentences.zh: 給事中吳時來劾楊順，因言論雷同附和，日昏酣，置邊警度外。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Wu Shilai impeached Yang Shun, also saying Lun echoed agreement, daily drunken stupor, placed border alarms outside concern.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Wu Shilai impeached Yang Shun and charged that Lun echoed him in slavish agreement, spent his days in drunken stupor, and treated frontier alerts as beneath notice.

sentences.zh: 帝遂削論籍。

translations.literal: The emperor then stripped Lun's registration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon struck Lun from the roster of officials.

sentences.zh: 嵩微為之解，亦不能救也。

translations.literal: Song slightly interceded for him but also could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Song offered a mild plea on his behalf but could not save him.

sentences.zh: 三十八年復起故官，督薊、遼、保定軍務。

translations.literal: In the thirty-eighth year he was restored to his former office and supervised military affairs in Ji, Liao, and Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-eighth year he was restored to his former office and put in charge of military affairs in Ji, Liaodong, and Baoding.

sentences.zh: 把都兒犯薊西，論厚集精銳以待。

translations.literal: Badu'er invaded western Ji; Lun heavily gathered elite troops to await.
translations.idiomatic: Badu'er raided western Ji; Lun massed picked troops to meet him.

sentences.zh: 至則為遊擊胡鎮所破。

translations.literal: When he arrived he was broken by guerrilla officer Hu Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders came they were defeated by guerrilla commander Hu Zhen.

sentences.zh: 分掠沙兒嶺、燕子窩，又卻，乃遁去。

translations.literal: Dividing to plunder Sha'er Ridge and Swallow Nest, again repulsed, then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: They split off to plunder Sha'er Ridge and Swallow Nest but were driven back again and then fled.

sentences.zh: 事聞，厚賫銀幣。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, he was generously rewarded with silver and coins.
translations.idiomatic: When the victory was reported, he was generously rewarded with silver and silks.

sentences.zh: 尋又奏密雲、昌平二鎮防秋，須餉銀三十余萬。

translations.literal: Soon again memorialized that Miyun and Changping two garrisons' autumn defense needed more than three hundred thousand in silver provisions.
