translations.idiomatic: He soon memorialized that the Miyun and Changping garrisons needed more than three hundred thousand taels for autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄭茂言論奏請過多，請察其侵冒弊，詔論回籍聽勘。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zheng Mao said Lun's memorial requests were too many; please investigate his embezzlement malpractices; an edict ordered Lun to return home and await investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zheng Mao charged that Lun's requests were excessive and asked that his corrupt practices be examined; Lun was ordered home pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄧棟往核，具得虛冒狀，奪官閑住。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Deng Dong went to verify and fully obtained false claims; his office was stripped and he lived in idleness.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Deng Dong went to audit the accounts, found clear evidence of fraud, and Lun was dismissed and relegated to private life.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Before long he died, age seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he died, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，復官，謚恭襄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing his office was restored; posthumous title Gongxiang.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign his offices were restored and he was given the posthumous title Gongxiang (Respectful Assistant).

sentences.zh: 曾孫浩然，由世蔭歷官太子太保，左都督。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Haoran, through hereditary privilege rose in office to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandson Haoran rose through hereditary privilege to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Left Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 浩然子達胤，錦衣指揮。

translations.literal: Haoran's son Dayin was an Embroidered Uniform Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: Haoran's son Dayin was a commander in the Embroidered Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷京師，不屈死。

translations.literal: Li Zicheng seized the capital; he did not submit and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took Beijing, Dayin refused to submit and died.

sentences.zh: 其從兄佳胤，弘農衛指揮。

translations.literal: His cousin Jiaoyin was commander of Hongnong Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Jiaoyin served as commander of Hongnong Guard.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十四年賊破靈寶，持刀赴鬥，死焉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen bandits broke Lingbao; he took a blade and went to fight and died there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chongzhen, when rebels took Lingbao, he seized a blade and rushed into battle and died there.

sentences.zh: 雍泰，字世隆，鹹寧人。

translations.literal: Yong Tai, style Shilong, a native of Xianning.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Tai, courtesy name Shilong, was a native of Xianning.

sentences.zh: 成化五年進士。

translations.literal: Advanced scholar in the fifth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the imperial examinations in the fifth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除吳縣知縣。

translations.literal: Removed to magistrate of Wu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Wu County.

sentences.zh: 太湖漲，沒田千頃，泰作堤為民利，稱「雍公堤」。

translations.literal: Tai Lake rose and submerged fields a thousand qing; Tai built a dike for the people's benefit, called "Duke Yong's Dike."
translations.idiomatic: When Tai Lake flooded and drowned a thousand qing of fields, Tai built a dike for the people's benefit, known as "Duke Yong's Dike."

sentences.zh: 民妾亡去，妾父訟其夫密殺女匿屍湖石下。

translations.literal: A commoner's concubine ran away; the concubine's father sued her husband for secretly killing the daughter and hiding the corpse under lake rocks.
translations.idiomatic: When a man's concubine absconded, her father sued the husband, claiming he had murdered her in secret and hidden the body beneath rocks by the lake.

sentences.zh: 泰詰曰：「彼密殺汝女，汝何以知匿所。

translations.literal: Tai questioned, saying: "If he secretly killed your daughter, how do you know the hiding place?
translations.idiomatic: Tai interrogated him: "If he secretly killed your daughter, how would you know where the body was hidden?

sentences.zh: 且此非兩月屍，必汝殺他人女，冀得賂耳。」

translations.literal: Moreover this is not a two-month corpse; surely you killed another person's daughter, hoping to obtain bribe money."
translations.idiomatic: And this corpse is not two months old—you must have killed someone else's daughter, hoping to extort a payoff."

sentences.zh: 一考而服。

translations.literal: One examination and he submitted.
translations.idiomatic: A single round of questioning and the father confessed.

sentences.zh: 召為御史，巡鹽兩淮。

translations.literal: Summoned as censor to tour salt of the two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as investigating censor to inspect the salt administration of the two Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 竈丁無妻者，泰為婚匹。

translations.literal: Salt workers without wives—Tai matched them in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: For salt workers who had no wives, Tai arranged marriages.

sentences.zh: 出知鳳陽府。

translations.literal: Went out as prefect of Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: He left the capital to serve as prefect of Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 父憂去，服闋起知南陽。

translations.literal: Father mourning left; when mourning ended rose as prefect of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He left office for his father's mourning; when the mourning period ended he was appointed prefect of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 余子俊督師，薦為大同兵備副使，擢山西按察使。

translations.literal: Yu Zijun supervised the army, recommended him as Datong military preparedness vice commissioner, promoted to Shanxi surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu Zijun supervised the army, Tai was recommended as Datong vice commissioner for military preparedness and was promoted to Shanxi surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 泰剛廉，所至好搏擊豪強。

translations.literal: Tai was upright and incorruptible; wherever he went he liked to strike down powerful bullies.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was stern and incorrupt; wherever he served he took pleasure in crushing powerful wrongdoers.

sentences.zh: 太原知府尹珍塗遇弗及避，泰召至，跽而數之。

translations.literal: Taiyuan Prefect Yin Zhen on the road encountered him and did not yield in time; Tai summoned him, made him kneel, and counted his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Taiyuan Prefect Yin Zhen failed to give way promptly when they met on the road; Tai summoned him, made him kneel, and rebuked him to his face.

sentences.zh: 珍不服，泰竟笞珍。

translations.literal: Zhen did not submit; Tai ultimately flogged Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin refused to accept this; Tai had him caned anyway.

sentences.zh: 珍訴於朝，且告泰非罪杖人死，逮下詔獄。

translations.literal: Zhen appealed to the court and also reported that Tai beat a man to death without cause; he was arrested and sent down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: Yin appealed to the court and accused Tai of killing a man by improper beating; Tai was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 王恕請寬泰罪，會事經赦，乃降湖廣參議。

translations.literal: Wang Shu requested leniency for Tai's crime; the matter coincided with amnesty, and he was demoted to Huguang participant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shu asked that Tai's punishment be lightened; as the matter coincided with a general amnesty, he was demoted to participant in Huguang.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年轉浙江右布政使，復以母憂去。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongzhi transferred to Zhejiang Right Administering Commissioner; again left on mother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongzhi he was transferred to Right Administering Commissioner of Zhejiang, then left again for his mother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 十二年起右副都御史，巡撫宣府。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governed Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 官馬死，軍士不能償，泰言於朝，以官帑市。

translations.literal: Official horses died; soldiers could not repay; Tai spoke to the court to use the official treasury to buy.
translations.idiomatic: When government horses died, the troops could not afford replacements; Tai petitioned the court to purchase them from the public treasury.

sentences.zh: 邊軍貧，有妻者輒鬻，泰請官為資給。

translations.literal: Frontier soldiers were poor; those with wives often sold them; Tai requested officials provide funds.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops were so poor that married men often sold their wives; Tai asked that the government provide funds.

sentences.zh: 尚書周經因令貧者給聘財，典賣者收贖，軍盡歡。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jing therefore ordered the poor given betrothal money and pawned wives redeemed; the army entirely rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jing followed through: the poor were given betrothal funds and redeemed wives were restored, and the troops were overjoyed.

sentences.zh: 參將王傑有罪，泰劾之，下泰逮問。

translations.literal: Deputy commander Wang Jie had a crime; Tai impeached him; Tai was sent down for arrest and questioning.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commander Wang Jie had committed an offense; Tai impeached him and was himself ordered down for questioning.

sentences.zh: 泰又請按千戶八人，帝以泰屢抑武臣，方詔都察院行勘。

translations.literal: Tai again requested investigating eight battalion commanders; the emperor, because Tai repeatedly suppressed military officials, had just issued an edict the Censorate to conduct investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Tai also asked to investigate eight battalion commanders; the emperor, seeing that Tai repeatedly humbled military officers, had just ordered the Censorate to investigate.

sentences.zh: 而參將李稽坐事畏泰重劾，乞受杖，泰取大杖決之。

translations.literal: But Deputy Commander Li Ji sat in a matter, feared Tai's heavy impeachment, begged to receive flogging; Tai took a large staff and decided it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Deputy Commander Li Ji, embroiled in a case and fearing Tai's harsh impeachment, asked to accept beating; Tai took up a heavy rod and thrashed him.

sentences.zh: 稽乃奏泰淩虐，帝遣給事中徐仁偕錦衣千戶往按。

translations.literal: Ji then memorialized that Tai bullied; the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Xu Ren with an Embroidered Uniform Guard thousand-household to investigate on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Li then memorialized that Tai was brutal; the emperor sent Supervising Secretary Xu Ren with a thousand-household of the Embroidered Uniform Guard to investigate on the spot.

sentences.zh: 傑復使人走登聞鼓下，訟泰妄逮將校至八十六人，並及其婿納賂事。

translations.literal: Jie again sent a man to run below the Denunciation Drum, suing Tai for false arrest of officers to eighty-six people, together with his son-in-law's bribery matter.
translations.idiomatic: Jie also sent agents to beat the Denunciation Drum, accusing Tai of wrongful arrests of eighty-six officers and alleging bribery by his son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 法司核上，褫為民。

translations.literal: The judicial offices verified and submitted; he was stripped to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: The judicial offices reviewed the case and submitted their findings; Tai was degraded to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，給事中潘鐸等薦泰有敢死之節，克亂之才。

translations.literal: When Wuzong was established, Supervising Secretaries Pan Duo and others recommended that Tai had integrity of daring death and talent to quell disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When the Wuzong emperor came to the throne, Supervising Secretaries Pan Duo and others recommended Tai for his fearless integrity and talent for putting down disorder.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書馬文升遂起泰南京右副都御史，提督操江，固辭不赴。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng then raised Tai to Nanjing Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise Yangtze training; he firmly declined and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Ma Wensheng thereupon recalled Tai as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief at Nanjing to supervise the Yangtze fleet; Tai firmly declined and did not take up the post.

sentences.zh: 正德三年春，許進為吏部，復起前官。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year of Zhengde Xu Jin became Minister of Personnel and again raised him to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Zhengde Xu Jin became Minister of Personnel and restored Tai to his former post.

sentences.zh: 七月擢南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh month promoted to Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was promoted to Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾，泰鄉人也，怒泰不與通，甫四日即令致仕。

translations.literal: Liu Jin was Tai's fellow townsman; angry that Tai would not communicate with him, after only four days he ordered retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin was Tai's fellow townsman and resented Tai for refusing to deal with him; after only four days in office Tai was ordered to retire.

sentences.zh: 謂進私泰，遂削二人籍，而追斥馬文升及前薦泰者尚書劉大夏、給事中趙士賢、御史張津等為民，其他罰米輸邊者又五十余人。

translations.literal: Claiming Jin privately favored Tai, he then stripped both men's registration, and pursued reprimand of Ma Wensheng and former recommenders of Tai—Minister Liu Daxia, Supervising Secretary Zhao Shixian, Censor Zhang Jin, and others—to commoner; others fined rice sent to the frontier numbered more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Claiming that Xu Jin had favored Tai privately, Jin stripped both men from the roster and also punished Ma Wensheng and those who had earlier recommended Tai—Minister Liu Daxia, Supervising Secretary Zhao Shixian, Censor Zhang Jin, and others—by reducing them to commoner status; more than fifty others were fined grain for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 泰歸，居韋曲別墅，不入城市。

translations.literal: Tai returned and lived in a separate villa at Wei Qu, not entering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tai went home, lived in a villa at Wei Qu, and never entered the city.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed his office was restored; he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed his offices were restored, and he retired.

sentences.zh: 年八十卒。

translations.literal: Age eighty he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty.

sentences.zh: 卒時榻下有聲若霆者。

translations.literal: At the time of death beneath the couch there was a sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: At the moment of his death a sound like thunder came from beneath his couch.

sentences.zh: 泰奉身儉素。

translations.literal: Tai maintained his person thrifty and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Tai lived a frugal and austere life.

sentences.zh: 貴賓至，不過二肉。

translations.literal: When honored guests arrived, not more than two meat dishes.
translations.idiomatic: Even when honored guests came, he served no more than two meat dishes.

sentences.zh: 為尚書，無緋衣。

translations.literal: As Minister he had no red robes.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen to minister, he owned no ceremonial red robe.

sentences.zh: 及卒，家人始制以斂。

translations.literal: When he died the family only then made one to enshroud him.
translations.idiomatic: Only after his death did his family have one made for his burial.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，追謚端惠。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi period posthumously titled Duanhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi period he was granted the posthumous title Duanhui (Upright and Kind).

sentences.zh: 張津，字廣漢，博羅人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jin, style Guanghan, a native of Boluo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jin, courtesy name Guanghan, was a native of Boluo.

sentences.zh: 成化末進士，除建陽知縣。

translations.literal: Late Chenghua advanced scholar; removed to magistrate of Jianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the examinations in the late Chenghua reign, he was appointed magistrate of Jianyang.

sentences.zh: 築城郭，遏礦盜，建朱熹、蔡元定諸賢祠，置祭田畀其子孫。

translations.literal: Built city walls, checked mining bandits, built shrines to Zhu Xi, Cai Yuanding, and other worthies, set sacrificial fields given to their descendants.
translations.idiomatic: He walled the city, curbed mining bandits, erected shrines to Zhu Xi, Cai Yuanding, and other sages, and endowed sacrificial fields for their descendants.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，補大治，征授御史。

translations.literal: Mourning return; supplemented Dazhi; summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was transferred to Dazhi, then summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年冬，吏部缺尚書，廷臣推馬文升、閔珪，而津偕同官文森、曾大有請用致仕尚書周經、兩廣總督劉大夏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi the Ministry of Personnel lacked a minister; court ministers recommended Ma Wensheng and Min Gui, while Jin together with colleagues Wen Sen and Zeng Dayou requested employing retired Minister Zhou Jing and the two Guangs governor-general Liu Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the fourteenth year of Hongzhi the Ministry of Personnel had no minister; court officials recommended Ma Wensheng and Min Gui, while Jin together with colleagues Wen Sen and Zeng Dayou petitioned to appoint the retired Minister Zhou Jing and the governor-general of the two Guangs Liu Daxia.

sentences.zh: 忤旨下詔獄。

translations.literal: Contrary to the edict he was sent down to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: The petition offended the throne and he was sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 給事御史論救，得釋。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censors debated rescue; he obtained release.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censors protested on his behalf and he was released.

sentences.zh: 已，言：「陛下延訪大臣，而庶官不預，非所以明目達聰也。

translations.literal: Already he memorialized: "Your Majesty extends consultation to great ministers, yet common officials are not included—this is not the way to brighten the eyes and reach keen hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he memorialized: "Your Majesty consults chief ministers, but ordinary officials are not admitted—this is not how to see clearly and hear acutely.

sentences.zh: 乞命卿佐侍從及考滿朝覲諸外僚，鹹得以時進見，通達下情。」

translations.literal: I beg ordering ministers, aides in attendance, and outer officials after examination completed paying court visit—all may at times advance to audience and penetrate to reach lower feelings."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that ministers, aides-in-waiting, and outer officials who have finished their tenure and come to court be allowed audience from time to time, so lower grievances may be heard."

sentences.zh: 武宗初，巡按廣西，劾總鎮中官韋經擅移官帑。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuzong he toured and inspected Guangxi, impeaching the overall commander eunuch Wei Jing for overstepping in moving official funds.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Wuzong's reign he inspected Guangxi as touring censor and impeached the eunuch grand commander Wei Jing for misappropriating official funds.

sentences.zh: 預平富賀賊，被賚，出為泉州知府。

translations.literal: Participated in pacifying Fu and He bandits, was rewarded, and left office as Quanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying bandits in Fu and He counties, was rewarded, and left office as prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐嘗舉泰，勒為民。

translations.literal: Sat because he once recommended Tai; compelled to commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to commoner status for having once recommended Tai.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾敗，起寧波知府，遷山東左參政，擢右僉都御史，提督操江。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin was defeated he was raised as Ningbo prefect, moved to Shandong Left Participant, promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise Yangtze training.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Jin's fall he was made prefect of Ningbo, transferred to Left Participant in Shandong, then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise the Yangtze fleet.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，巡撫應天諸府。

translations.literal: Advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governed the Yingtian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was further promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made governor of the Yingtian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 所部水旱，請停織造。

translations.literal: His jurisdiction had flood and drought; he requested stopping weaving manufacture.
translations.idiomatic: In his district flood and drought struck, and he asked that imperial weaving be halted.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，疏諫，不報。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage toured north; [he] memorialized in remonstrance; no response.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured the north, he submitted a remonstrating memorial, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 浙孝豐奸民據深山拒捕，積二十年莫能制。

translations.literal: In Zhejiang Xiaofeng, treacherous people occupied deep mountains resisting arrest; piled up twenty years—none could control them.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaofeng, Zhejiang, lawless villagers held out in the deep mountains and resisted arrest; for twenty years no one could subdue them.

sentences.zh: 津托別事赴浙，悉縛之。

translations.literal: Jin used another matter as pretext to go to Zhejiang; all bound them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin went to Zhejiang on another pretext and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 加戶部右侍郎，巡撫如故。

translations.literal: Added Right Vice Minister of Revenue; governor as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Right Vice Minister of Revenue while retaining his post as governor.

sentences.zh: 帝自宣府還，復欲北幸，津疏切諫，不報。

translations.literal: The emperor returned from Xuanfu, again wished to visit the north; Jin memorialized with cutting remonstrance; no response.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned from Xuanfu he wished to go north again; Jin submitted a forceful remonstrance, again without reply.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Died; posthumously granted Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 陳壽，字本仁，其先新淦人。

translations.literal: Chen Shou, style Benren; his ancestors were people of Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shou, courtesy name Benren, came from a family originally of Xingan.

sentences.zh: 祖誌弘，洪武間代兄戍遼東，遂籍寧遠衛。

translations.literal: Grandfather Zhihong, during Hongwu replaced his elder brother to garrison Liaodong, thus registered at Ningyuan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhihong, in the Hongwu reign, took his elder brother's place on garrison duty in Liaodong and was registered at Ningyuan Guard.

sentences.zh: 壽少貧甚，得遺金，坐守至夜分，還其主。

translations.literal: Shou in youth was very poor; obtained lost gold, sat guarding until midnight, returned it to its owner.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was very poor in his youth; when he found lost gold he sat guarding it until midnight and returned it to its owner.

sentences.zh: 從鄉人賀欽學，登成化八年進士，授戶科給事中。

translations.literal: Followed fellow townsman He Qin in study; rose as jinshi in the eighth year of Chenghua; appointed Household Section supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under his fellow townsman He Qin, passed the examinations in the eighth year of Chenghua, and was appointed supervising secretary of the Household Section.

sentences.zh: 視宣、大邊防，劾去鎮守中官不檢者。

translations.literal: Inspected Xuan and Da border defense; impeached and removed stationed eunuchs who were unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting border defenses at Xuanfu and Datong, he impeached and removed stationed eunuchs who had grown lax.

sentences.zh: 又嘗劾萬貴妃兄弟及中官梁芳、僧繼曉，系詔獄。

translations.literal: Also once impeached Consort Wan's brothers and eunuch Liang Fang and monk Jixiao; tied in the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: He also once impeached the brothers of Consort Wan, the eunuch Liang Fang, and the monk Jixiao, and was sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 得釋，屢遷都給事中。

translations.literal: Obtained release; repeatedly moved to Chief Supervising Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was released and was repeatedly promoted to Chief Supervising Secretary.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，王恕為吏部，擢壽大理丞。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi, Wang Shu was at the Ministry of Personnel; promoted Shou to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Hongzhi, when Wang Shu headed the Ministry of Personnel, Shou was promoted to Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 劉吉憾恕，諷御史劾壽不習刑名，冀以罪恕。

translations.literal: Liu Ji resented Shu; induced a censor to impeach Shou for not being versed in penal law, hoping thereby to implicate Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji bore a grudge against Shu and prompted a censor to impeach Shou for ignorance of penal law, hoping to bring Shu down with him.

sentences.zh: 竟調壽南京光祿少卿，就轉鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: In the end transferred Shou to Nanjing Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, then turned to Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was in the end transferred to Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments at Nanjing and soon after made Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 十三年冬，以右僉都御史巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the winter of the thirteenth year, with the title Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he governed Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the thirteenth year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made governor of Yansui.

sentences.zh: 火篩數盜邊，前鎮巡官俱得罪去。

translations.literal: Huosai repeatedly raided the border; former command and inspection officials all were faulted and left.
translations.idiomatic: Huosai had repeatedly raided the frontier, and successive commanders and inspectors had all been punished and removed.

sentences.zh: 壽至，蒐軍實，廣間諜，分布士馬為十道，使互相應援，軍勢始振。

translations.literal: When Shou arrived, he searched out military strength, expanded spies, distributed troops and horses into ten routes so they could support one another; military momentum began to revive.
translations.idiomatic: When Shou arrived he reviewed true military strength, expanded intelligence networks, and deployed troops and horses in ten columns that could support one another, and the army's morale began to recover.

sentences.zh: 明年，諸部大入，先以百余騎來誘。

translations.literal: The next year all tribes entered in force; first they came with more than a hundred riders to lure [the Ming].
translations.idiomatic: The next year the tribes invaded in force, first sending more than a hundred horsemen as bait.

sentences.zh: 諸將請擊之，壽不可。

translations.literal: The generals requested to strike them; Shou would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The generals asked to attack, but Shou refused.

sentences.zh: 自出帳，擁數十騎，據胡床指麾飲食。

translations.literal: He himself went out of the tent, surrounded by several tens of riders, sat on a folding chair directing drinking and eating.
translations.idiomatic: He came out of the tent himself with only a few dozen horsemen, sat on a camp chair, and calmly directed his meal.

sentences.zh: 寇望見，疑之，引去。

translations.literal: The bandits saw and suspected [a trap]; led their forces away.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders saw this, grew suspicious, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 諸道襲擊，斬獲甚多。

translations.literal: All routes raided in attack; beheaded and captured very many.
translations.idiomatic: The columns then struck from every direction and killed or captured a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 朝廷方遣苗逵等重兵至，而壽已奏捷。

translations.literal: The court was just sending Miao Kui and others with heavy troops when Shou had already memorialized victory.
translations.idiomatic: The court was just dispatching Miao Kui and other commanders with a large relief force when Shou had already reported victory.

sentences.zh: 孝宗嘉之，加錄一等。

translations.literal: Xiaozong praised it; added one grade in the record.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong commended him and raised his recorded rank by one grade.

sentences.zh: 逵欲乘勝搗巢。

translations.literal: Kui wished to ride the victory to destroy the nest.
translations.idiomatic: Kui wanted to follow up the victory by destroying the enemy base.

sentences.zh: 駐延綏久，戰馬三萬匹日費芻菽不貲。

translations.literal: Stationed at Yansui long; thirty thousand war horses daily cost fodder and beans beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: After long encampment at Yansui, the daily cost of fodder for thirty thousand war horses was enormous.

sentences.zh: 壽請出牧近塞，就水草，眾有難色。

translations.literal: Shou requested going out to pasture near the border, near water and grass; the troops looked uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Shou asked to drive the herds out to pasture near the border where there was water and grass, but the men were reluctant.

sentences.zh: 壽跨馬先行，眾皆從之，省費數十萬。

translations.literal: Shou straddled his horse and went first; the masses all followed; saved expenses of several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shou mounted his horse and led the way, and everyone followed; the move saved several hundred thousand in costs.

sentences.zh: 當戰捷時，或勸註子弟名籍，壽曰：「吾子弟不知弓槊，寧當與血戰士同受賞哉？」

translations.literal: When the battle victory came, some urged registering his sons and younger brothers on the rolls; Shou said: "My sons and younger brothers do not know bow and spear—should they really share rewards with soldiers who fought in blood?"
translations.idiomatic: After the victory some urged him to register his sons and younger brothers for rewards, but Shou said, "My sons and younger brothers do not know bow and spear—should they really share rewards with men who fought in blood?"

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end he did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He would not allow it in the end.

sentences.zh: 十六年以右副都御史掌南院。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he managed the Southern Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of the Censorate at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 正德初，劉瑾矯詔逮南京科道戴銑、薄彥徽等，壽抗章論救。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde, Liu Jin forged an edict to arrest Nanjing Secretariat and censorial officials Dai Xuan, Bo Yanhui, and others; Shou resisted with a memorial arguing for their rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign Liu Jin forged an edict to arrest the Nanjing censors and supervising secretaries Dai Xuan, Bo Yanhui, and others; Shou submitted a forceful memorial in their defense.

sentences.zh: 瑾怒，令致仕。

translations.literal: Jin was angry and ordered him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was enraged and forced him to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋坐延綏倉儲虧損，罰米二千三百石、布千五百匹。

translations.literal: Soon he was charged because Yansui granary storage showed a deficit; fined two thousand three hundred shi of grain and one thousand five hundred bolts of cloth.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon punished for deficits in the Yansui granaries with a fine of 2,300 shi of grain and 1,500 bolts of cloth.

sentences.zh: 貧不能償，上章自訴。

translations.literal: Poor and unable to pay, he submitted a memorial pleading his case.
translations.idiomatic: Too poor to pay, he memorialized the throne in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 瑾廉知壽貧，特免之。

translations.literal: Jin investigated and knew Shou was poor; specially exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin looked into the matter, learned that Shou was poor, and specially exempted him.

sentences.zh: 中官廖堂鎮陜西貪暴，楊一清以壽剛果，九年正月起撫其地。

translations.literal: Eunuch Liao Tang governed Shaanxi greedily and violently; Yang Yiqing, because Shou was firm and resolute, in the first month of the ninth year raised him to govern that region.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Liao Tang ruled Shaanxi with greed and violence; Yang Yiqing, valuing Shou's firmness and resolve, had him recalled in the first month of the ninth year to govern the province.

sentences.zh: 堂初奉詔制氈幄百六十間，贏金數萬，將遺權幸。

translations.literal: Tang at first received an edict to make one hundred sixty felt tents, gained gold of several tens of thousands, and intended to present them to powerful favorites.
translations.idiomatic: Tang had first been ordered to make 160 felt tents, skimmed off tens of thousands in gold, and planned to give the surplus to powerful favorites at court.

sentences.zh: 壽檄所司留備振，復戒諭堂勿假貢獻名有所科取。

translations.literal: Shou issued an edict the responsible offices to retain them for relief reserves; again warned and instructed Tang not to borrow the name of tribute to levy exactions.
translations.idiomatic: Shou ordered the relevant offices to keep the goods for famine relief and warned Tang not to levy exactions under the pretense of presenting tribute.

sentences.zh: 堂怒，將傾之。

translations.literal: Tang was angry and was about to overturn him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang was furious and set out to ruin him.

sentences.zh: 壽四疏乞休，不得。

translations.literal: Shou four times memorialized begging to retire; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shou submitted four memorials asking to retire, but was not allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 堂爪牙數十輩散府縣漁利，壽命捕之，皆逃歸，氣益沮。

translations.literal: Several tens of Tang's henchmen scattered through prefectures and counties to fish for profit; Shou ordered them arrested; all fled back; their spirit grew increasingly discouraged.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen of Tang's agents were scattered through the prefectures and counties extorting profit; Shou ordered them arrested, and they all fled back to him, so that his arrogance was much diminished.

sentences.zh: 其秋，拜南京兵部侍郎，陜人號呼擁輿，移日不得行。

translations.literal: That autumn he was appointed Nanjing Vice Minister of War; Shaanxi people shouted and crowded his carriage; for days he could not travel.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was appointed Vice Minister of War at Nanjing; the people of Shaanxi shouted and thronged his carriage so that for days he could not move on.

sentences.zh: 逾年，乞駭骨，就進刑部尚書，致仕。

translations.literal: After more than a year he begged to retire his worn bones; then advanced to Minister of Punishments and retired.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he asked to retire; he was promoted on departure to Minister of Punishments and then retired.

sentences.zh: 壽為給事中，言時政無隱，獨不喜劾人，曰：「吾父戒吾勿作刑官，易枉人。

translations.literal: As supervising secretary Shou spoke on current politics without concealment, but alone did not like impeaching people; he said: "My father warned me not to be a penal official, for it is easy to wrong people.
translations.idiomatic: As a supervising secretary Shou spoke frankly on current affairs, but he disliked impeaching others and said, "My father warned me not to become a penal official, for it is easy to wrong people.

sentences.zh: 言官枉人尤甚，吾不敢妄言也。」

translations.literal: Censorial officials wrong people even more severely; I dare not speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Censors wrong people even more readily, and I dare not speak rashly."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖改元，詔進一品階，遣有司存問，時年八十有三。

translations.literal: When Jiajing changed the reign title, an edict advanced him one grade; officials were sent to inquire after him; at the time he was eighty-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing reign began, an edict raised him one rank and sent local officials to inquire after him; he was then eighty-three years old.

sentences.zh: 壽廉，歷官四十年，無家可歸。

translations.literal: Shou was incorrupt; he held office forty years and had no home to which to return.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was incorruptible; after forty years in office he had no home of his own to return to.

sentences.zh: 寓南京，所居不蔽風雨。

translations.literal: He lodged at Nanjing; his dwelling did not shelter against wind and rain.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Nanjing in a house that could scarcely keep out wind and rain.

sentences.zh: 其卒也，尚書李充嗣、府尹寇天敘為之斂。

translations.literal: At his death, Ministers Li Chongsi and Prefect Kou Tianxu enshrouded him.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, the minister Li Chongsi and the prefect Kou Tianxu prepared his body for burial.

sentences.zh: 又數年，親舊賻助，始得歸葬新淦。

translations.literal: After several more years, relatives and friends aided with funeral gifts, and only then could he be returned and buried at Xingan.
translations.idiomatic: Only after several more years, with help from relatives and friends in funeral gifts, was he at last buried in his native Xingan.

sentences.zh: 樊瑩，字廷璧，常山人。

translations.literal: Fan Ying, style Tingbi, a native of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying, courtesy name Tingbi, was a native of Changshan.

sentences.zh: 天順末，舉進士，引疾歸養。

translations.literal: Late in Tianshun he was raised as jinshi; citing illness he returned to nurture [his parents].
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianshun reign he passed the examinations as a jinshi, then pleaded illness and returned home to care for his parents.

sentences.zh: 久之，授行人，使蜀不受饋，土官作卻金亭識之。

translations.literal: Long afterward he was appointed traveling envoy; sent to Shu he did not accept gifts; native officials built a Refused-Gold Pavilion to commemorate it.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was appointed a traveling envoy; on a mission to Shu he refused all gifts, and the native officials erected a Refused-Gold Pavilion in his honor.

sentences.zh: 成化八年，擢御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua he was promoted to censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Chenghua he was promoted to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 山東盜起，奉命捕獲其魁。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Shandong; he received orders and captured their chief.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Shandong he was ordered to capture them and seized their leader.

sentences.zh: 清軍江北，所條奏多著為例。

translations.literal: He inspected troops north of the Yangtze; his submitted items many were established as precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Inspecting troops north of the Yangtze, he submitted many proposals that were adopted as permanent regulations.

sentences.zh: 改按雲南，交阯誘邊氓為寇，馳檄寢其謀。

translations.literal: He was changed to inspect Yunnan; Jiaozhi lured border commoners to become bandits; he galloped out an edict and quelled their plot.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to inspect Yunnan, he found that Jiaozhi was inciting border subjects to raid; he issued a swift proclamation that put an end to the scheme.

sentences.zh: 出知松江府。

translations.literal: He left office to become prefect of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He left the censorate to serve as prefect of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 運夫苦耗折，瑩革民夫，令糧長專運，而寬其綱，用以優之。

translations.literal: Transport laborers suffered from loss deductions; Ying abolished civilian laborers, ordered grain chiefs to transport exclusively, and relaxed their quotas, using this to favor them.
translations.idiomatic: Transport workers were burdened by wastage deductions; Ying abolished civilian corvée transport, put grain chiefs in sole charge of hauling, and eased their quotas as a benefit to them.

sentences.zh: 賦役循周忱舊法，稍為變通，民困大蘇。

translations.literal: Taxes and corvée followed Zhou Chen's old law, with slight changes; the people's hardship was greatly relieved.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Zhou Chen's old tax and corvée system with modest adjustments, and the people's distress was greatly eased.

sentences.zh: 憂歸，起知平陽。

translations.literal: He returned for mourning; on recall he became prefect of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was recalled and appointed prefect of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，詔大臣舉方面官。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi, an edict ordered great ministers to recommend regional officials.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign the throne ordered senior ministers to recommend provincial officials.

sentences.zh: 侍郎黃孔昭以瑩應，尚書王恕亦器之，擢河南按察使。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Huang Kongzhao nominated Ying in response; Minister Wang Shu also valued him; he was promoted to Henan Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Huang Kongzhao recommended Ying, Minister Wang Shu also esteemed him, and he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 黃河為患，民多流移。

translations.literal: The Yellow River became a disaster; many people drifted away.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River brought disaster, many people were displaced.

sentences.zh: 瑩巡振，全活甚眾。

translations.literal: Ying toured and gave relief; he wholly saved very many.
translations.idiomatic: Ying toured the region distributing relief and saved a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 河南田賦多積弊，巡撫都御史徐恪欲考本末，眾難之。

translations.literal: Henan field taxes had many piled-up abuses; Governor Censor-in-Chief Xu Ke wished to examine root and branch; the crowd found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's land taxes were riddled with long-standing abuses; Governor Xu Ke wanted to trace every account to its source, but others thought it impossible.

sentences.zh: 瑩曰：「視萬猶千，視千猶百耳，何難。」

translations.literal: Ying said: "View ten thousand as a thousand, view a thousand as a hundred—that is all; what difficulty is there?"
translations.idiomatic: Ying said, "Treat ten thousand as a thousand and a thousand as a hundred—that is all there is to it; what is so hard?"

sentences.zh: 恪以屬瑩部吏鉤考，旬日間，宿蠹一清。

translations.literal: Ke entrusted it to Ying's department clerks to examine and verify; within ten days, long-standing corruption was entirely cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ke put the task in the hands of Ying's clerks for a full audit, and within ten days every long-standing abuse had been cleared away.

sentences.zh: 四年遷應天府尹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was moved to magistrate of the Capital Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to magistrate of the Capital Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 守備中官蔣琮與言官訐奏，所蔓引多至罪黜。

translations.literal: Garrison eunuch Jiang Cong and censors mutually impeached one another; those implicated in the widening accusations many reached punishment and removal.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison eunuch Jiang Cong and the censors traded accusations, and many of those drawn into the affair were punished or dismissed.

sentences.zh: 瑩承命推鞫，初若不為異者，琮大喜。

translations.literal: Ying received orders to conduct the investigation; at first he seemed to show no difference [in treatment]; Cong was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Ying was ordered to conduct the inquiry and at first appeared to treat Jiang Cong no differently, to Cong's great delight.

sentences.zh: 後奏其傷孝陵山脈事，琮遂下獄，充凈軍。

translations.literal: Later he memorialized the matter of injuring the mountain vein of Xiaoling; Cong was then sent down to prison and made a pure-army laborer.
translations.idiomatic: He then reported that Cong had damaged the geomantic line of the Xiaoling tombs; Cong was imprisoned and reduced to menial service.

sentences.zh: 七年遷南京工部右侍郎，尋改右副都御史巡撫湖廣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing; soon changed to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief governing Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made Right Vice Minister of Works at Nanjing, then soon appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and governor of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 錦田賊結兩廣瑤、僮為寇，瑩諭散余黨，戮首惡十八人。

translations.literal: Jintian bandits joined with Yao and Zhuang of the two Guangs as bandits; Ying instructed and dispersed the remainder, executing eighteen chief evildoers.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits at Jintian allied with Yao and Zhuang raiders from the two Guangs; Ying persuaded the lesser followers to disperse and executed eighteen ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾乞休。

translations.literal: After more than a year, because of illness he begged to retire.
translations.idiomatic: After a little more than a year he asked to retire on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 家居七年，中外交薦，起故官撫治鄖陽，旋改南京刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: At home seven years; court and regions mutually recommended; he was raised to his former office to govern Yunyang, soon changed to Right Vice Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home for seven years until recommended from every quarter, was recalled to his former rank to govern Yunyang, and was soon made Right Vice Minister of Punishments at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 十六年，雲南景東衛晝晦七日，宜良地震如雷，曲靖大火數發，貴州亦多災異，命瑩巡視。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, at Yunnan's Jingdong Guard daylight was dark for seven days; Yiliang's earthquake was like thunder; Qujing had great fires several times; Guizhou also had many disasters and portents; Ying was ordered to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year Jingdong Guard in Yunnan was dark at noon for seven days, Yiliang was shaken by thunderous earthquakes, Qujing suffered repeated great fires, and Guizhou too reported many omens; Ying was ordered to investigate.

sentences.zh: 至則劾鎮巡官罪，黜文武不職者千七百人。

translations.literal: When he arrived he impeached the crimes of command and inspection officials; dismissed one thousand seven hundred civil and military officers who did not perform their duties.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he impeached the frontier commanders and inspectors and dismissed 1,700 incompetent civil and military officials.

sentences.zh: 廉知景東之變，乃指揮吳勇侵官帑，圖脫罪，因雲霧晦冥虛張其事，劾罪之。

translations.literal: On investigation he knew the Jingdong affair was actually Commander Wu Yong encroaching on the official treasury, plotting to escape guilt; because of cloud and fog darkness he had inflated the affair; he impeached and punished him.
translations.idiomatic: His inquiry showed that the Jingdong portent was really Commander Wu Yong's embezzlement of public funds; to escape blame Wu had exaggerated the omen of darkness and mist, and Ying impeached and punished him.

sentences.zh: 還進本部尚書。

translations.literal: On return he advanced to Minister of his department.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to Minister of his department.

sentences.zh: 武宗踐阼，致仕歸。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended the throne, he retired and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne he retired and went home.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾以會勘隆平侯爭襲事，連及瑩，削籍。

translations.literal: Liu Jin, because of the joint investigation of the Longping Marquis succession dispute, implicated Ying and stripped his registry.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin implicated Ying in the joint inquiry into the Longping Marquis's disputed succession and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 明年又坐減松江官布，罰米五百石輸邊。

translations.literal: The next year he was again charged because of reducing Songjiang official cloth; fined five hundred shi of grain to be sent to the border.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was again punished for having reduced the official cloth quota at Songjiang and was fined 500 shi of grain for the frontier.

sentences.zh: 瑩素貧，至是益窘。

translations.literal: Ying had always been poor; reaching this he was increasingly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had always been poor, and now his circumstances grew still worse.

sentences.zh: 三年十一月卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year he died; age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eleventh month of the third year, aged seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，復官，贈太子少保，謚清簡。

translations.literal: When Jin was defeated, his office was restored; posthumously granted Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince; posthumous name Qingjian.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall his office was restored; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Crown Prince with the posthumous name Qingjian (Pure and Simple).

sentences.zh: 瑩性誠愨，農月坐籃輿戴笠，子孫舁行田間，曰：「非徒視稼，欲子孫習勞也。」

translations.literal: Ying's nature was sincere and honest; in farming months he sat in a bamboo litter wearing a bamboo hat, his sons and grandsons carrying him through the fields; he said: "It is not only to view the crops—I wish my sons and grandsons to learn labor."
translations.idiomatic: Ying was sincere and unassuming; in the farming season he rode in a bamboo litter under a straw hat while his sons and grandsons carried him through the fields, saying, "This is not only to inspect the crops—I want my descendants to learn hard work."

sentences.zh: 其後人率教，多願樸力學者。

translations.literal: His later descendants uniformly followed his teaching; many wished to be plain and diligent scholars.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants generally followed his teaching, and many became men of plain habits who devoted themselves to learning.

sentences.zh: 熊繡，字汝明，道州人，其先以戍籍自豐城徙焉。

translations.literal: Xiong Xiu, style Ruming, a native of Daozhou; his ancestors because of garrison registry moved there from Fengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Xiu, courtesy name Ruming, was a native of Daozhou; his forebears had moved there from Fengcheng on military registration.

sentences.zh: 繡舉成化二年進士，授行人。

translations.literal: Xiu was raised as jinshi in the second year of Chenghua; appointed traveling envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu passed the examinations as a jinshi in the second year of Chenghua and was appointed a traveling envoy.

sentences.zh: 奉使楚府，巡茶四川，力拒饋遺。

translations.literal: He received a mission to the Chu princely establishment and inspected tea in Sichuan; forcefully refused gifts.
translations.idiomatic: On missions to the Chu princely establishment and on tea inspection in Sichuan he firmly refused all gifts.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，巡按陜西。

translations.literal: Promoted to censor; toured and inspected Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to censor and sent to inspect Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 左布政於璠以官帑銀饋苑馬卿邵進，繡發其罪。

translations.literal: Left Administration Commissioner Yu Fan used official treasury silver to gift Park Horse Director Shao Jin; Xiu exposed his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Left Administration Commissioner Yu Fan had given official silver from the treasury to the Park of Imperial Horses director Shao Jin; Xiu exposed the crime.

sentences.zh: 璠遁赴京訐繡，帝並下繡吏，謫知清豐，璠、進亦除名。

translations.literal: Fan fled to the capital to accuse Xiu; the emperor sent down both Xiu to the clerks, demoted to prefect of Qingfeng; Fan and Jin also had their names removed.
translations.idiomatic: Fan fled to the capital to accuse Xiu; the emperor had both men arrested, demoted Xiu to magistrate of Qingfeng, and struck Fan and Jin from the rolls as well.

sentences.zh: 久之，鳳翔闕知府，擢繡任之。

translations.literal: Long afterward Fengxiang lacked a prefect; Xiu was promoted to fill the post.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward, when Fengxiang had no prefect, Xiu was promoted to the post.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，遷山東左參政，進右布政使。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he was moved to Left Participant in Shandong; advanced to Right Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he was transferred to Left Participant in Shandong and then promoted to Right Administration Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年以右副都御史巡撫延綏。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he governed Yansui.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made governor of Yansui.

sentences.zh: 榆林初僅小堡，屯兵備冬。

translations.literal: Yulin at first was only a small fort; troops were stationed to prepare for winter.
translations.idiomatic: Yulin was at first only a small fort, with troops stationed there to prepare for winter.

sentences.zh: 景泰中，始移巡撫、總兵官居之，遂為西北巨鎮，城隘弗能容，繡因請增築千二百余丈。

translations.literal: In the Jingtai period, the grand coordinator and regional commander were first moved to dwell there; it then became a great northwestern stronghold. The walls were narrow and could not hold them; Xiu therefore requested an extension of more than twelve hundred zhang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingtai reign the grand coordinator and regional commander were first posted there, and it became a major northwestern stronghold. The walls were too cramped to hold the garrison; Xiu therefore requested an extension of more than twelve hundred zhang.

sentences.zh: 涖鎮數年，練兵積粟，邊政修舉。

translations.literal: After several years governing the post, he drilled troops and accumulated grain; frontier administration was put in good order.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in command he drilled troops and built up grain stores, and frontier administration was brought into good order.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部左、右侍郎，尚書劉大夏深倚信之。

translations.literal: He served successively as Left and Right Vice Minister of War; Minister Liu Daxia relied on him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as Left and Right Vice Minister of War, and Minister Liu Daxia placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 勝騰四衛勇士額三四萬人，率虛籍。

translations.literal: The warrior rolls of the four Tengxiang guards totaled thirty to forty thousand men; for the most part they were empty rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The warrior rolls of the four Tengxiang guards listed thirty to forty thousand men, but for the most part the rolls were fictitious.

sentences.zh: 歲糜錢谷數十萬，多入奄人家。

translations.literal: Each year hundreds of thousands in money and grain were squandered, much of it going into eunuchs' households.
translations.idiomatic: Every year hundreds of thousands in money and grain were wasted, much of it ending up in eunuchs' households.

sentences.zh: 廷臣屢請稽核，輒被撓。

translations.literal: Court officials repeatedly requested audits, but each time were obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials repeatedly called for audits, but each time their efforts were blocked.

sentences.zh: 十八年命繡清厘，未竟而孝宗崩。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Xiu was ordered to investigate and settle accounts; before he finished, Emperor Xiaozong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Xiu was ordered to investigate and clear the rolls, but before he could finish, Emperor Xiaozong died.

sentences.zh: 朝政漸變，繡力持不顧，得詭冒者萬四千人。

translations.literal: Court policy gradually shifted; Xiu held firm without regard, and uncovered fourteen thousand fraudulent enrollees.
translations.idiomatic: Court policy gradually changed, yet Xiu stood firm regardless and exposed fourteen thousand fraudulent enrollees.

sentences.zh: 禦馬太監寧瑾等疏請復舊，給事御史交章劾瑾，大夏亦力爭。

translations.literal: Imperial Horse Supervisor eunuch Ning Jin and others memorialized to restore the old rolls; supervising secretaries and censors submitted successive memorials impeaching Jin, and Daxia also argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Horse Supervisor Ning Jin and other eunuchs memorialized to restore the old rolls; supervising secretaries and censors submitted memorial after memorial impeaching Jin, and Liu Daxia argued forcefully as well.

sentences.zh: 武宗不得已從之，而宥瑾等不問。

translations.literal: Emperor Wuzong had no choice but to agree, yet pardoned Jin and the others without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wuzong had no choice but to assent, yet pardoned Jin and the others without pursuing the matter.

sentences.zh: 正德元年擢右都御史，總督兩廣軍務兼巡撫事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, overall commander of Guang military affairs and concurrently grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief, placed in overall command of military affairs in the two Guang, and made grand coordinator as well.

sentences.zh: 既抵鎮，盡裁幕府供億，秋毫無所取。

translations.literal: Once he reached his post, he cut all staff provision expenses; he took not the slightest for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Once he reached his post he slashed all staff provisioning to the bone and took nothing for himself, however small.

sentences.zh: 二年與總兵官伏羌伯毛銳討平賀縣僮。

translations.literal: In the second year, together with Regional Commander Ma Rui, Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, he campaigned and pacified the Zhuang of Hexian.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, together with Regional Commander Ma Rui, the Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, he campaigned and pacified the Zhuang of Hexian.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾以前汰勇士事深疾繡，伺察無所得。

translations.literal: Liu Jin deeply resented Xiu for his earlier purge of warriors; he spied on him but found nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin deeply resented Xiu for his earlier purge of the warrior rolls and kept watch on him, but found nothing to use against him.

sentences.zh: 召掌南京都察院事，尋以中旨罷之。

translations.literal: He was summoned to head the Nanjing Censorate; soon thereafter he was dismissed by a direct edict from the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to head the Nanjing Censorate, but soon afterward was dismissed by a direct edict from the throne.

sentences.zh: 已，復摭延綏倉儲浥爛為繡罪，罰米五百石，責繡躬輸於邊。

translations.literal: Later, moldy grain in the Yansui granaries was seized upon as Xiu's crime; he was fined five hundred shi of grain and ordered to deliver it in person to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Later, spoiled grain in the Yansui granaries was made Xiu's crime; he was fined five hundred shi of grain and ordered to deliver it in person to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 繡家遂破。

translations.literal: Xiu's household was thus ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's household was thus ruined.

sentences.zh: 十年閏四月卒，無子。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, intercalary fourth month, he died without sons.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, in the intercalary fourth month, he died without sons.

sentences.zh: 巡撫秦金頌其清節於朝，贈刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Qin Jin praised his integrity at court; he was posthumously granted Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Qin Jin praised his integrity at court, and he was posthumously made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 太仆少卿何孟春以繡承繼孫幼且貧，無以為養，請如主事張鳳翔孔琦例，賜月廩，且乞予謚。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud He Mengchun noted that Xiu's adopted heir's grandson was young and poor and could not support himself, and requested, following the precedents of Director Zhang Fengxiang and Kong Qi, a monthly grain allowance and also a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud He Mengchun said that the grandson of Xiu's adopted heir was young and poor and had no means of support, and asked that he be granted a monthly grain allowance on the precedent of Directors Zhang Fengxiang and Kong Qi, and also that Xiu be given a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 遂謚莊簡，給其孫米月一石。

translations.literal: He was therefore given the posthumous title Zhuangjian, and his grandson was granted one shi of grain per month.
translations.idiomatic: He was therefore given the posthumous title Zhuangjian, and his grandson was granted one shi of grain each month.

sentences.zh: 潘蕃，字廷芳，崇德人。

translations.literal: Pan Fan, style Tingfang, a native of Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Fan, courtesy name Tingfang, was a native of Chongde.

sentences.zh: 初冒鐘姓，既顯始復。

translations.literal: At first he used the surname Zhong; after he rose to prominence he restored his own name.
translations.idiomatic: At first he had taken the surname Zhong; after he rose to prominence he restored his own surname.

sentences.zh: 成化二年舉進士，授刑部主事。

translations.literal: In Chenghua year 2 he passed as jinshi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chenghua he passed the examinations as a jinshi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 歷郎中。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 雲南鎮守中官錢能為巡撫王恕所劾，詔蕃按，盡得其實。

translations.literal: Yunnan garrison eunuch Qian Neng was impeached by Grand Coordinator Wang Shu; Fan was ordered to investigate and obtained the full truth.
translations.idiomatic: The Yunnan garrison eunuch Qian Neng was impeached by Grand Coordinator Wang Shu; Fan was ordered to investigate and established the facts in full.

sentences.zh: 出為安慶知府，改鄖陽。

translations.literal: He went out as prefect of Anqing, then was transferred to Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Anqing and then transferred to Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 時府治初設，陜、洛流民畢聚。

translations.literal: At that time the prefectural seat had only just been established, and displaced people from Shaanxi and Luoyang all gathered there.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the prefectural seat had only just been established, and displaced people from Shaanxi and the Luoyang region all gathered there.

sentences.zh: 蕃悉心撫循，皆成土著。

translations.literal: Fan devoted himself to settling and guiding them, and all became permanent residents.
translations.idiomatic: Fan devoted himself to settling and guiding them until all became permanent residents.

sentences.zh: 累遷山東、湖廣左右布政使。

translations.literal: He was promoted in turn to Left and Right Administration Commissioner in Shandong and Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in turn to Left and Right Administration Commissioner in Shandong and Huguang.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年，以右副都御史巡撫四川，兼提督松潘軍務。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 9, as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief he was grand coordinator of Sichuan, concurrently supervising Songpan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of Sichuan, with concurrent charge of Songpan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣布威信，蠻人畏服，單車行松、茂莫敢犯。

translations.literal: He proclaimed authority and trust; the barbarians feared and submitted. Traveling alone through Song and Mao, none dared molest him.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed his authority and won trust; the tribes feared and submitted. Traveling alone through Song and Mao, none dared molest him.

sentences.zh: 遷南京兵部右侍郎，就改刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War in Nanjing, then immediately shifted to the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of War in Nanjing and then immediately moved to the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 十四年進右都御史，總督兩廣。

translations.literal: Year 14 he advanced to Right Censor-in-Chief and overall commander of the two Guang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and placed in overall command of the two Guang.

sentences.zh: 帳下士舊不下萬人，蕃汰之，才給使令而已。

translations.literal: Staff under his command had formerly numbered no less than ten thousand; Fan cut them down until only enough remained to carry out his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Staff under his command had formerly numbered no less than ten thousand; Fan cut them back until only enough remained to carry out his orders.

sentences.zh: 黎寇符南蛇亂海南，聚眾數萬。

translations.literal: The Li bandit Fu Nan She rebelled in Hainan and gathered tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The Li rebel Fu Nan She rose in Hainan and gathered tens of thousands of followers.

sentences.zh: 蕃令副使胡富調狼土兵討斬之，平賊巢千二百余所。

translations.literal: Fan ordered Vice Commissioner Hu Fu to mobilize Lang and Tu native troops to campaign and behead him, pacifying more than twelve hundred bandit lairs.
translations.idiomatic: Fan ordered Vice Commissioner Hu Fu to mobilize Lang and Tu native troops to campaign against him and take his head, pacifying more than twelve hundred bandit lairs.

sentences.zh: 論功，進左都御史。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his merit he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 已，又平歸善劇賊古三仔、唐大鬢等。

translations.literal: Later he also pacified the fierce bandits Gu Sanzai, Tang Dabin, and others in Guishan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he also pacified the fierce bandits Gu Sanzai, Tang Dabin, and others in Guishan.

sentences.zh: 思恩知府岑濬與田州知府岑猛相仇殺，攻陷田州，猛窮乞援。

translations.literal: Sin'en Prefect Cen Jun and Tianzhou Prefect Cen Meng feuded and killed one another's men; Jun seized Tianzhou, and Meng, driven to desperation, begged for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Sin'en Prefect Cen Jun and Tianzhou Prefect Cen Meng feuded and slaughtered one another's followers; Jun seized Tianzhou, and Meng, driven to desperation, begged for aid.

sentences.zh: 蕃諭濬罷兵，不從，乃與鎮守太監韋經、總兵官伏羌伯毛銳集兵十余萬，分六哨討之。

translations.literal: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities; he refused, so Fan joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Ma Rui, Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, gathering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Fan exhorted Jun to cease hostilities, but Jun refused; Fan then joined Garrison Supervisor Wei Jing and Regional Commander Ma Rui, the Earl Who Pacified the Qiang, mustering more than a hundred thousand troops in six columns to attack.

sentences.zh: 濬死，傳首軍門，斬級四千七百，盡平其地。

translations.literal: Jun died; his head was sent to the army gate. Four thousand seven hundred heads were taken, and the territory was wholly pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Jun died and his head was sent to the army gate; four thousand seven hundred heads were taken in all, and the territory was wholly pacified.

sentences.zh: 回軍討平南海縣豐湖賊褟元祖。

translations.literal: On the return march he also campaigned and pacified Tan Yuanzu, bandit of Fenghu in Nanhai County.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march he also campaigned and pacified Tan Yuanzu, the bandit of Fenghu in Nanhai County.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，璽書嘉勞。

translations.literal: News of victory arrived; an imperial letter commended and rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: When news of victory arrived, an imperial letter commended and rewarded them.

sentences.zh: 蕃奏，思恩宜設流官，猛構兵失地，宜降同知，俾還守舊土。

translations.literal: Fan memorialized that Sin'en ought to have an appointed official, and that Meng, for raising troops and losing territory, ought to be demoted to sub-prefect and allowed to return and guard his old lands.
translations.idiomatic: Fan memorialized that Sin'en ought to receive an appointed official, and that Meng, for raising troops and losing his territory, ought to be demoted to sub-prefect and allowed to return and guard his old lands.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書劉大夏議，猛世濟兇惡，不宜歸舊治，請兩府皆設流官，而降猛為千戶，徙之福建。

translations.literal: War Minister Liu Daxia argued that Meng's family had long been vicious and he ought not return to his old jurisdiction; he requested appointed officials in both prefectures, with Meng demoted to company commander and relocated to Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: War Minister Liu Daxia argued that Meng's line had long been vicious and he ought not return to his old jurisdiction; he asked that both prefectures receive appointed officials, with Meng demoted to company commander and relocated to Fujian.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 正德改元之正月召為南京刑部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month after the Zhengde reign change he was summoned as Minister of Justice in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the new Zhengde reign he was summoned as Minister of Justice in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 逾年，致仕。

translations.literal: After a year he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he retired from office.

sentences.zh: 初，蕃去兩廣，岑猛據田州不肯徙，知府謝湖畏猛悍，亦逗遛。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fan left the two Guang, Cen Meng held Tianzhou and would not move; Prefect Xie Hu feared Meng's ferocity and also lingered.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fan left the two Guang, Cen Meng held Tianzhou and refused to move; Prefect Xie Hu feared Meng's ferocity and also delayed.

sentences.zh: 事聞，逮湖詔獄。

translations.literal: When word reached the court, Hu was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, Hu was arrested and sent to the imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 湖委罪蕃及韋經、毛銳，經復委罪於尚書大夏。

translations.literal: Hu laid blame on Fan, Wei Jing, and Mao Rui; Jing in turn laid blame on Minister Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: Hu shifted blame onto Fan, Wei Jing, and Mao Rui; Jing in turn shifted blame onto Minister Liu Daxia.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾方惡大夏，遂並逮四人。

translations.literal: Liu Jin happened to hate Daxia, so all four were arrested.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin happened to hate Daxia, so all four were arrested together.

sentences.zh: 大夏以不從蕃言為罪，而蕃亦坐不能撫猛，俱謫戍肅州，三年九月也。

translations.literal: Daxia was punished for not following Fan's proposal, and Fan also was punished for failing to pacify Meng; all were exiled to garrison duty at Suzhou—this was in the ninth month of year 3.
translations.idiomatic: Daxia was punished for not following Fan's proposal, and Fan was also punished for failing to pacify Meng; all were exiled to garrison Suzhou in Gansu—this was in the ninth month of the third year.

sentences.zh: 既而瑾從戶部郎中莊祥言，遣太監韋霦核廣東庫藏，奏應解贓罰諸物多朽敝，梧州貯鹽利軍賞銀六十余萬兩不以時解。

translations.literal: Later Jin, following Bureau Director Zhuang Xiang's advice, sent eunuch Wei Yin to audit Guangdong treasuries. The memorial reported that goods due as fines and penalties were mostly rotten, and that more than six hundred thousand taels of silver from salt profits stored at Wuzhou for military rewards had not been forwarded on time.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at Bureau Director Zhuang Xiang's urging, Jin sent eunuch Wei Yin to audit Guangdong treasuries. The memorial reported that goods due as fines and penalties were mostly rotten, and that more than six hundred thousand taels of silver from salt profits stored at Wuzhou for military rewards had not been forwarded on time.

sentences.zh: 逮問蕃及前總督大夏、前左布政使仁和沈銳等八百九十九人，罰米輸邊。

translations.literal: Fan, former overall commander Daxia, former Left Administration Commissioner Shen Rui of Renhe, and eight hundred ninety-nine others were arrested and questioned, fined grain to be sent to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Fan, former overall commander Liu Daxia, former Left Administration Commissioner Shen Rui of Renhe, and eight hundred ninety-nine others were arrested and questioned, and fined grain to be delivered to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 銳廉介，已遷南京刑部右侍郎，乞休歸，至是奪職。

translations.literal: Rui was upright and incorruptible; he had already been promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing and had asked to retire home, but now lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Rui was upright and incorruptible; he had already been promoted to Right Vice Minister of Justice in Nanjing and had asked to retire home, but now lost his post.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，蕃以原官致仕。

translations.literal: After Jin was executed, Fan retired with his original rank restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Fan retired with his original rank restored.

sentences.zh: 逾六年，卒。

translations.literal: More than six years later, he died.
translations.idiomatic: More than six years later he died.

sentences.zh: 銳至嘉靖初，始復職致仕。

translations.literal: Rui was not restored to office and allowed to retire until the early Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Rui was not restored to office and allowed to retire until the early Jiajing reign.

sentences.zh: 方蕃解官歸，無屋，稅他人宅居之。

translations.literal: When Fan left office and returned home, he had no house and rented another's dwelling to live in.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan left office and returned home, he had no house of his own and rented another's dwelling to live in.

sentences.zh: 與鄉人飲，露坐花下，醉則任所之。

translations.literal: Drinking with fellow townsmen, he would sit in the open beneath the flowers; when drunk he would go wherever he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Drinking with fellow townsmen, he would sit in the open beneath the flowers, and when drunk would go wherever he pleased.

sentences.zh: 其風致如此。

translations.literal: Such was his bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Such was his bearing.

sentences.zh: 胡富，字永年，績溪人。

translations.literal: Hu Fu, style Yongnian, a native of Jixi.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fu, courtesy name Yongnian, was a native of Jixi.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 14 jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations as a jinshi in the fourteenth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授南京大理評事。

translations.literal: Appointed reviewing clerk at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a reviewing clerk at the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，歷福建僉事。

translations.literal: Early in Hongzhi he served as Fujian Assistant Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Hongzhi reign he served as Fujian Assistant Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 福寧系囚二百余人，富一訊皆定，囹圄頓空。

translations.literal: At Funing more than two hundred prisoners awaited trial; Fu investigated once and settled all cases, and the prisons were suddenly empty.
translations.idiomatic: At Funing more than two hundred prisoners awaited trial; Fu examined them once and settled every case, and the prisons were suddenly empty.

sentences.zh: 以憂去，起補山東，遷廣東副使。

translations.literal: He left on mourning leave, then was recalled to Shandong and transferred to Guangdong Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to observe mourning, then was recalled to Shandong and transferred to Guangdong Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四會瑤亂，剿擒五百余人。

translations.literal: When the Yao of Sihui rebelled, he campaigned and captured more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao of Sihui rebelled, he campaigned against them and captured more than five hundred.

sentences.zh: 瀧水瑤出沒無時，富度其所經地，得荒田三千余頃，招僮戶耕牧其中。

translations.literal: The Yao of Longshui raided without fixed times; Fu surveyed the routes they took and found more than three thousand qing of wasteland, recruiting Zhuang households to farm and herd within it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao of Longshui raided at unpredictable times; Fu surveyed the routes they used and found more than three thousand qing of wasteland, then recruited Zhuang households to farm and herd there.

sentences.zh: 瑤畏僮不敢出擾，居民得田作。

translations.literal: The Yao feared the Zhuang and dared not come out to raid; residents could work the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The Yao feared the Zhuang and dared not come out to raid, and local residents were able to work the fields.

sentences.zh: 符南蛇圍儋州，富與參議劉信往覘。

translations.literal: Fu Nan She besieged Danzhou; Fu and Participant Liu Xin went to reconnoiter.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Nan She besieged Danzhou; Hu Fu and Participant Liu Xin went to reconnoiter.

sentences.zh: 賊突至，殺信，富手斬劇賊一人，賊乃退。

translations.literal: Bandits charged in suddenly and killed Xin; Fu personally beheaded one fierce bandit, and the bandits then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits charged in suddenly and killed Liu Xin; Fu personally beheaded one fierce bandit, and the bandits then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 還益兵討平之。

translations.literal: He returned, reinforced his troops, and campaigned until they were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He returned, reinforced his troops, and campaigned until the rebels were pacified.

sentences.zh: 歷陜西左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Administration Commissioner in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Administration Commissioner in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 正德初，入為順天府尹。

translations.literal: Early in Zhengde he entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengde reign he entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 三年進南京大理寺卿，就遷戶部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Year 3 he was promoted to Chief Minister of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and immediately transferred to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was promoted to Chief Minister of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review and immediately transferred to Right Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 五年正月坐大理時勘事遲緩，勒致仕。

translations.literal: In the first month of year 5 he was forced to retire for slow handling of cases when at the Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year he was forced to retire for slow handling of cases during his tenure at the Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 亦瑾意也。

translations.literal: This too was at Jin's instigation.
translations.idiomatic: This too was at Liu Jin's instigation.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，起故官。

translations.literal: After Jin's fall he was restored to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored to his former post.

sentences.zh: 七年拜本部尚書。

translations.literal: Year 7 he was appointed Minister of this ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 南都倉儲僅支一年，富在部三載，有六年積。

translations.literal: Nanjing's grain stores could barely supply one year; after three years under Fu there was a six-year reserve.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing's grain stores could barely supply one year when he took office; after three years under Fu there was a six-year reserve.

sentences.zh: 上十余事，率權貴所不便，格不行，遂引年歸。

translations.literal: He submitted more than ten proposals, most inconvenient to powerful families; they were all blocked, so he cited his years and retired.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten proposals, most of them inconvenient to powerful families; when they were all blocked he cited his years and retired.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年卒。

translations.literal: He died in Jiajing 1.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚康惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and the title Kanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and given the posthumous title Kanghui.

sentences.zh: 張泰，字叔亨，廣東順德人。

translations.literal: Zhang Tai, style Shuheng, a native of Shunde in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tai, courtesy name Shuheng, was a native of Shunde in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 成化二年進士。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 2 jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examinations as a jinshi in the second year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 除知沙縣。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 時經鄧茂七之亂，泰撫綏招集，流亡盡復。

translations.literal: The district had just passed through Deng Maoqi's rebellion; Tai soothed, rallied, and gathered people, and all exiles returned.
translations.idiomatic: The district had just passed through Deng Maoqi's rebellion; Tai soothed and rallied the people, and all exiles returned.

sentences.zh: 入為御史，偕同官諫萬貴妃幹政，廷杖幾斃。

translations.literal: He entered service as a censor; together with colleagues he remonstrated against Consort Wan's interference in government and was nearly beaten to death in court.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a censor; together with colleagues he remonstrated against Consort Wan's interference in government and was nearly beaten to death in the outer court.

sentences.zh: 出督京畿學校，以憂去，家居十余年。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise metropolitan-area schools, left on mourning, and remained at home more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to supervise schools in the metropolitan region, left on mourning, and remained at home for more than ten years.

sentences.zh: 弘治五年起故官，按雲南。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 5 he was recalled to his former post and sent to inspect Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Hongzhi he was recalled to his former post and sent to inspect Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 孟密土舍思揲構亂，以兵遏木邦宣慰使罕挖法於孟乃寨。

translations.literal: Mengmi native chieftain Si Die fomented rebellion and used troops to block Mang Myit pacification commissioner Han Wafa at Mengnai stockade.
translations.idiomatic: Mengmi native official Si Die fomented rebellion and used troops to block Mang Myit pacification commissioner Han Wafa at Mengnai stockade.

sentences.zh: 守臣撫諭，拒不聽。

translations.literal: Border officials exhorted him peacefully; he refused to heed.
