translations.idiomatic: Border officials tried to pacify him by exhortation, but he refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 泰與巡撫張誥集兵示必討，思揲懼，始罷兵。

translations.literal: Tai and Grand Coordinator Zhang Hao massed troops showing they would certainly campaign; Si Die feared this and only then ceased hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Tai and Grand Coordinator Zhang Hao massed troops to show they would certainly campaign; Si Die grew afraid and only then ceased hostilities.

sentences.zh: 滇池溢，為民災，泰築堤以弭其患。

translations.literal: Lake Dian overflowed and brought disaster on the people; Tai built dikes to quell the harm.
translations.idiomatic: Lake Dian overflowed and brought disaster on the people; Tai built dikes to check the damage.

sentences.zh: 還朝，乞罷織造內臣，減皇莊及貴戚莊田被災稅賦，給畿省災民牛種。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he requested abolition of palace silk-weaving eunuchs, reduction of tax levies on imperial estates and noble estates stricken by disaster, and provision of cattle and seed to disaster victims in the metropolitan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to court he asked that palace silk-weaving eunuchs be abolished, that tax levies on imperial estates and noble estates stricken by disaster be reduced, and that cattle and seed be given to disaster victims in the metropolitan provinces.

sentences.zh: 詔止給牛種，余不行。

translations.literal: An edict granted only cattle and seed; the rest was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted only cattle and seed; the rest was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 寇入永昌，甘肅遊擊魯麟委罪副總兵陶禎，而總兵官劉寧疏言守臣不和，詔泰往勘。

translations.literal: Bandits entered Yongchang; Gansu roving-attendant Lu Lin shifted blame to Vice Regional Commander Tao Zhen, while Regional Commander Liu Ning memorialized that the defending officials were at odds; an edict ordered Tai to go investigate.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits raided Yongchang, Gansu roving-attendant Lu Lin laid the blame on Vice Regional Commander Tao Zhen, while Regional Commander Liu Ning memorialized that the defending officials were at odds; the court ordered Tai to go and investigate.

sentences.zh: 泰奏鎮守太監傅德、故總兵官周玉侵據屯田。

translations.literal: Tai memorialized that garrison eunuch Fu De and the former regional commander Zhou Yu had seized military colony lands.
translations.idiomatic: Tai reported that Garrison Eunuch Fu De and former Regional Commander Zhou Yu had encroached on military colony lands.

sentences.zh: 巡撫馮續減削軍餉，寇數入莫肯為禦，失士卒六百余、馬駝牛羊二萬皆不以聞。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Feng Xu cut military pay; bandits repeatedly entered and no one would defend, and losses of more than six hundred soldiers and twenty thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep were all not reported.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Feng Xu had cut military pay; when bandits repeatedly raided, no one would stand and fight, and losses of more than six hundred troops and twenty thousand horses, camels, cattle, and sheep were never reported.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，下之吏。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and handed them over to the judicial officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was enraged and had them turned over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 德降內使，錮南京，續編氓口外。

translations.literal: De was demoted to inner attendant, imprisoned in Nanjing; Xu was registered as a commoner beyond the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: De was demoted to inner attendant and confined in Nanjing; Xu was registered as a commoner and exiled beyond the frontier.

sentences.zh: 泰又言甘州膏腴地悉為中官、武臣所據，仍責軍稅；

translations.literal: Tai also said that Ganzhou's fertile lands were all occupied by inner eunuchs and military officials, who still levied military taxes;
translations.idiomatic: Tai also reported that Ganzhou's fertile lands had all been seized by palace eunuchs and military officials, who still exacted military taxes from them;

sentences.zh: 城北草湖資戍卒牧馬，今亦被占。

translations.literal: the Grass Lake north of the city, which supplied pasturage for garrison troops' horses, was now also occupied.
translations.idiomatic: the Grass Lake north of the city, which provided pasture for the garrison's horses, had now been taken as well.

sentences.zh: 請悉歸之軍，且推行於延、寧二鎮，詔皆從之。

translations.literal: He requested that all be returned to the army and that the policy be extended to the Yan and Ning garrisons; edicts approved all of it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that everything be restored to the army and that the same policy be applied in the Yan and Ning garrisons; the court approved it all.

sentences.zh: 遷太僕少卿，改大理。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then moved to the Dali Tribunal.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then transferred to the Dali Tribunal.

sentences.zh: 初，薊州民田多為牧馬草場所侵，又侵禦馬監及神機營草場、皇莊，貧民失業，草場亦虧故額。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jizhou commoners' fields had largely been encroached on by horse-pasture grounds, which also encroached on Imperial Horse Directorate and Divine Engine Corps pastures and imperial estates; poor people lost their livelihoods, and the pastures also fell short of their original quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, much of the farmland in Jizhou had been swallowed up by horse pastures, which also encroached on pastures of the Imperial Horse Directorate and the Divine Engine Corps as well as on imperial estates; the poor lost their livelihoods, and the pastures themselves fell below their original quotas.

sentences.zh: 孝宗屢遣給事中周旋，侍郎顧佐、熊翀等往勘，皆不能決。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozong repeatedly sent Supervising Secretary Zhou Huan, Vice Ministers Gu Zuo, Xiong Chong, and others to investigate, but none could settle the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozong repeatedly sent Supervising Secretary Zhou Huan and Vice Ministers Gu Zuo, Xiong Chong, and others to investigate, yet none could resolve the dispute.

sentences.zh: 至是命泰偕錦衣官會巡撫周季麟復勘。

translations.literal: At this time he ordered Tai, together with Brocade Guard officials, to join Grand Coordinator Zhou Jilin in reinvestigating.
translations.idiomatic: Now he ordered Tai, together with Brocade Guard officers, to join Grand Coordinator Zhou Jilin in a fresh investigation.

sentences.zh: 泰密求得永樂間舊籍，參互稽考，田當歸民者九百三十余頃，而京營及禦馬監牧地鹹不失故額。

translations.literal: Tai secretly obtained old registers from the Yongle reign and cross-checked them; fields that should return to the people totaled more than nine hundred thirty-odd qing, while capital garrison and Imperial Horse Directorate pasture lands all retained their original quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Tai secretly obtained old registers from the Yongle reign and cross-checked them; he found more than nine hundred thirty qing of land that should be returned to the people, while the capital garrison and Imperial Horse Directorate pastures would all keep their original quotas intact.

sentences.zh: 奏入，駁議者再，尚書韓文力持之，留中未下。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, objectors debated it twice; Minister Han Wen held firm, and it was kept at court without being issued.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, opponents debated it twice; Minister Han Wen stood firm, and the memorial was held at court without being promulgated.

sentences.zh: 及武宗嗣位，文再請，始出泰奏，流亡者鹹得復業。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong succeeded, Wen again requested, and only then was Tai's memorial issued; those in exile all regained their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Wen petitioned again, and only then was Tai's memorial issued; those who had been driven off all returned to their fields.

sentences.zh: 尋遷右副都御史督儲南京。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to supervise grain stores at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of grain stores at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 奏厘革十二事，多報可。

translations.literal: He memorialized twelve items for reform and rectification; most received approval.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized twelve reforms; most were approved.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，召為工部右侍郎，逾年遷南京右都御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde he was summoned as Right Vice Minister of Works; after a year he was transferred to Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Works; a year later he was made Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 泰清謹。

translations.literal: Tai was pure and cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Tai was upright and scrupulous.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾專權，朝貴爭賂遺。

translations.literal: Liu Jin monopolized power, and court nobles vied in presenting bribes and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin monopolized power, court grandees competed in offering him bribes and gifts.

sentences.zh: 泰奏表至京，惟饋土葛。

translations.literal: When Tai's memorial of felicitation reached the capital, he presented only local hemp cloth.
translations.idiomatic: When Tai's congratulatory memorial reached the capital, he sent only local hemp cloth as a gift.

sentences.zh: 瑾憾之，其年十月令以南京戶部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Jin resented this; in the tenth month of that year he ordered him to retire as Nanjing Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Jin resented this; in the tenth month of that year he had him retired as Nanjing Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年七月卒，摭他事罰米數百石。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the following year he died; on other pretexts he was fined several hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh month of the following year; on other pretexts a fine of several hundred piculs of grain was imposed on his estate.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，予葬祭如制。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, burial and sacrifices were granted according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, burial and sacrifices were granted according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 吳文度，字憲之，晉江人，從父客江寧，遂家焉。

translations.literal: Wu Wendu, style Xianzhi, a native of Jinjiang; he followed his father as a guest in Jiangning and there made his home.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wendu, courtesy name Xianzhi, was a native of Jinjiang; he accompanied his father to Jiangning as a guest and settled his family there.

sentences.zh: 登成化八年進士，除龍泉知縣，征授南京御史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed magistrate of Longquan, and was summoned to serve as Nanjing censor.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua, was appointed magistrate of Longquan, and was then summoned to serve as a Nanjing censor.

sentences.zh: 偕同官孫需等論妖僧繼曉，被廷杖。

translations.literal: Together with fellow censors Sun Xu and others he denounced the heterodox monk Jixiao and was beaten at court.
translations.idiomatic: Together with fellow censors Sun Xu and others he denounced the heterodox monk Jixiao and was beaten in a court flogging.

sentences.zh: 尋遷汀州知府。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to prefect of Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made prefect of Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑤弗靖，設方略綏撫，瑤承賦如居民。

translations.literal: The Yao were unsettled; he devised measures to pacify them, and the Yao bore tax levies like ordinary residents.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yao were restless, he devised policies to pacify them, and the Yao paid taxes like ordinary subjects.

sentences.zh: 弘治中歷江西左參政，山西、河南左、右布政使。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he successively served as Left Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi and Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During Hongzhi he served in turn as Left Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi and as Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 正德元年遷右副都御史，巡撫雲南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengde he was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengde he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 師宗州賊阿本等作亂，諭不從，乃遣參議陳一經等督軍二萬攻之，別遣兵截盤江，據賊巢背，先後俘斬千人。

translations.literal: Bandits Aben and others of Shizong Prefecture rose in rebellion; exhortation failed, so he sent Administration Commissioner Chen Yijing and others to lead twenty thousand troops against them, and separately sent troops to block the Pan River and seize the rear of the bandit lair; in all more than a thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits Aben and others of Shizong Prefecture rebelled, persuasion failed; he then sent Administration Commissioner Chen Yijing and others to lead twenty thousand troops against them, while another force blocked the Pan River and took the bandits' lair from the rear; more than a thousand were captured or killed in all.

sentences.zh: 入歷戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital and served as Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital and served as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三年冬進南京右都御史。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year he was advanced to Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year he was promoted to Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 方文度召自雲南，劉瑾以地產金寶，屢責賄。

translations.literal: Just as Wendu was summoned from Yunnan, Liu Jin, because the region produced gold and jewels, repeatedly demanded bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Wendu was recalled from Yunnan, Liu Jin—knowing the region produced gold and jewels—repeatedly demanded bribes from him.

sentences.zh: 文度無以應，瑾深銜之。

translations.literal: Wendu had nothing with which to comply; Jin deeply bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu had nothing to give; Jin bore a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 會工部尚書李鐩致仕，廷推文度及南京戶部侍郎王珩，遂改文度南京戶部尚書，與珩俱致仕。

translations.literal: When Minister of Works Li Yong retired, the court nominated Wendu and Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Heng; Wendu was then changed to Nanjing Minister of Revenue, and both he and Heng were retired.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of Works Li Yong retired, the court nominated Wendu and Nanjing Vice Minister of Revenue Wang Heng; Wendu was then made Nanjing Minister of Revenue, and both he and Heng were forced to retire.

sentences.zh: 命下，舉朝駭異。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, the whole court was shocked and astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When the order was issued, the whole court was astonished.

sentences.zh: 既歸，所居屋僅數椽。

translations.literal: After returning home, the house he lived in had only a few rafters.
translations.idiomatic: After he returned home, his dwelling had only a few beams.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，未及用而卒。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, before he could be employed again he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he died before he could be reappointed.

sentences.zh: 珩，趙人。

translations.literal: Heng was a man of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was a native of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 起家進士，亦以清操聞。

translations.literal: Rising from jinshi, he was also known for pure conduct.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi by origin, he was also known for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 張鼐，字用和，歷城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Nai, style Yonghe, a native of Licheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Nai, courtesy name Yonghe, was a native of Licheng.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 授襄陵知縣，入為御史。

translations.literal: Appointed magistrate of Xiangling, he entered [the capital] as censor.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed magistrate of Xiangling, he was later recalled to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 憲宗末年數笞言官，鼐力諫。

translations.literal: In the late years of Emperor Xianzong remonstrance officials were repeatedly flogged; Nai remonstrated forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Xianzong, remonstrance officials were repeatedly flogged; Nai remonstrated forcefully against this.

sentences.zh: 又嘗劾妖僧繼曉、方士鄧常恩等。

translations.literal: He also once impeached the heterodox monk Jixiao, Daoist adept Deng Chang'en, and others.
translations.idiomatic: He also once impeached the heterodox monk Jixiao, the Daoist adept Deng Chang'en, and others.

sentences.zh: 帝心惡之。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart turned against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took a dislike to him.

sentences.zh: 出按江西。

translations.literal: He went out to inspect Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out to inspect Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 盜賊多強宗佃仆，鼐與巡撫閔珪交奏其事。

translations.literal: Bandits were mostly tenant servants of powerful clans; Nai and Grand Coordinator Min Gui submitted alternating memorials on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Most bandits were tenant servants of powerful clans; Nai and Grand Coordinator Min Gui submitted joint memorials on the matter.

sentences.zh: 尹直等構之，乃貶珪而坐鼐尹旻黨，謫郴州判官。

translations.literal: Yin Zhi and others framed them; Gui was demoted while Nai was seated in the Yin Min faction and banished to judge of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Zhi and others framed them; Gui was demoted while Nai was treated as part of the Yin Min faction and banished to the post of judge in Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，擢河南僉事，進參議，以協治黃陵岡遷副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Hongzhi he was promoted to Henan Surveillance Commissioner, advanced to Administration Commissioner, and for assisting in managing Huangling Gorge was transferred to Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Hongzhi he was promoted to Henan Surveillance Commissioner and then to Administration Commissioner; for helping manage the Huangling Gorge works he was made Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十五年進按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was advanced to Surveillance Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was promoted to Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鼐官河南久，屢遭河患，督治有方，民為立祠。

translations.literal: Nai served long in Henan, repeatedly suffered river disasters, supervised repairs with effective methods, and the people erected a shrine for him.
translations.idiomatic: Nai served in Henan for many years, faced repeated floods, and supervised repairs with such skill that the people erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，擢右僉都御史巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: That autumn he was promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 時軍政久馳，又許余丁納貲助驛遞，給冠帶，復其身。

translations.literal: At the time military administration had long been lax; moreover surplus sons were allowed to pay a fee to support courier service, were given caps and belts, and regained personal status.
translations.idiomatic: Military administration had long been lax; moreover surplus sons were allowed to pay a fee to support the courier service, receive caps and belts, and regain personal status.

sentences.zh: 邊人競援例避役。

translations.literal: Frontier people all cited the precedent to avoid corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier people rushed to cite the precedent to avoid corvée service.

sentences.zh: 鼐言不可，因條上定馬制、核屯糧、清隱占、稽客戶、減軍伴數事，悉允行。

translations.literal: Nai said this could not be allowed, and accordingly listed items on fixing horse regulations, auditing colony grain, clearing concealed encroachments, checking tenant households, and reducing military attendants; all were approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Nai said this could not stand, and memorialized measures to fix horse regulations, audit colony grain, clear concealed encroachments, check tenant households, and reduce military attendants; all were approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 尋劾分守中官劉恭貪虐罪，築邊墻自山海關迄開原叆陽堡凡千餘里。

translations.literal: Soon he impeached the garrison eunuch Liu Gong for greedy cruelty, and built border walls from Shanhaiguan to Kaiyuan's Aiyang Fort for more than a thousand li in all.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Garrison Eunuch Liu Gong for greed and cruelty, and built border walls from Shanhaiguan to Aiyang Fort at Kaiyuan—a stretch of more than a thousand li in all.

sentences.zh: 遼撫自徐貫後，歷張岫、張玉、陳瑤、韓重四人，多得罪去，至鼐稱能。

translations.literal: Liaodong grand coordinators after Xu Guan included Zhang Xiu, Zhang Yu, Chen Yao, and Han Chong—four men, most of whom offended and left office; only with Nai was ability acknowledged.
translations.idiomatic: After Xu Guan, Liaodong had four grand coordinators in succession—Zhang Xiu, Zhang Yu, Chen Yao, and Han Chong—most of whom left office in disgrace; only under Nai was ability acknowledged.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，移撫宣府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, he was transferred to grand coordinator of Xuanfu.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Nai was transferred to Grand Coordinator of Xuanfu.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，召還，尋進右副都御史署院事。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title in Zhengde he was recalled; soon he was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief to act as head of the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: At the change of reign title in Zhengde he was recalled; soon he was made Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and put in charge of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 有知縣犯贓當褫職，卒殺人當抵死。

translations.literal: A magistrate had committed corruption and should be dismissed from office; a soldier had killed a man and should pay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: A magistrate had taken bribes and should be dismissed; a soldier had killed a man and should pay with his life.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾納重賄，欲寬之，鼐執不可，出為南京右都御史。

translations.literal: Liu Jin accepted heavy bribes and wished to leniently treat them; Nai held firm that this could not be done and was sent out as Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin had taken heavy bribes and wanted leniency; Nai refused, and was sent out as Nanjing Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 焦芳子黃中欲強市其居，畀通政魏訥，鼐不從，芳父子亦怨之。

translations.literal: Jiao Fang's son Huang Zhong wished to force the sale of his residence and hand it to Communications Commissioner Wei Na; Nai would not comply, and the Jiao father and son also resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao Fang's son Huang Zhong tried to force the sale of his residence and hand it to Communications Commissioner Wei Na; Nai refused, and the Jiao father and son resented him as well.

sentences.zh: 會瑾遣給事中王翊等核遼東軍餉，還奏芻粟多浥爛，遂以為守臣罪，逮鼐及繼任巡撫馬中錫、鄧章，前參政冒政，參議方矩，郎中王藎、劉繹下詔獄，令其家人輸米遼東。

translations.literal: When Jin sent Supervising Secretary Wang Yi and others to audit Liaodong military provisions, on returning they memorialized that fodder grain was largely rotted from damp; thereupon the defending officials were held guilty, and Nai, his successor Grand Coordinator Ma Zhongxi, Deng Zhang, former Administration Commissioner Mao Zheng, Administration Commissioner Fang Ju, Bureau Director Wang Jin, and Liu Yi were seized and sent to the imperial prison, with orders that their families deliver grain to Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin sent Supervising Secretary Wang Yi and others to audit Liaodong military provisions, they reported on their return that much of the fodder grain had rotted from damp; the defending officials were then held guilty, and Nai, his successor Grand Coordinator Ma Zhongxi, Deng Zhang, former Administration Commissioner Mao Zheng, Administration Commissioner Fang Ju, Bureau Director Wang Jin, and Liu Yi were arrested and sent to the imperial prison, with orders that their families deliver grain to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 鼐坐輸二千石，以力不辦，系遼東。

translations.literal: Nai was sentenced to deliver two thousand piculs; being unable to manage it, he was detained in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Nai was sentenced to deliver two thousand piculs of grain; unable to pay, he was detained in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 久之，總兵官毛倫等具奏諸人苦狀，請得折價，瑾勉從之。

translations.literal: After a long time Regional Commander Mao Lun and others fully memorialized the people's bitter condition and requested that payment be allowed in cash equivalent; Jin reluctantly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time Regional Commander Mao Lun and others memorialized in full on the men's plight and asked that they be allowed to pay in cash; Jin reluctantly agreed.

sentences.zh: 閱三年事始竟，皆斥為民。

translations.literal: After three years the affair was finally concluded; all were dismissed as commoners.
translations.idiomatic: After three years the case was finally closed; all were reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復官。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, their offices were restored.

sentences.zh: 鼐前卒，世宗初予恤。

translations.literal: Nai had died earlier; at the beginning of Emperor Shizong posthumous favor was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Nai had already died; at the beginning of Emperor Shizong's reign posthumous honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 冒政，泰州人。

translations.literal: Mao Zheng was a man of Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Zheng was a native of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 鼐同年進士，歷官右副都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the same year as Nai, he successively served as Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the same year as Nai, he rose to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and served as Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 守官廉，劉瑾覬賄不得，遂假遼東事逮之，罰米至三千石。

translations.literal: He held office with integrity; Liu Jin coveted bribes but could not obtain them, so on the pretext of the Liaodong affair he was seized and fined grain up to three thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He served with integrity; Liu Jin coveted bribes but could not get them, so on the pretext of the Liaodong affair he was arrested and fined up to three thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，復職致仕。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, his office was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒。

translations.literal: After a long time he died.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he died.

sentences.zh: 王璟，字廷采，沂人。

translations.literal: Wang Jing, style Tingcai, a native of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jing, courtesy name Tingcai, was a native of Yi.

sentences.zh: 成化八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi in the eighth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua.

sentences.zh: 為登封知縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Dengfeng.

sentences.zh: 歷兩京御史。

translations.literal: He successively served as censor in both capitals.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as a censor in both capitals.

sentences.zh: 弘治十四年，以南京鴻臚卿拜右僉都御史，理兩浙鹽政。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi, from Nanjing Director of Ceremonials he was appointed Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief to administer the salt administration of the two Zhe provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Hongzhi he was made Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief from his post as Nanjing Director of Ceremonials and put in charge of the salt administration of the two Zhe provinces.

sentences.zh: 振荒浙江，奏行荒政十事，多所全活。

translations.literal: Relieving famine in Zhejiang, he memorialized ten famine policies for implementation; many lives were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: While relieving famine in Zhejiang, he memorialized ten famine-relief measures; many lives were saved.

sentences.zh: 十七年冬巡撫保定。

translations.literal: In the winter of the seventeenth year he became Grand Coordinator of Baoding.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the seventeenth year he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Baoding.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，太監夏綬乞於真定諸府歲加葦場稅，少監傅琢請履畝核靜海、永清、隆平諸縣田，太監張峻欲稅寧晉小河往來客貨，詔皆許之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, eunuch Xia Shou requested an annual reed-marsh tax in Zhending and other prefectures; Junior Supervisor Fu Zhuo requested surveying mu to verify fields in Jinghai, Yongqing, Longping, and other counties; eunuch Zhang Jun wished to tax goods carried by travelers on the small river at Ningjin; edicts approved all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Eunuch Xia Shou asked for an annual reed-marsh tax in Zhending and other prefectures; Junior Supervisor Fu Zhuo asked to survey fields mu by mu in Jinghai, Yongqing, Longping, and other counties; Eunuch Zhang Jun wanted to tax goods carried by travelers on the small river at Ningjin; the court approved them all.

sentences.zh: 又以莊田故，遣緹騎逮民魯堂等二百余人，畿南騷動。

translations.literal: Also on account of estate lands, brocade-clad guards were sent to seize commoners Lu Tang and more than two hundred others; south of the capital region was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: On account of estate lands as well, brocade-clad guards were sent to arrest commoners Lu Tang and more than two hundred others, throwing the region south of the capital into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 璟抗疏切諫。

translations.literal: Jing submitted a forceful memorial in sharp remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing submitted a forceful memorial of remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 尚書韓文等力持之，管莊內臣稍得召還。

translations.literal: Minister Han Wen and others held firm, and the inner eunuchs managing estates were somewhat able to be recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Han Wen and others stood firm, and the eunuchs managing the estates were partly recalled.

sentences.zh: 正德元年四月引疾致仕，命馳傳歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhengde he cited illness and retired; he was ordered to return home by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Zhengde he cited illness and retired; he was ordered home by express relay.

sentences.zh: 三年坐累奪官閑住。

translations.literal: In the third year, implicated in a case, he was stripped of office and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was implicated in a case, stripped of office, and lived in retirement.

sentences.zh: 六年起撫山西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was raised to grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was reappointed Grand Coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 制火槍萬余，槍藏箭六，皆傅毒藥，用以禦寇，寇不敢西。

translations.literal: He made more than ten thousand fire lances; each lance held six arrows, all coated with poison, used to repel bandits, and the bandits did not dare go west.
translations.idiomatic: He had more than ten thousand fire lances made; each lance held six arrows, all coated with poison, and with these he repelled bandits so that they did not dare advance westward.

sentences.zh: 累遷右都御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly transferred to Right Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to Right Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 已，遷左，以張綸為右都御史代之。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to the Left, and Zhang Lun was made Right Censor-in-Chief to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Left Censor-in-Chief, and Zhang Lun was appointed Right Censor-in-Chief in his place.

sentences.zh: 後陳金以太子太保左都御史入院，位璟上，人號璟「中都御史」焉。

translations.literal: Later Chen Jin entered the Censorate as Left Censor-in-Chief with the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, ranking above Jing; people nicknamed Jing the "Central Capital Censor."
translations.idiomatic: Later Chen Jin entered the Censorate as Left Censor-in-Chief with the title Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, ranking above Jing; people nicknamed Jing the "Central Capital Censor."

sentences.zh: 時群小用事，大臣靡然附之，璟獨守故操。

translations.literal: At the time petty men held power; great ministers all inclined to attach themselves, but Jing alone kept his former conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men held power at court; great ministers all fawned on them, but Jing alone held to his old principles.

sentences.zh: 再進太子太保。

translations.literal: He was again advanced to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was again promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，致仕，卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he retired and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong took the throne, he retired and died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚恭靖。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given Junior Guardian and the posthumous title Gongjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Gongjing.

sentences.zh: 初，璟自保定巡撫歸，其後兵科給事中高淓勘滄州鹽山牧地，劾六十一人，及璟與前巡撫都御史高銓。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Jing returned from his grand coordinator post at Baoding, later Supervising Secretary of the Military Bureau Gao Shu investigated pasture lands at Cangzhou and Yanshan, impeaching sixty-one people, including Jing and the former grand coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Gao Quan.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after Jing returned from his post as Grand Coordinator of Baoding, Supervising Secretary of the Military Bureau Gao Shu later investigated pasture lands at Cangzhou and Yanshan and impeached sixty-one people, including Jing and former Grand Coordinator and Censor-in-Chief Gao Quan.

sentences.zh: 銓即淓父也。

translations.literal: Quan was Shu's father.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was Shu's father.

sentences.zh: 詔去職者勿問，璟、銓並獲免。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that those who had left office not be prosecuted; Jing and Nai were both pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared that dismissed officials would not be prosecuted; both Jing and Nai were spared.

sentences.zh: 銓，江都人，累官南京戶部尚書。

translations.literal: Nai was a native of Jiangdu and rose through offices to minister of Revenue at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Nai came from Jiangdu and eventually served as minister of Revenue at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 正德二年廷推左都御史，瑾勒令致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde the court recommended him for left censor-in-chief; Jin forced him to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhengde the court nominated him for left censor-in-chief, but Liu Jin compelled him to retire.

sentences.zh: 尋坐事逮下獄，復坐隆平侯家襲爵事除名，罰米五百石。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was arrested and imprisoned on a charge; again, on the matter of the Marquis of Longping's household inheriting a title, he was struck from the rolls and fined five hundred piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon arrested and imprisoned on a charge, then struck from the rolls over the Marquis of Longping's inheritance dispute and fined five hundred piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 後瑾益事操切，每遣使勘核，多務苛急承瑾意，淓遂並銓在劾中。

translations.literal: Later Jin grew still more harsh in control; each time he sent envoys to investigate, most strove for severity to please Jin, and Fang and Nai were both among those impeached.
translations.idiomatic: As Jin grew harsher, his investigators usually sought severity to please him, and both Fang and Nai were caught up in the prosecutions.

sentences.zh: 淓後官至光祿少卿，以劾父不齒於人。

translations.literal: Fang later reached vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but because he impeached his father he was scorned by others.
translations.idiomatic: Fang later rose to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, but men despised him for having impeached his own father.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，銓復官致仕，卒。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, Nai was restored to office and retired, then died.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, Nai was restored to office, retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 朱欽，字懋恭，邵武人。

translations.literal: Zhu Qin, style name Maogong, was a native of Shaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qin, whose style was Maogong, came from Shaowu.

sentences.zh: 師吳與弼，以學行稱。

translations.literal: He studied under Wu Yubi and was famed for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Wu Yubi and was renowned for scholarship and integrity.

sentences.zh: 舉成化八年進士，授寧波推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua and was appointed judicial assistant of Ningbo.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of Chenghua and was appointed judicial assistant of Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 治最，征授御史。

translations.literal: His governance was rated highest and he was summoned and appointed censor.
translations.idiomatic: His administration was rated the best in the province, and he was summoned to serve as a censor.

sentences.zh: 出督漕運，按河南，清軍廣西，並著風節。

translations.literal: He went out to supervise grain transport, investigated Henan, and inspected troops in Guangxi, in each case showing moral force.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised grain transport, investigated Henan, and inspected troops in Guangxi, earning a reputation for moral courage in each post.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，遷山東副使，歷浙江按察使。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign he was transferred to vice commissioner of Shandong and served as surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he became vice commissioner of Shandong and later surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 十五年入覲。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he came to court for audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he came to the capital for an audience.

sentences.zh: 吏部舉天下治行卓異者六人，欽與焉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel nominated six men throughout the realm for outstanding governance, and Qin was among them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Personnel nominated six officials empire-wide for outstanding governance, and Qin was one of them.

sentences.zh: 僉都御史林俊又舉欽自代，乃稍遷湖廣左布政使。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun also recommended Qin to succeed himself, and he was gradually promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun also recommended Qin as his successor, and he was promoted to left provincial administration commissioner of Huguang.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，以右副都御史巡撫山東。

translations.literal: When Wuzong came to the throne, he was made right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Qin was appointed right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 中官王嶽被謫，道死。

translations.literal: The inner official Wang Yue was banished and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Wang Yue was banished and died en route.

sentences.zh: 欽上言：「嶽謫守祖陵，罪狀未暴，賜死道路，不厭人心。

translations.literal: Qin submitted a memorial saying, "Yue was banished to guard the imperial tombs; his crimes were not yet made public, yet he was granted death on the road—this does not satisfy men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Qin memorialized: "Yue was banished to guard the imperial tombs; his crimes were never made public, yet he was put to death on the road—this cannot satisfy public opinion.

sentences.zh: 臣知嶽為劉瑾輩所惡，必瑾譖毀以至此。

translations.literal: Your minister knows that Yue was hated by Liu Jin's faction and that Jin must have slandered and ruined him to bring this about.
translations.idiomatic: I know that Yue was hated by Liu Jin's faction and that Jin must have slandered him to bring about this end.

sentences.zh: 望陛下察嶽非辜，懲瑾讒賊。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will discern that Yue was innocent and punish Jin the slanderous villain."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to see that Yue was innocent and punish Jin the slanderer."

sentences.zh: 疏至，瑾屏不奏，銜之。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Jin suppressed it and did not transmit it, and bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Jin suppressed it and bore a deep grudge against Qin.

sentences.zh: 欽以山東俗淫酗，嚴禁市酤，令濟南推官張元魁察之，犯者罪及鄰。

translations.literal: Qin, because Shandong custom was licentious and drunken, strictly forbade market sale of wine, ordered Zhang Yuankui, judicial assistant of Jinan, to investigate, and made neighbors liable for offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Because Shandong was given to licentious drinking, Qin strictly banned the sale of wine in markets, ordered Zhang Yuankui of Jinan to enforce the ban, and made neighbors liable when offenders were found.

sentences.zh: 比有懼而自縊者，其母欲奏訴，元魁與知府趙璜賄之乃已。

translations.literal: Soon someone in fear hanged himself; his mother wished to memorialize in complaint, but Yuankui and prefect Zhao Huang bribed her and she desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a man hanged himself in fear; when his mother tried to lodge a complaint, Yuankui and Prefect Zhao Huang bribed her into silence.

sentences.zh: 瑾使偵事校尉發之，俱逮下詔獄，勒欽致仕，璜除名，元魁謫戍。

translations.literal: Jin sent investigating guards to expose the matter; all were arrested and sent to the imperial prison; Qin was forced to retire, Huang was struck from the rolls, and Yuankui was banished to military service.
translations.idiomatic: Jin sent investigating guards to expose the affair; all were imprisoned, Qin was forced to retire, Huang was struck from the rolls, and Yuankui was banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 瑾憾欽未已，摭前湖廣時小故，下巡按御史逮問。

translations.literal: Jin's resentment toward Qin was not ended; he gathered petty matters from Qin's earlier days in Huguang and ordered the touring censor to arrest and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's resentment was not satisfied; he dredged up petty matters from Qin's time in Huguang and ordered the touring censor to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 俄坐山東勘地事，斥為民。

translations.literal: Soon, on the matter of surveying land in Shandong, he was reduced to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reduced to commoner status over a land survey in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 又坐修曲阜先聖廟會計數多，罰輸米六百石塞下。

translations.literal: Again, on repairing the temple of the ancient sage at Qufu, the accounts showed excess and he was fined six hundred piculs of grain for the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was also fined six hundred piculs of frontier grain because the accounts for repairing Confucius's temple at Qufu showed a surplus.

sentences.zh: 又坐撫山東時，以民夫給事尚書秦纮家，再下巡按御史逮問。

translations.literal: Again, while pacifying Shandong he had used corvée laborers to serve at the home of Minister Qin Xian, and once more the touring censor was ordered to arrest and question him.
translations.idiomatic: He was again prosecuted for assigning corvée laborers to serve at Minister Qin Xian's household while grand coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 瑾誅，乃復官。

translations.literal: When Jin was executed, he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin was executed, he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 十五年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifteenth year, aged seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 與弼之門以宦學顯者，欽為稱首。

translations.literal: Among those of Yubi's school who achieved distinction through official learning, Qin was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among Wu Yubi's disciples who achieved distinction in public life, Qin was the foremost.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：武宗初，劉、謝受遺輔政，韓文、張敷華等為列卿長，當路多正人，國事有賴。

translations.literal: The commentator says: At the beginning of Wuzong's reign, Liu and Xie received the testament and assisted in government; Han Wen, Zhang Fuhua, and others were chief ministers; those in power were mostly upright men, and state affairs had support.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: At the start of Wuzong's reign, Liu Jian and Xie Qian received the deathbed charge and assisted the government; Han Wen, Zhang Fuhua, and others headed the ministries; upright men held power, and the state had reason to hope.

sentences.zh: 「八虎」潛伏左右，雖未敢顯與朝士為難，固腹心之蠹也。

translations.literal: The Eight Tigers lurked at the ruler's side; though they did not yet dare openly contend with court officials, they were vermin in the vitals.
translations.idiomatic: The "Eight Tigers" lurked at the emperor's side; though they did not yet dare openly challenge the court, they were parasites at the heart of the state.

sentences.zh: 夫以外攻內，勢所甚難。

translations.literal: To attack inward from without is by its nature very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking an inner foe from outside is inherently very difficult.

sentences.zh: 況相權之輕，遠異前代，雖抱韓琦之忠，初無書敕之柄。

translations.literal: Moreover, prime ministerial power was light, far unlike former ages; though one might embrace Han Qi's loyalty, at first one had no authority over written edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Grand Secretaries wielded far less power than in earlier dynasties; even with Han Qi's loyalty, they lacked control over imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 區區爭勝於筆舌間，此難必之剛明之主，而以望之武宗，庸有濟乎？

translations.literal: To struggle for victory only in brush and tongue—this difficulty surely required a firm and enlightened ruler; to expect it of Wuzong, how could there be success?
translations.idiomatic: To fight with memorials alone required a firm and enlightened ruler; to expect success from Wuzong was hopeless.

sentences.zh: 一擊不勝，反噬必毒，消長之機，間不容發。

translations.literal: One blow that does not succeed— the counter-bite is sure to be venomous; the moment when strength waxes or wanes allows no interval.
translations.idiomatic: A failed strike invites a deadly counterattack; the turning point allows no delay.

sentences.zh: 宦豎之貽禍烈也，籲可畏哉！

translations.literal: The calamity left by palace minions is fierce indeed—ah, how dreadful!
translations.idiomatic: The calamity wrought by palace eunuchs is terrible indeed—how frightening!
